It is the reach of punishment: when adjudicating cases to punish wrongdoing, whether relying on testimony and evidence or on supporting grounds adduced, there are always persons whom punishment reaches. One must also scrutinize grounds for acquittal or conviction and weigh what to accept or reject. The guilty must not be lightly pardoned, and one must not dare indiscriminately to implicate the innocent. Only then will matters be right. Otherwise, punishment will overstep its bounds and lack restraint. Is not its reach, then, what must be weighed?

If one devotes one's whole mind to selecting people, the populace will feel affection for their superiors; if one treats punishments with reverence, the populace will cherish life; if one weighs whom punishment reaches, the populace will be encouraged toward goodness. Truly, the people will enjoy peace, and punishment will bring blessings! Moreover, from this…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而知穆王訓刑之善焉何者用刑之不善者法
立未嘗不善也用心之不善耳故私心間而小
人進怠心生而天德微忮心行而民命蹙反是
而求盡心焉穆王之善訓也雖其制刑有非先
王之舊而欽恤之遺意猶若未泯嗚呼孔子所
以不得不錄其書也
詩
葛之覃兮施于中谷維葉萋萋黃鳥于飛
集于灌木其鳴喈喈
===
鄧直卿
同考試官訓導黃批能分葛葉黃鳥輕重而文體整齊
場中無如之者
同考試官教諭於批能玩朱傳黃鳥鳴于其上而為文是
可錄矣
同考試官學正李批后妃既成絺綌而追叙葛方盛時乃
以黃鳥附之必有說矣此作獨能知之
考試官教諭張批文不重疊而理亦明白錄之
考試官教諭應批講葛葉黃鳥得后妃本意可取
punctuated:
而知穆王訓刑之善焉。何者？用刑之不善者，法立未嘗不善也，用心之不善耳。故私心間而小人進，怠心生而天德微，忮心行而民命蹙。反是而求盡心焉，穆王之善訓也。雖其制刑有非先王之舊，而欽恤之遺意猶若未泯。嗚呼！孔子所以不得不錄其書也。

詩
葛之覃兮，施于中谷，維葉萋萋。黃鳥于飛，集于灌木，其鳴喈喈。

鄧直卿

同考試官訓導黃批：能分葛葉、黃鳥輕重，而文體整齊，場中無如之者。

同考試官教諭於批：能玩朱傳黃鳥鳴于其上而為文，是可錄矣。

同考試官學正李批：后妃既成絺綌，而追叙葛方盛時，乃以黃鳥附之，必有說矣。此作獨能知之。

考試官教諭張批：文不重疊，而理亦明白，錄之。

考試官教諭應批：講葛葉、黃鳥，得后妃本意，可取。
translation_en:
…and thus we recognize the excellence of King Mu’s instructions concerning punishments. Why is this? When punishments are applied badly, it is not that the laws, when established, were bad; the fault lies solely in the disposition of those applying them. Thus, when selfish motives intrude, petty men advance; when indolence arises, heavenly virtue wanes; when malice takes effect, the people’s lives are imperiled. To reverse these tendencies and seek to exert one’s heart to the utmost—this is the excellence of King Mu’s instruction. Although the punishments he established departed in some respects from the ancient practices of the former kings, the surviving spirit of reverence and compassion seems not yet to have been extinguished. Alas! This is why Confucius could not but include his text in the Book of Documents.

Book of Odes
“How the kudzu spreads,
Extending into the valley’s midst,
Its leaves luxuriant!
The yellow birds take flight,
Alight upon the shrubs,
And sing in harmony.”

Deng Zhiqing 鄧直卿

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor: “He distinguishes the relative importance of the kudzu leaves and the yellow birds, and his composition is well ordered. None in this examination matches it.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor: “He has reflected closely on Zhu Xi’s commentary concerning the yellow birds singing above it and composed his essay accordingly. This merits selection.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, School Instructor: “After the queen consort had finished making fine and coarse kudzu cloth, she recalled the time when the kudzu was flourishing and included the yellow birds in her account. There must be a reason for this. This essay alone grasps it.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “The composition avoids repetition, and its reasoning is clear. Select it.”

Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: “His discussion of the kudzu leaves and the yellow birds captures the queen consort’s original intent. It merits acceptance.”

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
賢妃追敘植物方盛而致動物之適情以見女
工之所自也夫葛葉方盛則女工將有所施而
黃鳥來鳴又因葛而知其所止者也既成女工
者得不追敘以為言哉昔后妃既成絺綌而賦
其事其追敘之意若曰葛雖成於盛夏而實始
於前時當夫初夏之際有葛生焉布濩覃延既
引夫不絕之蔓纏綿依附且移于中谷之間觀
其葉則萋萋然挹雨露之霑濡而發榮滋長之
性何其若也飽土膏之饒洽而憔悴隕籜之形
未之見焉是葛葉也刈濩之具絺綌之資不已
權輿於此乎適夫葛生之時有黃鳥焉熠燿其
羽載飛于陽和之天翔而後集斂翼于灌木之
上聽其鳴則喈喈然肆求友之聲而地之向遠
者無乎不達也調如簧之舌而人之有耳者皆
所共聞焉是黃鳥也安於所寓得其所止不因
葛葉而來乎夫以植物方盛則絺綌之功固有
以知其端動物來鳴則葛葉之生因有以驗其
盛后妃既成女工而追敘及此豈非不忘所自
punctuated:
賢妃追敘植物方盛，而致動物之適情，以見女工之所自也。夫葛葉方盛，則女工將有所施；而黃鳥來鳴，又因葛而知其所止者也。既成女工者，得不追敘以為言哉？
昔后妃既成絺綌而賦其事，其追敘之意若曰：葛雖成於盛夏，而實始於前時。當夫初夏之際，有葛生焉，布濩覃延，既引夫不絕之蔓；纏綿依附，且移于中谷之間。觀其葉，則萋萋然，挹雨露之霑濡，而發榮滋長之性，何其若也！飽土膏之饒洽，而憔悴隕籜之形，未之見焉。是葛葉也，刈濩之具，絺綌之資，不已權輿於此乎？適夫葛生之時，有黃鳥焉，熠燿其羽，載飛于陽和之天；翔而後集，斂翼于灌木之上。聽其鳴，則喈喈然，肆求友之聲，而地之向遠者，無乎不達也；調如簧之舌，而人之有耳者，皆所共聞焉。是黃鳥也，安於所寓，得其所止，不因葛葉而來乎？夫以植物方盛，則絺綌之功固有以知其端；動物來鳴，則葛葉之生因有以驗其盛。后妃既成女工而追敘及此，豈非不忘所自
translation_en:
The worthy consort recounts how the plants were flourishing and evokes the contentment of living creatures, thereby showing the origins of her textile work. When the kudzu leaves flourish, there will be material upon which women may exercise their skill; the yellow birds that come to sing likewise find their resting place through the kudzu. Having completed her textile work, how could she fail to recount these things in words?
In former times, the royal consort completed her fine and coarse kudzu cloth and composed a poem about her work. Her retrospective account seems to say: Although the kudzu reaches maturity in high summer, its beginnings lie earlier. At the onset of summer, kudzu grows, spreading and extending, sending out unbroken vines. Twining and clinging, it reaches into the valley. Look at its leaves: luxuriant, they drink in the moisture of rain and dew and display their propensity to flourish and grow—how abundant they are [?]! Nourished fully by the rich soil, they show no sign of withering or shedding their sheaths. In these kudzu leaves, do we not already have the beginnings of what is to be cut and boiled, the material for fine and coarse cloth? Just as the kudzu grows, yellow birds appear, their feathers gleaming as they fly through the warm, mild sky. After circling, they alight, folding their wings atop the bushy trees. Listen to their song: in harmonious notes they give free voice to their calls for companions, reaching even the most distant places. They tune their reed-like tongues, and all who have ears hear them. These yellow birds, at ease where they lodge and finding a suitable resting place—have they not come because of the kudzu leaves? Thus, when the plants flourish, one can already discern the beginnings of the work of making fine and coarse cloth; when living creatures come to sing, they in turn attest to the luxuriant growth of the kudzu leaves. Having completed her textile work, the royal consort recalls even these things: is this not because she does not forget its origins…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
者哉抑考葛覃之詩后妃所自作而無賛美之
詞然其勤儉孝敬之德悉具焉宜其配至尊而
爲宗廟主也桃夭兎罝芣苢之風漢廣汝墳之
化曾謂無所本哉嗚呼文王身脩家齊之效亦
可見矣雖然內有賢妃所以助之者深虞之二
女夏之塗山殷之有娀周之太姒其致一也讀
是詩者又當知周之所以興乎
明明天子令聞不已
潘大賓
===
同考試官訓導黃批不已處得穆公之心可謂善說詩者
同考試官教諭朱批講不已最是
同考試官學正李批令聞不已含下文矢文德洽四國之
意此作得之
考試官教諭張批說明召穆公愛君之心錄之
考試官教諭應批穆公以文德望其君此作發揚盡矣
大臣賛中興之賢君益中興之善譽蓋善譽固
難而益之尤可尚也古人於君美而進之如此
忠愛之心何如哉昔宣王命召穆公平淮南之
punctuated:
者哉？抑考《葛覃》之詩，后妃所自作，而無賛美之詞，然其勤儉孝敬之德悉具焉，宜其配至尊而爲宗廟主也。《桃夭》《兎罝》《芣苢》之風，《漢廣》《汝墳》之化，曾謂無所本哉？嗚呼！文王身脩家齊之效，亦可見矣。雖然，內有賢妃，所以助之者深。虞之二女、夏之塗山、殷之有娀、周之太姒，其致一也。讀是詩者，又當知周之所以興乎！
明明天子，令聞不已。
潘大賓
同考試官訓導黃批：「不已處得穆公之心，可謂善說詩者。」
同考試官教諭朱批：「講不已最是。」
同考試官學正李批：「令聞不已，含下文矢文德洽四國之意，此作得之。」
考試官教諭張批：「說明召穆公愛君之心，錄之。」
考試官教諭應批：「穆公以文德望其君，此作發揚盡矣。」
大臣賛中興之賢君，益中興之善譽。蓋善譽固難，而益之尤可尚也。古人於君，美而進之如此，忠愛之心何如哉！昔宣王命召穆公平淮南之
translation_en:
…one who did not forget her beginnings? Moreover, consider the poem “The Kudzu Spreads” (Ge tan): the royal consort composed it herself, and it contains no words of praise for her; nevertheless, her virtues of diligence, frugality, filial piety, and reverence are all present in it. Fittingly, she became the consort of the supreme ruler and presided over the ancestral temple. Could the moral influence expressed in “The Peach Tree” (Tao yao), “The Rabbit Nets” (Tu ju), and “Plantain” (Fu yi), and the transforming influence expressed in “The Broad Han” (Han guang) and “The Banks of the Ru” (Ru fen), possibly have had no source? Ah! Here we can also see the effects of King Wen’s cultivation of himself and ordering of his household. Yet within the palace there was a worthy consort whose assistance was profound. The two daughters associated with Yu, the woman of Tushan associated with Xia, the woman of Yousong associated with Yin, and Tai Si of Zhou were alike in this respect. Those who read this poem should also recognize why Zhou rose to power!

“Resplendent is the Son of Heaven; his fine reputation never ceases.”
Pan Dabin

Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The treatment of ‘never ceases’ captures Duke Mu’s intent. The author may be called a skilled interpreter of the Odes.”

Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “The explanation of ‘never ceases’ is particularly apt.”

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “‘His fine reputation never ceases’ contains the meaning of the subsequent passage, ‘He sets forth his civil virtue, bringing harmony to the four quarters.’ This composition captures it.”

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “It elucidates Duke Mu of Shao’s love for his ruler. Include it.”

Examiner Ying, Instructor, comments: “Duke Mu looked to his ruler to display civil virtue. This composition fully brings out that meaning.”

A great minister praises the worthy ruler who restores the dynasty, urging him to enhance the fine reputation of that restoration. For a fine reputation is certainly difficult to achieve, and enhancing it is still more admirable. Such was the way men of antiquity praised their rulers and urged them onward: how deep their loyalty and affection! Formerly, King Xuan commanded Duke Mu of Shao to pacify the … south of the Huai River …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
夷詩人美之至此則述穆公美其君而進之之
詞若曰王業必厎於大成治道不貴於自足我
明明之天子也遠紹文武之顯承而煥重明於
五位近纉成康之熙洽而炳離照於九重旁燭
無疆誠不世出之主光被四表實大有爲之君
試以興師江漢則跋扈來歸而乾坤有再造之
績赫赫厥聲洋溢遐邇可謂有令聞矣且將如
日方升有隆而未艾用兵淮夷則桀驁内附而
日月啟重光之運濯濯厥靈流布夷夏是固有
善譽矣殆必如川方至有增而不已圖關長治
之謀而充拓光前之業頌於今而曰興衰者播
揚於後日則曰中國之聖人焉慮切乂安之計
而恢弘裕後之規稱於今而曰撥亂者膾炙於
方來則曰太平之令主焉是則致令聞者固在
於武功之成益令聞者又出於武功之外也吾
王庶幾以文德而加之意哉考之舞干羽而有
苗格退脩教而崇侯降聖帝明王雖用兵之際
猶以文德爲本况武功既成之後而可不濟之
punctuated: 夷，詩人美之。至此，則述穆公美其君而進之之詞，若曰：「王業必厎於大成，治道不貴於自足。我明明之天子也，遠紹文武之顯承，而煥重明於五位；近纉成康之熙洽，而炳離照於九重。旁燭無疆，誠不世出之主；光被四表，實大有爲之君。試以興師江漢，則跋扈來歸，而乾坤有再造之績。赫赫厥聲，洋溢遐邇，可謂有令聞矣，且將如日方升，有隆而未艾。用兵淮夷，則桀驁内附，而日月啟重光之運。濯濯厥靈，流布夷夏，是固有善譽矣，殆必如川方至，有增而不已。圖關長治之謀，而充拓光前之業，頌於今而曰興衰者，播揚於後日，則曰中國之聖人焉。慮切乂安之計，而恢弘裕後之規，稱於今而曰撥亂者，膾炙於方來，則曰太平之令主焉。是則致令聞者，固在於武功之成；益令聞者，又出於武功之外也。吾王庶幾以文德而加之意哉！」考之，舞干羽而有苗格，退脩教而崇侯降。聖帝明王，雖用兵之際，猶以文德爲本，况武功既成之後，而可不濟之
translation_en:
…the Yi peoples, and the poet praised him. At this point, the poem relates the words with which Duke Mu praised his ruler and urged him onward, as if to say: “The royal enterprise must be brought to full accomplishment; in the way of government, complacency is no virtue. Our brilliantly enlightened Son of Heaven reaches back to continue the illustrious legacy of Kings Wen and Wu, displaying renewed brilliance in the fifth position, the ruler’s seat. He carries forward the more recent flourishing harmony of Kings Cheng and Kang, shining with the radiance of fire within the ninefold palace. His light shines in every direction without limit: truly he is a ruler seldom seen in the world. His radiance reaches the four farthest bounds: truly he is a sovereign capable of great achievements.

“When he raised an army in the Jiang and Han regions, the unruly came over in submission, and he accomplished the renewal of Heaven and Earth. His resounding fame spread far and near: he may indeed be said to possess an excellent reputation. Moreover, like the newly rising sun, it will continue to grow without abating. When he campaigned against the Huai Yi, the defiant submitted to his authority, and the sun and moon ushered in an era of renewed light. His shining majesty spread among Yi peoples and Xia alike: he certainly possesses a fine reputation. Surely, like a river whose waters are arriving, it must increase without end.

“He devises plans concerned with lasting good government and expands achievements that outshine those of earlier times. Those who praise him today as one who revives what has declined will spread his fame in later days, calling him the sage of the Central States. His thoughts dwell earnestly on measures for order and peace, and he enlarges plans that will enrich posterity. Those who acclaim him today as one who puts down disorder will celebrate him in times to come as the excellent ruler of an age of great peace. Thus, gaining an excellent reputation certainly rests upon the accomplishment of military exploits; increasing that reputation, however, requires something beyond military exploits. May our king give thought to adding civil virtue to these achievements!”

“By way of evidence, when shields and feather plumes were brandished in a dance, the Youmiao submitted; when the ruler withdrew and cultivated moral instruction, the Marquis of Chong surrendered. Even when employing troops, sage emperors and enlightened kings still took civil virtue as their foundation. How much more, once military success has been achieved, can they fail to complement it with…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以文以消其窮黷之心以衍太平之業乎此忠
愛之穆公所以拳拳於令聞不已進其君而必
繼之以矢其文德洽此四國也嗚呼宣王卒為
有周中興之賢王者謂召穆公無少助焉可乎
春秋
盟于召陵齊人執陳轅濤塗秋及江
人黃人伐陳冬十有二月公孫玆帥
師會齊人宋人衛人鄭人許人曹人侵
陳〔俱僖公四年〕
劉一松
同考試官教諭王批大傳於齊桓服楚虐陳得失
自見此作援引斷制明白有學之士也
考試官教諭張批通暢可取
考試官教諭應批得謹嚴之體可錄
霸事有近於王者春秋序其績霸德有歉於王
者春秋重其譏此桓公不戰以服楚庶幾王者
之事而逞威以虐陳殊無王者之德也春秋予
奪之宜哉且屈完觀師結盟而退則桓之伐楚
punctuated:
以文，以消其窮黷之心，以衍太平之業乎？此忠愛之穆公所以拳拳於令聞，不已進其君，而必繼之以矢其文德，洽此四國也。嗚呼！宣王卒為有周中興之賢王者，謂召穆公無少助焉，可乎？

春秋

盟于召陵。齊人執陳轅濤塗。秋，及江人、黃人伐陳。冬，十有二月，公孫玆帥師，會齊人、宋人、衛人、鄭人、許人、曹人侵陳。〔俱僖公四年〕

劉一松

同考試官教諭王批：大傳於齊桓服楚虐陳，得失自見。此作援引斷制明白，有學之士也。

考試官教諭張批：通暢可取。

考試官教諭應批：得謹嚴之體，可錄。

霸事有近於王者，春秋序其績；霸德有歉於王者，春秋重其譏。此桓公不戰以服楚，庶幾王者之事，而逞威以虐陳，殊無王者之德也。春秋予奪之宜哉！且屈完觀師，結盟而退，則桓之伐楚
translation_en:
…with civil virtue, to dispel his impulse toward unrestrained warfare and perpetuate the achievement of peace? This is why Duke Mu, loyal and devoted, was so earnestly concerned with his ruler’s good reputation: he never ceased encouraging his ruler to advance, and insisted that military achievement be followed by the display of civil virtue, bringing harmony to the states of the four quarters. Ah! King Xuan ultimately became the worthy king who restored the fortunes of Zhou. Could one say that Duke Mu of Shao contributed nothing to this?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“They concluded an alliance at Shaoling. The men of Qi seized Yuan Taotu of Chen. In autumn, together with the men of Jiang and Huang, they attacked Chen. In winter, in the twelfth month, Gongsun Zi led an army to join the men of Qi, Song, Wei, Zheng, Xu, and Cao in invading Chen.” 〔All these entries are from the fourth year of Duke Xi.〕

Liu Yisong

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “In the Great Commentary [?], the merits and faults of Duke Huan of Qi’s subjugation of Chu and mistreatment of Chen are evident of themselves. This essay is clear in its citations and judgments. Its author is a man of learning.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Fluent and lucid; worthy of acceptance.”

Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: “It achieves a careful and rigorous style; it may be selected.”

Where a hegemon’s deeds approach those of a true king, the Spring and Autumn Annals recounts his achievements; where a hegemon’s virtue falls short of that of a true king, the Spring and Autumn Annals censures him severely. Thus Duke Huan’s subjugation of Chu without fighting came close to the conduct of a true king, whereas his flaunting of might to mistreat Chen utterly lacked a true king’s virtue. How fitting are the praise and blame bestowed by the Spring and Autumn Annals! Moreover, Qu Wan inspected the army, concluded an alliance, and withdrew; thus Duke Huan’s campaign against Chu…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
固未大挫也春秋予之何耶誠以脩德來遠王
者之事也伐楚之役語兵力則已强矣語敵國
則已服矣在常情孰不欲一戰以取捷也而桓
也從容退舍盟好是脩兵雖强也以律用之而
不暴敵已服也以禮下之而不驕其心必曰善
爲國者不師善師者不陣善陣者不戰吾何以
勝楚爲哉噫舞干而苗格者舜也因壘而崇降
者文王也桓之服楚殆庶幾乎故春秋特書盟
于召陵所以序其績者如此迨夫齊欲徑陳陳
===
不果納則桓之怒陳似未爲過也春秋奪之何
耶誠以敬慎不渝王者之德也召陵之盟語其
志則已得矣語其功則已盛矣在君子必將益
脩德以保終也而桓也驕心一生舉動頓異執
濤塗未已也復合兵以伐其國伐其國未足也
復潛師以掠其境曾不思曰愛人不親反其仁
治人不治反其智禮人不答反其敬吾何以責
陳爲哉噫勝夏而慄慄危懼成湯也東征而四
國是皇周公也桓之虐陳寧無歉乎故春秋始
punctuated:
固未大挫也，春秋予之何耶？誠以脩德來遠，王者之事也。伐楚之役，語兵力則已强矣，語敵國則已服矣。在常情，孰不欲一戰以取捷也？而桓也從容退舍，盟好是脩。兵雖强也，以律用之而不暴；敵已服也，以禮下之而不驕。其心必曰：「善爲國者不師，善師者不陣，善陣者不戰。吾何以勝楚爲哉？」噫！舞干而苗格者，舜也；因壘而崇降者，文王也。桓之服楚，殆庶幾乎！故春秋特書「盟于召陵」，所以序其績者如此。
迨夫齊欲徑陳，陳不果納，則桓之怒陳似未爲過也。春秋奪之何耶？誠以敬慎不渝，王者之德也。召陵之盟，語其志則已得矣，語其功則已盛矣。在君子，必將益脩德以保終也。而桓也驕心一生，舉動頓異。執濤塗未已也，復合兵以伐其國；伐其國未足也，復潛師以掠其境。曾不思曰：「愛人不親，反其仁；治人不治，反其智；禮人不答，反其敬。吾何以責陳爲哉？」噫！勝夏而慄慄危懼，成湯也；東征而四國是皇，周公也。桓之虐陳，寧無歉乎？故春秋始
translation_en:
…certainly had not inflicted any great defeat. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals accord him approval? Precisely because cultivating virtue to attract those far away is the work of a true king. In the campaign against Chu, his military strength was already overwhelming, and the opposing state had already submitted. By ordinary human sentiment, who would not have wished to win a victory in battle? Yet Duke Huan calmly withdrew his encampment and cultivated friendship through a covenant. Though his forces were strong, he employed them with discipline and without violence; though his enemy had submitted, he treated it with ritual courtesy and humility, without arrogance. He must surely have thought: “One who governs a state well does not resort to armies; one who commands armies well does not deploy them for battle; one who deploys them well does not fight. What need have I to defeat Chu?” Ah! It was Shun whose shield dance brought the Miao to submit; it was King Wen whose use of the existing ramparts brought Chong to surrender. Duke Huan’s subjugation of Chu came close indeed to these achievements! Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals expressly records that they “made a covenant at Shaoling.” Such was its way of giving due recognition to his accomplishment.
When Qi wished to pass through Chen and Chen ultimately refused it entry, Duke Huan’s anger at Chen would seem not to have been excessive. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals withhold its approval? Precisely because unwavering reverence and caution are the virtues of a true king. At the covenant of Shaoling, his ambitions had already been fulfilled and his achievement was already splendid. A gentleman would surely have cultivated his virtue still further, to ensure a good conclusion. But once arrogance arose in Duke Huan’s heart, his conduct changed abruptly. Not content with seizing Taotu, he again assembled troops to attack Taotu’s state; not satisfied with attacking that state, he again sent troops covertly to plunder its territory. He never thought to say: “If I love others and they do not draw close, I should examine my own benevolence; if I govern others and they remain ungoverned, I should examine my own wisdom; if I treat others courteously and they do not reciprocate, I should examine my own respectfulness. What grounds have I to blame Chen?” Ah! It was Cheng Tang who, after defeating Xia, trembled with apprehension and fear; it was the Duke of Zhou whose eastern expedition brought the four states to revere him. Could Duke Huan’s cruel treatment of Chen have been without deficiency? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals initially…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而稱人繼而書侵所以重其譏者又如此嗟夫
莫貴於王莫賤於霸王者之可貴規模宏大而
憂樂吉凶不足以動其方寸也霸者之可賤識
量淺狹而勝負得喪足以移其常心也王霸之
分大率如此然究其歸則在誠與僞之間耳故
曰以德行仁者王以力假仁者霸假之一字深
得春秋誅心之法
楚子伐鄭晉郤缺帥師救鄭宣公九年楚
子伐鄭宣公十年
===
同考試官教諭王批謹夷夏之防明君臣之義為主能
玩詞同意異之傳是可錄矣
考試官教諭張批得春秋屬比之意
考試官教諭應批合傳可取
春秋貶外夷虐貳而錄內救以見意不貶外夷
虐貳而削內救以示義觀于楚兩伐鄭而詞同
意異有以見聖人謹大防明大倫也慨昔中國
之霸緒寢微外夷之虐焰漸熾有曰楚莊崛起
banxin: 鄉試錄 四十一 周舜卿
punctuated:
而稱人，繼而書侵，所以重其譏者又如此。嗟夫！莫貴於王，莫賤於霸。王者之可貴，規模宏大，而憂樂吉凶不足以動其方寸也；霸者之可賤，識量淺狹，而勝負得喪足以移其常心也。王霸之分，大率如此。然究其歸，則在誠與僞之間耳。故曰：「以德行仁者王，以力假仁者霸。」假之一字，深得春秋誅心之法。
楚子伐鄭，晉郤缺帥師救鄭。宣公九年。楚子伐鄭。宣公十年。
同考試官教諭王批：謹夷夏之防，明君臣之義為主，能玩詞同意異之傳，是可錄矣。
考試官教諭張批：得春秋屬比之意。
考試官教諭應批：合傳可取。
春秋貶外夷虐貳，而錄內救以見意；不貶外夷虐貳，而削內救以示義。觀于楚兩伐鄭，而詞同意異，有以見聖人謹大防、明大倫也。慨昔中國之霸緒寢微，外夷之虐焰漸熾，有曰楚莊，崛起
translation_en:
…and designated them as “men,” then subsequently recorded their action as an “incursion”: this, too, was how it intensified its censure. Alas! Nothing is more estimable than true kingship, and nothing more contemptible than hegemony. What makes the true king estimable is the grandeur of his scope: sorrow and joy, good fortune and ill cannot disturb his heart. What makes the hegemon contemptible is the shallowness and narrowness of his understanding and capacity: victory and defeat, gain and loss suffice to unsettle his habitual disposition. Such, broadly, is the distinction between kingship and hegemony. Yet, traced to its ultimate basis, it lies simply between sincerity and pretence. Thus it is said: “One who practises benevolence through virtue becomes a true king; one who uses force to borrow the guise of benevolence becomes a hegemon.” The single word “borrow” profoundly captures the Spring and Autumn Annals’ method of censuring underlying motives.
“The Viscount of Chu attacked Zheng. Xi Que of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng.” Ninth year of Duke Xuan. “The Viscount of Chu attacked Zheng.” Tenth year of Duke Xuan.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: It takes as its central concerns safeguarding the distinction between the Yi and the Xia and clarifying the obligations between ruler and minister. It thoughtfully considers the commentary’s explanation of identical wording with different meanings. This merits inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: It grasps the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in linking and comparing entries.
Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: It accords with the commentary and is worthy of selection.
The Spring and Autumn Annals censures the foreign Yi for brutal treatment of a state wavering in its allegiance, and records the relief furnished by a state of the central realm to reveal its intent. Elsewhere, it does not censure the foreign Yi for brutal treatment of a wavering state, and omits the relief furnished by a state of the central realm to convey its judgment. Examining Chu’s two attacks on Zheng, where the wording is identical but the meaning differs, we can see how the Sage guarded the great distinction and clarified the fundamental human relationships. Alas, in former times the succession of hegemons in the central states gradually weakened, while the flames of foreign aggression grew ever fiercer. There was one known as King Zhuang of Chu, who rose abruptly…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
爭衡魯宣九年興師伐鄭斯時也鄭無可討之
罪而楚以僭竊之夷惟欲肆其强暴以服鄭爲
事非義舉矣幸而晉成畏此簡書特遣卻缺將
兵救鄭奏凱柳棼則誠攘夷狄安諸夏之兵也
春秋欲彰楚之罪得不錄晉之善乎故於楚之
伐鄭特稱爵者傳曰貶詞也若曰國君自將恃
强壓弱憑陵中夏之稱也知然者以下書晉卻
缺帥師救鄭則貶楚可知矣聖人謹夷夏之防
蓋如此嗣是南北之干戈日尋鄭人之玉帛兩
===
事楚莊憤怒力爭經營魯宣十年復駕伐鄭斯
時也陳有弑逆之惡而晉主中夏之盟苟能奉
行天討以風示天下斯盡職矣夫何晉景舍此
大義顧命士會舉兵爭鄭宣威潁北則失誅亂
臣討賊子之義也春秋欲著晉之罪得不沒其
救乎故於楚之伐鄭亦稱爵者傳曰直詞也若
曰以實屬詞書其重者而意不以楚爲罪也知
然者以傳書晉士會救鄭而經削之則責晉可
知矣聖人明君臣之義又如此嗟夫躬天下之
punctuated:
爭衡。魯宣九年，興師伐鄭。斯時也，鄭無可討之罪，而楚以僭竊之夷，惟欲肆其强暴，以服鄭爲事，非義舉矣。幸而晉成畏此簡書，特遣卻缺將兵救鄭，奏凱柳棼，則誠攘夷狄、安諸夏之兵也。《春秋》欲彰楚之罪，得不錄晉之善乎？故於楚之伐鄭特稱爵者，傳曰：「貶詞也。」若曰，國君自將，恃强壓弱，憑陵中夏之稱也。知然者，以下書晉卻缺帥師救鄭，則貶楚可知矣。聖人謹夷夏之防，蓋如此。
嗣是南北之干戈日尋，鄭人之玉帛兩事。楚莊憤怒，力爭經營，魯宣十年，復駕伐鄭。斯時也，陳有弑逆之惡，而晉主中夏之盟，苟能奉行天討，以風示天下，斯盡職矣。夫何晉景舍此大義，顧命士會舉兵爭鄭，宣威潁北，則失誅亂臣、討賊子之義也。《春秋》欲著晉之罪，得不沒其救乎？故於楚之伐鄭亦稱爵者，傳曰：「直詞也。」若曰，以實屬詞，書其重者，而意不以楚爲罪也。知然者，以傳書晉士會救鄭而經削之，則責晉可知矣。聖人明君臣之義，又如此。
嗟夫！躬天下之
translation_en:
…to contend for supremacy. In the ninth year of Duke Xuan of Lu, he raised an army to attack Zheng. At that time, Zheng had committed no offense warranting punishment. Yet Chu, a barbarian state that had usurped royal rank, sought only to unleash its violence and force Zheng into submission. This was no righteous undertaking. Fortunately, Duke Cheng of Jin, mindful of the obligations conveyed in the written summons, specially dispatched Que Que to lead troops to rescue Zheng. They returned victorious from Liufen [?]: this was truly an army that repelled the barbarians and secured the Chinese states. If the Spring and Autumn Annals wished to expose Chu’s guilt, could it fail to record Jin’s good deed? Thus, in recording Chu’s attack on Zheng, it specifically designated its ruler by his noble rank. The commentary says: “This is language of censure.” It is as though this designation says that the ruler personally commanded his forces, relying on strength to oppress the weak and overbearing the central Chinese states. We know this because the following entry records that Que Que of Jin led an army to rescue Zheng; the censure of Chu is therefore apparent. Such was the Sage’s care in maintaining the boundary between barbarians and the Chinese states.
Thereafter, warfare between north and south continued day after day, and the people of Zheng served both sides with offerings of jade and silk. King Zhuang of Chu, enraged, exerted himself in the struggle and laid his plans. In the tenth year of Duke Xuan of Lu, he again set out to attack Zheng. At that time, Chen had been stained by the crime of regicide, while Jin presided over the covenant of the central Chinese states. Had Jin carried out Heaven’s punishment and thereby admonished all under Heaven, it would have fulfilled its duty. Why, then, did Duke Jing of Jin abandon this great obligation and instead order Shi Hui to raise troops to contest control of Zheng, displaying his might north of the Ying River? In doing so, he failed in the duty to execute rebellious ministers and punish treacherous sons. If the Spring and Autumn Annals wished to make Jin’s guilt manifest, could it fail to omit its rescue of Zheng? Thus, when recording Chu’s attack on Zheng, it again designated its ruler by his noble rank. The commentary says: “This is straightforward language.” It is as though the wording was fitted to the facts, recording the weightier matter, without intending to condemn Chu. We know this because the commentary records that Shi Hui of Jin rescued Zheng, while the classic omits it; the reproach directed at Jin is therefore apparent. Such, too, was the Sage’s clarification of the duties between ruler and minister.
Alas! Personally to shoulder the world’s…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
大難斯可以成天下之大業桓文所以得諸侯
霸天下以其內獎王室外攘夷狄剪篡鋤兇汲
汲焉躬天下之難耳奈何春秋中葉霸圖不競
靈成景弗克負荷以討賊之大權遺楚莊號令
辰陵噫此中國所以淪於為夷而世道所以降
為戰國也安得起桓文於九原以定安攘之計
禮記
致禮以治躬則莊敬莊敬則嚴威
舒素蘊
===
同考試官教諭唐批莊敬嚴威處主表為說無此意說
理詳明措詞整潔真羣究心於禮者
考試官教諭張批簡明可錄
考試官教諭應批得旨
君子窮禮以脩身則禮之驗著於外矣蓋禮所
以管攝乎人情者也君子以之脩身則莊敬嚴
威之驗豈容已乎記樂者謂夫禮之不可斯須
去身者正以禮可以脩外焉耳彼經禮三百天
理所存也誠能研窮其要領以為檢身之準繩
punctuated:
大難，斯可以成天下之大業。桓文所以得諸侯、霸天下，以其內獎王室，外攘夷狄，剪篡鋤兇，汲汲焉躬天下之難耳。奈何春秋中葉，霸圖不競，靈成景弗克負荷，以討賊之大權遺楚莊，號令辰陵。噫！此中國所以淪於為夷，而世道所以降為戰國也。安得起桓文於九原，以定安攘之計？
禮記
致禮以治躬，則莊敬；莊敬，則嚴威。
舒素蘊
同考試官教諭唐批：莊敬嚴威處，主表為說，無此意。說理詳明，措詞整潔，真羣究心於禮者。
考試官教諭張批：簡明可錄。
考試官教諭應批：得旨。
君子窮禮以脩身，則禮之驗著於外矣。蓋禮所以管攝乎人情者也，君子以之脩身，則莊敬嚴威之驗豈容已乎？記樂者謂夫禮之不可斯須去身者，正以禮可以脩外焉耳。彼經禮三百，天理所存也，誠能研窮其要領，以為檢身之準繩
translation_en:
…the great difficulties of the world: only thus can one accomplish the world's great undertakings. Dukes Huan and Wen won the allegiance of the feudal lords and established hegemony over the realm because, within, they supported the royal house and, without, repelled the Yi and Di, cutting down usurpers and rooting out evildoers, earnestly taking upon themselves the world's difficulties. Why, then, in the middle of the Spring and Autumn period, did the enterprise of hegemony falter? Dukes Ling, Cheng, and Jing could not shoulder the burden, leaving the great authority to punish rebels to King Zhuang of Chu, who issued commands at Chenling. Alas! This is why the central states sank into barbarism and the course of the age declined into the Warring States. How might we raise Huan and Wen from their graves to settle a policy for securing the realm and repelling outsiders?
Record of Rites
“When one fully applies ritual to the regulation of one's person, one becomes dignified and reverent; being dignified and reverent, one becomes august and imposing.”
Shu Suyun
Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: In discussing dignity, reverence, augustness, and imposing bearing, the explanation centers on outward appearance, though this is not the intended meaning [?]. The reasoning is detailed and clear, and the wording orderly and polished. Truly someone who has devoted thought to ritual [?].
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Concise and clear; worthy of selection.
Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: Captures the essential meaning.
When the gentleman thoroughly investigates ritual in order to cultivate himself, its effects become manifest outwardly. Ritual is what regulates and restrains human feelings. When the gentleman uses it to cultivate himself, how could its effects—dignity, reverence, augustness, and imposing bearing—fail to appear? The author of the Record of Music says that ritual must not depart from one's person even for a moment precisely because ritual can cultivate one's outward conduct. Those three hundred principal rules of ritual are where heavenly principle resides. If one can truly investigate their essentials thoroughly and take them as the standard for disciplining oneself…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
匪但稽其繁文而已曲禮三千妙道所寓也誠
能推究其旨歸以為脩身之矩度非徒事其末
節而已或視聽也非禮勿視非禮勿聽而省察
克治之必力或言動也言不過辭動不過則而
體驗力行之益至夫然則脩身之功盡而驗之
著於外者當何如哉吾見不矜而莊衣冠自爾
其整齊不動而敬瞻視自爾其尊重出入起居
罔有不欽也動容周旋自中乎禮也不亦莊敬
矣乎旣莊敬矣將見翼翼德容形於謙光之際
===
抑抑威儀見於晉接之頃色足憚貌足畏凜然
有不敢慢者在也威可畏儀可象儼然有不可
犯者存也不其嚴威矣乎君子致禮治躬之驗
如此然則著誠去僞之心其可少有間斷哉嗟
夫心與身相為流通禮與樂不可偏廢君子致
禮以治躬致樂以治心內外交養功夫罔間至
於內和而外順則德煇動於內而民莫不承聽
理發諸外而民莫不承順禮樂之有益於心身
豈細故哉古昔聖帝明王致雍熙悠久之盛治
punctuated: 匪但稽其繁文而已。曲禮三千，妙道所寓也，誠能推究其旨歸，以為脩身之矩度，非徒事其末節而已。或視聽也，非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，而省察克治之必力；或言動也，言不過辭，動不過則，而體驗力行之益至。夫然，則脩身之功盡，而驗之著於外者當何如哉？吾見不矜而莊，衣冠自爾其整齊；不動而敬，瞻視自爾其尊重。出入起居，罔有不欽也；動容周旋，自中乎禮也。不亦莊敬矣乎？旣莊敬矣，將見翼翼德容形於謙光之際，抑抑威儀見於晉接之頃。色足憚，貌足畏，凜然有不敢慢者在也；威可畏，儀可象，儼然有不可犯者存也。不其嚴威矣乎？君子致禮治躬之驗如此，然則著誠去僞之心，其可少有間斷哉？嗟夫！心與身相為流通，禮與樂不可偏廢。君子致禮以治躬，致樂以治心，內外交養，功夫罔間。至於內和而外順，則德煇動於內，而民莫不承聽；理發諸外，而民莫不承順。禮樂之有益於心身，豈細故哉？古昔聖帝明王致雍熙悠久之盛治
translation_en:
…not merely examine their elaborate forms. The three thousand detailed rules of ritual are where the subtle Way resides. If one can truly investigate their purport, making them the standards for cultivating oneself, one will not merely attend to their minor details. In looking and listening, one looks at nothing contrary to ritual and listens to nothing contrary to ritual, exerting oneself fully in self-examination and self-mastery. In speech and action, one’s words do not exceed the bounds of appropriate expression, and one’s movements do not exceed the rules; one becomes ever more thorough in personally apprehending and diligently practicing them. When this is so, the work of self-cultivation is complete. How, then, will its effects manifest themselves outwardly? I see that one is dignified without affectation, one’s cap and robes naturally orderly; reverent without exertion, one’s gaze naturally respectful. In going out and coming in, rising and resting, one is never without reverence; one’s bearing and every movement naturally accord with ritual. Is this not dignity and reverence? Once dignified and reverent, one’s attentively virtuous bearing will appear in the radiance of humility, and one’s measured deportment will be evident when receiving and meeting others. One’s expression commands awe, one’s appearance inspires respect: there is a solemn quality that none dares slight. One’s majesty inspires awe and one’s deportment provides a model: there is a gravity that none dares affront. Is this not solemnity and majesty? Such are the effects when the gentleman brings ritual to its fullest realization in governing his person. How, then, could his resolve to manifest sincerity and eliminate falseness admit even the slightest interruption?

Ah! Heart and body communicate with one another, and neither ritual nor music may be neglected. The gentleman brings ritual to its fullest realization to govern his person, and music to its fullest realization to govern his heart. He nourishes the inner and outer together, without interruption in his efforts. When he attains harmony within and accord without, the radiance of virtue stirs within, and none among the people fails to heed him; principle manifests itself outwardly, and none among the people fails to comply. Could the benefit that ritual and music confer upon heart and body be a trifling matter? That the sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity attained a flourishing reign of harmony and enduring peace…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
者用此道也故曰致禮樂之道舉而措之天下
無難矣
言而履之禮也行而樂之樂也
陳大韶
同考試官教諭唐批知和序之理本於人君之身且詞不
陳腐宜錄之以式後學
考試官教諭張批理明詞暢
考試官教諭應批禮樂重人君說可取
聖人答賢者問政有指所以爲序之道者有指
===
所以爲和之道者蓋禮樂之道和序而已自非
聖人指其言行之本於吾身者以示子張抑孰
知其然哉且禮樂之道舉而措之固可化成乎
天下遡而求之初非有外於吾身何則言者心
之聲言而不履於理如禮何必也游言不倡所
倡者措之於躬行妄言不發所發者形之於實
踐如言夫閨門也使夫內外之有辨而毋事乎
虛文言夫朝廷也使夫貴賤之有章而務求其
明驗言而履之如此則自然之序得之於我而
punctuated:
者，用此道也。故曰：「致禮樂之道，舉而措之天下，無難矣。」

言而履之，禮也；行而樂之，樂也。

陳大韶

同考試官教諭唐批：知和序之理本於人君之身，且詞不陳腐，宜錄之以式後學。
考試官教諭張批：理明詞暢。
考試官教諭應批：禮樂重人君，說可取。

聖人答賢者問政，有指所以爲序之道者，有指所以爲和之道者。蓋禮樂之道，和序而已。自非聖人指其言行之本於吾身者以示子張，抑孰知其然哉？且禮樂之道，舉而措之，固可化成乎天下；遡而求之，初非有外於吾身。何則？言者，心之聲。言而不履於理，如禮何？必也游言不倡，所倡者措之於躬行；妄言不發，所發者形之於實踐。如言夫閨門也，使夫內外之有辨，而毋事乎虛文；言夫朝廷也，使夫貴賤之有章，而務求其明驗。言而履之如此，則自然之序得之於我，而
translation_en:
…achieved this by employing this Way. Thus it is said: “Bring the Way of rites and music to its fullest realization and apply it throughout the realm, and there will be no difficulty.”

“To speak and put one’s words into practice is ritual; to act and take pleasure in doing so is music.”

Chen Dashao

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: He understands that the principles of harmony and order are rooted in the ruler’s own person. Moreover, his language is not stale. This should be recorded as a model for later students.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The reasoning is clear and the language fluent.
Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: His explanation that rites and music place particular weight on the ruler is worthy of adoption.

When the sage answered the worthy man’s questions about government, some of his statements indicated the way to establish order, while others indicated the way to establish harmony. For the Way of rites and music consists simply in harmony and order. Had the sage not shown Zizhang that its words and actions are rooted in one’s own person, who would have understood that this was so? Indeed, when the Way of rites and music is taken up and applied, it can transform the whole realm; yet if we trace it back to its source, it has never been external to our own persons. Why is this? Words are the voice of the heart. If one speaks but does not put principle into practice, what becomes of ritual? One must refrain from advancing idle words, and personally carry out whatever one does advance; one must refrain from uttering reckless words, and give concrete effect to whatever one does utter. Thus, when speaking of the household, one must ensure that the inner and outer spheres are distinguished, without concerning oneself with empty formalities. When speaking of the court, one must ensure that distinctions between noble and humble are manifest, striving for clear evidence of their realization. If one speaks and puts one’s words into practice in this way, the natural order is realized in oneself, and…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
小大顯微之禮胥此焉備所以一法制而防範
人情者如是所以辨上下而綱維世變者如是
矣若乃几筵之鋪獻酬之交特儀物耳禮云乎
哉行者言之實行而不樂乎理如樂何必也優
而游之凡躬行者脫然而無所累厭而飫之凡
實踐者坦然而無所疑行之閨門而成肅雍和
睦之化無乖戾也行之朝廷而有都俞吁咈之
風何順適也行而樂之如此則自然之和由我
而出而欣喜歡愛之樂於是乎具所以和神人
===
而通天下之志者如是所以移風俗而平天下
之情者如是矣若乃綴兆之行鐘鼓之作特聲
容耳樂云乎哉吁禮樂之道本乎言行如此君
子可不深探其本哉大抵至禮不讓而天下治
至樂無聲而天下和世之人主顧乃不能養中
正而樂和平以先乎天下而徒規規於制度文
爲之末以爲粉飾太平之具治道之不古若又
何怪哉
第貳場
punctuated:
小大顯微之禮胥此焉備。所以一法制而防範人情者如是，所以辨上下而綱維世變者如是矣。若乃几筵之鋪、獻酬之交，特儀物耳，禮云乎哉？行者，言之實。行而不樂乎理，如樂何？必也優而游之，凡躬行者脫然而無所累；厭而飫之，凡實踐者坦然而無所疑。行之閨門而成肅雍和睦之化，無乖戾也；行之朝廷而有都俞吁咈之風，何順適也！行而樂之如此，則自然之和由我而出，而欣喜歡愛之樂於是乎具。所以和神人而通天下之志者如是，所以移風俗而平天下之情者如是矣。若乃綴兆之行、鐘鼓之作，特聲容耳，樂云乎哉？吁！禮樂之道本乎言行如此，君子可不深探其本哉？大抵至禮不讓而天下治，至樂無聲而天下和。世之人主顧乃不能養中正而樂和平，以先乎天下，而徒規規於制度文爲之末，以爲粉飾太平之具。治道之不古若，又何怪哉？

第貳場
translation_en:
…and rites, great and small, manifest and subtle, are all fully present therein. This is how laws and institutions are unified and human feelings kept within bounds; this is how distinctions between superior and inferior are maintained and the changing affairs of the world held in order. As for setting out stands and mats and exchanging ceremonial offerings of wine, these are merely ritual objects and observances. Can these alone be called ritual? Conduct is the realization of words. If one acts without taking delight in principle, what can one do with music? One must dwell at ease in it, so that all one personally carries out is free and unencumbered; one must become thoroughly steeped and satisfied in it, so that all one puts into practice is composed and without doubt. Practiced within the household, it brings about a transformation toward reverence, concord, and harmony, without discord. Practiced at court, it produces a spirit of frank assent and dissent—how harmonious and fitting! When one acts and takes delight in this way, natural harmony issues from oneself, and the music of joy, happiness, delight, and affection is thereby complete. This is how spirits and human beings are brought into harmony and the aspirations of all under Heaven brought into communication; this is how customs are transformed and the feelings of all under Heaven brought into balance. As for the ranks of dancers in their appointed positions and the sounding of bells and drums, these are merely sounds and outward forms. Can these alone be called music? Ah! Since the Way of ritual and music is thus rooted in speech and conduct, can the gentleman fail to investigate its foundations deeply? In general, the highest ritual requires no ceremonial yielding, yet all under Heaven is well governed; the highest music has no sound, yet all under Heaven is harmonious. Yet the rulers of this age cannot cultivate centrality and correctness and delight in peace and harmony, thereby setting an example for all under Heaven. Instead, they merely busy themselves with the superficial details of institutions and ceremonial forms, treating these as instruments for embellishing an appearance of Great Peace. What wonder, then, that their governance falls short of antiquity?

Second Session

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
論
賢主獨觀萬化之原
潘大賓
同考試官訓導黃批立論甚正而結處晃徐樂餘言之
非深為有見
同考試官教諭朱批以萬化之原歸之心最是
同考試官學正李批不雕琢浮詞而節節整齊有學之士也
考試官教諭張批開闔抑揚曲盡賢主獨觀之意
考試官教諭應批說原字明白可錄
===
天下無心外之治也善治天下者反求諸心而
已矣天下至大也然其理實具於一心一心雖
微也然其用實周乎天下故化行於天下雖萬
殊而原於吾心則至一圖治者自其萬殊而觀
之固紛乎其不齊而難乎其為力也自其一原
而觀之則一以貫之而又何疑焉自心學不明
於天下而世主往往忽之雖有雄才大略上嘉
下樂之志非不好安而惡危好治而惡亂也而
反就其所惡違其所好豈非鹵莽滅裂於本原
punctuated:
論
賢主獨觀萬化之原
潘大賓

同考試官訓導黃批：立論甚正，而結處晃徐樂餘言之非，深為有見。
同考試官教諭朱批：以萬化之原歸之心，最是。
同考試官學正李批：不雕琢浮詞，而節節整齊，有學之士也。
考試官教諭張批：開闔抑揚，曲盡賢主獨觀之意。
考試官教諭應批：說原字明白，可錄。

天下無心外之治也，善治天下者，反求諸心而已矣。天下至大也，然其理實具於一心；一心雖微也，然其用實周乎天下。故化行於天下雖萬殊，而原於吾心則至一。圖治者自其萬殊而觀之，固紛乎其不齊，而難乎其為力也；自其一原而觀之，則一以貫之，而又何疑焉？自心學不明於天下，而世主往往忽之。雖有雄才大略、上嘉下樂之志，非不好安而惡危、好治而惡亂也，而反就其所惡，違其所好，豈非鹵莽滅裂於本原
translation_en:
Discourse
“The Worthy Ruler Alone Discerns the Source of the Myriad Transformations”
Pan Dabin

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor: The argument is thoroughly sound, and the conclusion’s exposure of the errors in Xu Le’s remaining statements [?] shows considerable insight.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Locating the source of the myriad transformations in the mind is entirely correct.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: He does not embellish empty phrases; every section is orderly. He is a man of learning.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Through the argument’s opening and closing, restraint and emphasis, he fully develops every nuance of the worthy ruler’s unique discernment.
Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: He explains the word “source” clearly. Worthy of inclusion in the record.

There is no ordering of the realm apart from the mind. Those skilled in governing the realm simply turn back and seek within their own minds. The realm is exceedingly vast, yet its principles are fully contained within a single mind. Though a single mind is subtle, its functioning in fact extends throughout the realm. Thus, although the transformations unfolding throughout the realm differ in myriad ways, in their source within my mind they are utterly one. If those seeking good government view them in their myriad differences, they will indeed find them bewilderingly disparate and difficult to address. If they view them from their single source, however, one principle runs through them all: what uncertainty can remain?

Since the learning of the mind ceased to be clearly understood throughout the realm, rulers have often neglected it. Even when they possess outstanding abilities, grand strategies, and the aspiration that those above should approve and those below rejoice, it is not that they fail to love security and hate danger, or to love order and hate disorder. Yet they instead approach what they hate and depart from what they love. Is this not because they are careless and slipshod about the very source…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之地歟故求治於天下不若求治於吾心泛觀
於萬化不若約觀於一原大原既正大化自行
天下可以乂安長治而何有意外之虞耶漢徐
樂告武帝以安危之明要而曰賢主獨觀萬化
之原其亦有所見矣請論之夫天以天下畀之
君非徒以崇高富貴之也欲其代天而理物也
合四海九州之民而奉乎君亦非徒以奔走承
順之也欲其爲民而立命也父母君師之責皆
萃於人主之一身不可謂不重矣日有萬幾事
===
有萬變紛至而沓來嬰前而躡後政敎號令之
繁皆歸於人主之獨斷不可謂不煩矣然馭天
下之至博者必以至約制天下之至動者必以
至靜不觀萬化之原而何以爲治於天下乎人
主之於天下導之而欲其樂於善也禁之而欲
其戒於惡也紀綱法度禮樂刑賞之屬雖有萬
不同皆其所以化之之具耳然孰主張是孰綱
維是庸非人主之心乎人主所以制天下事者
固本乎一心而心之所以能應天下事者以具
punctuated:
之地歟？故求治於天下，不若求治於吾心；泛觀於萬化，不若約觀於一原。大原既正，大化自行，天下可以乂安長治，而何有意外之虞耶？漢徐樂告武帝以安危之明要，而曰：「賢主獨觀萬化之原。」其亦有所見矣。請論之。
夫天以天下畀之君，非徒以崇高富貴之也，欲其代天而理物也。合四海九州之民而奉乎君，亦非徒以奔走承順之也，欲其爲民而立命也。父母君師之責，皆萃於人主之一身，不可謂不重矣。日有萬幾，事有萬變，紛至而沓來，嬰前而躡後，政敎號令之繁，皆歸於人主之獨斷，不可謂不煩矣。然馭天下之至博者，必以至約；制天下之至動者，必以至靜。不觀萬化之原，而何以爲治於天下乎？人主之於天下，導之而欲其樂於善也，禁之而欲其戒於惡也。紀綱法度、禮樂刑賞之屬，雖有萬不同，皆其所以化之之具耳。然孰主張是？孰綱維是？庸非人主之心乎？人主所以制天下事者，固本乎一心，而心之所以能應天下事者，以具
translation_en:
…at the very foundation? Thus, seeking order in the realm is less effective than seeking order in one’s own mind; surveying the myriad transformations broadly is less effective than concentrating one’s gaze upon their single source. Once the great source is rectified, the great transformation proceeds of itself. The realm can enjoy peace and lasting order: what unforeseen danger could there be? Xu Le of the Han explained to Emperor Wu the essential principles of security and peril, saying: “The worthy ruler alone discerns the source of the myriad transformations.” He, too, had insight into this. Allow me to discuss it.
Heaven entrusts the realm to the ruler not merely to exalt him and enrich him, but so that he may act on Heaven’s behalf in bringing order to all things. The people of the Four Seas and Nine Provinces together serve the ruler not merely to hasten about obediently at his command, but so that he may secure their lives. The responsibilities of parent, sovereign, and teacher all converge upon the ruler’s single person; these cannot be called anything but weighty. Each day brings myriad matters requiring judgment, and affairs undergo myriad changes. They arrive in bewildering succession, entangling him in front and pressing upon him from behind. The profusion of government measures, moral instruction, orders, and commands all falls to the ruler’s sole decision; this cannot be called anything but burdensome. Yet to govern the utmost breadth of the realm requires the utmost simplicity; to control its utmost activity requires the utmost stillness. Without discerning the source of the myriad transformations, how could one bring order to the realm? In dealing with the realm, the ruler guides the people because he wishes them to delight in goodness, and restrains them because he wishes them to guard against evil. The principles of government, laws and standards, rites and music, punishments and rewards, though differing in myriad ways, are all merely instruments by which he transforms the people. Yet what directs these? What holds them together? Is it not the ruler’s mind? The ruler’s means of directing the affairs of the realm are indeed rooted in his single mind; and the mind can respond to the affairs of the realm because it contains…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乎衆理也方寸之小中涵太虛一腔之內畢備
萬物而謂非萬化之原乎然天理雖根於道心
而人欲未嘗不萌於人心苟吾一心之間理欲
並行眞妄錯雜而欲以化天下亦難矣故人主
之心正則天下之事無一不正人主之心不正
則天下之事無一不邪而危微精一之旨所以
丁寧於虞廷授受之間而爲萬世帝王之心法
也世之人主不察於是一心之微衆欲攻之聲
色珍奇馳驅游衍土木之華貨利之殖邊功方
===
技之張皇詭異紛然前陳皆得以入之而君心
荒矣荒則好大勤遠窮奢極欲而無所不至若
武帝是也本原旣失如治化何此民之所以不
安而大勢之所以易動也徐樂以賢主之事啓
之其意善矣然賢主所以觀萬化之原者蓋其
講學以明是心寡欲以養是心以禮而制是心
固皆所以用力於正本端原而爲應變神化之
地也至於燕閒蠖濩之時尸居淵默之地一念
之萌尤必謹而察之果天理也則敬以擴之而
punctuated:
乎衆理也。方寸之小，中涵太虛；一腔之內，畢備萬物，而謂非萬化之原乎？然天理雖根於道心，而人欲未嘗不萌於人心。苟吾一心之間，理欲並行，眞妄錯雜，而欲以化天下，亦難矣。故人主之心正，則天下之事無一不正；人主之心不正，則天下之事無一不邪。而危微精一之旨，所以丁寧於虞廷授受之間，而爲萬世帝王之心法也。世之人主不察於此，一心之微，衆欲攻之：聲色珍奇、馳驅游衍、土木之華、貨利之殖、邊功方技之張皇詭異，紛然前陳，皆得以入之，而君心荒矣。荒則好大勤遠，窮奢極欲，而無所不至，若武帝是也。本原旣失，如治化何？此民之所以不安，而大勢之所以易動也。
徐樂以賢主之事啓之，其意善矣。然賢主所以觀萬化之原者，蓋其講學以明是心，寡欲以養是心，以禮而制是心，固皆所以用力於正本端原，而爲應變神化之地也。至於燕閒蠖濩之時、尸居淵默之地，一念之萌，尤必謹而察之。果天理也，則敬以擴之，而
translation_en:
…because it contains the manifold principles. Small though the heart is, it embraces the Great Void; within its single chamber, all things are fully present. Can one say that it is not the source of all transformations? Yet although heavenly principle is rooted in the moral mind, human desires never cease to sprout in the human mind. If principle and desire operate side by side within my single heart, with truth and delusion intermingled, transforming the world will indeed be difficult. Thus, when the ruler’s heart is upright, nothing in the affairs of the realm is other than upright; when his heart is not upright, nothing in the affairs of the realm is other than deviant. This is why the teaching that the human mind is precarious and the moral mind subtle, and that one must be discerning and single-minded, was earnestly reiterated at the transmission of rule in Shun’s court, becoming the method of cultivating the heart for emperors and kings of all ages. Rulers who fail to perceive this leave their subtle hearts besieged by desires. Music and sensual pleasures, rarities and curiosities, riding and excursions, splendid buildings, the accumulation of wealth and profit, and the extravagant and bizarre pursuit of frontier achievements and occult arts crowd before them. All gain entry, and the ruler’s heart falls into neglect. Once this happens, he delights in grand undertakings and expends his energies on distant ventures, exhausting the possibilities of luxury and indulging desire to the utmost, stopping at nothing. Emperor Wu was such a ruler. Once the fundamental source has been lost, what can be done about governance and moral transformation? This is why the people are unsettled and the overall political situation is easily shaken.
Xu Le sought to enlighten him through the deeds of worthy rulers, and his intention was good. Yet the means by which a worthy ruler contemplates the source of all transformations are these: pursuing learning to illuminate this heart, reducing desires to nourish it, and regulating it through ritual propriety. All are efforts to rectify the root and set the source aright, establishing a foundation for responding to change and effecting wondrous transformation. Even during periods of quiet leisure and secluded repose [?], when he sits still in profound silence, he must be especially vigilant in examining the first stirring of a thought. If it truly accords with heavenly principle, he must reverently expand it, and…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不使其少有壅閼果人欲也則敬以克之而不
使其少有凝滯此非賢主獨致其决而他人何
所與力哉蓋至此而後道心純爲一身之主矣
然雖獨觀乎此而謹之尤不敢獨恃乎此而遂
已也於是盤有銘几有戒器有箴圖有規而在
輿位宁旅賁官師皆有規典而無地不寓其警
焉前有疑後有丞左納言右納史而侍御僕從
罔非正人以朝夕承弼而靡人不獻其忠焉皆
所以爲此心之防此理之輔而正萬化之本原
===
此其所以居靜制動守約施博措諸天下國家
無所處而不當化成雍煕泰和之盛亦由此而
可致而武帝何足以知之然樂非能爲是言也
殆先漢儒者之緒論而樂能援之以自售耳方
告以此且曰明於安危之機脩之廟堂之上而
銷未形之患似也而復蠱之以逐走獸射飛鳥
弘遊燕之囿淫縱恣之觀極馳騁之樂自若金
石絲竹之聲不絶於耳帷幄之私俳優侏儒之
笑不乏於前而天下無宿憂何哉繼勉之以天
punctuated:
不使其少有壅閼；果人欲也，則敬以克之，而不使其少有凝滯。此非賢主獨致其决，而他人何所與力哉？蓋至此而後，道心純爲一身之主矣。然雖獨觀乎此而謹之，尤不敢獨恃乎此而遂已也。於是盤有銘，几有戒，器有箴，圖有規；而在輿位宁，旅賁官師皆有規典，而無地不寓其警焉。前有疑，後有丞，左納言，右納史，而侍御僕從罔非正人，以朝夕承弼，而靡人不獻其忠焉。皆所以爲此心之防、此理之輔，而正萬化之本原。
此其所以居靜制動，守約施博，措諸天下國家，無所處而不當。化成雍煕泰和之盛，亦由此而可致，而武帝何足以知之？然樂非能爲是言也，殆先漢儒者之緒論，而樂能援之以自售耳。方告以此，且曰：「明於安危之機，脩之廟堂之上，而銷未形之患。」似也。而復蠱之以逐走獸、射飛鳥，弘遊燕之囿，淫縱恣之觀，極馳騁之樂，自若金石絲竹之聲不絶於耳，帷幄之私，俳優侏儒之笑不乏於前，而天下無宿憂，何哉？繼勉之以天
translation_en:
…and allow it not the slightest obstruction. If it is indeed human desire, he must reverently overcome it, allowing not the slightest lingering attachment. Unless the worthy ruler himself exercises his resolve in this, how can anyone else contribute? Only when this point has been reached does the moral mind become the sole master of his person. Yet although he examines this inwardly and attends to it carefully, he especially dares not rely on this alone and stop there. Thus his basin bears an inscription, his table an admonition, his utensils corrective maxims, and his pictures warnings. Whether he rides in his carriage or stands at court, his guards and officials all have prescribed rules for remonstrance, so that nowhere is he without a reminder to be vigilant. Before him stands a counselor, behind him an assistant; to his left is a transmitter of admonitions, and to his right a recorder [?]. His attendants and servants are all upright men, supporting and assisting him morning and evening, and each offers his loyal counsel. All these serve to guard this mind, assist this principle, and rectify the source of all transforming influence.
This is how he governs movement while remaining still, holds to essentials while extending their application widely, and applies them throughout the realm and the state, dealing appropriately with every situation. Through this, too, he can bring about the flourishing of concord, prosperity, and supreme harmony through moral transformation. But how could Emperor Wu have understood this? Yet Xu Le was not himself capable of originating such a statement. It was probably a surviving teaching of earlier Han Confucian scholars, which Le was able to invoke to advance himself. While advising the emperor in these terms, he also said: “Understand clearly the critical junctures of security and danger, attend to them in the court, and eliminate troubles before they take shape.” This seems sound. Yet he then enticed him with the prospect of chasing beasts and shooting birds, enlarging the parks for his outings and banquets, indulging to excess in unrestrained spectacles, and enjoying galloping about to the utmost; of continuing at ease with the sounds of bells, chimes, strings, and pipes never ceasing in his ears, and, in the privacy of his curtained chambers, the jests of entertainers and dwarfs never lacking before him—all while the realm remained free of lingering worries. Why was this? He next encouraged him to take as his concern all under Heaven…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
下爲務則湯文不難侔而成康之俗可復興亦
是也而復餌之以圖王不成其敝足以安安則
何求而不得何威而不成奚征而不服何哉夫
未有人主縱欲而能安且無憂者也樂之言不
我誣歟蓋其一出一入一捭一闔雅樂方陳而
淫哇卽繼無非詭遇以求合耳陋儒之希世取
寵一至於此此識者所以謂汲長孺內多欲而
外施仁義一語爲苦口之藥董仲舒正心以正
朝廷數言爲格心之論歟惜乎帝之不悟而徒
===
恨樂等相見之晩也
表
擬
賜大臣歷代名臣奏議謝表永樂十四年
舒素蘊
同考試官敎諭唐 批駢儷中寫出人臣對揚
休美之心宜錄
考試官敎諭張 批得體
考試官敎諭應 批四六過人可取
punctuated:
下爲務，則湯文不難侔，而成康之俗可復興，亦是也。而復餌之以圖王不成，其敝足以安，安則何求而不得，何威而不成，奚征而不服，何哉？夫未有人主縱欲而能安且無憂者也。樂之言不我誣歟？蓋其一出一入，一捭一闔，雅樂方陳，而淫哇卽繼，無非詭遇以求合耳。陋儒之希世取寵，一至於此！此識者所以謂汲長孺「內多欲而外施仁義」一語爲苦口之藥，董仲舒「正心以正朝廷」數言爲格心之論歟？惜乎帝之不悟，而徒恨樂等相見之晩也！
表
擬賜大臣《歷代名臣奏議》謝表，永樂十四年。
舒素蘊
同考試官敎諭唐，批：「駢儷中寫出人臣對揚休美之心，宜錄。」
考試官敎諭張，批：「得體。」
考試官敎諭應，批：「四六過人，可取。」
translation_en:
…to make the realm his concern, so that matching Tang and Wen would not be difficult, and the customs of the reigns of Cheng and Kang could flourish again: this, too, was right. Yet he then baited him with the claim that even if his pursuit of true kingship failed, its least successful outcome would suffice to secure peace; and once secure, what could he seek and not obtain, what display of might could fail, and whom could he campaign against without securing submission? Why say this? No ruler has ever indulged his desires and yet remained secure and free from care. Do Le’s words not deceive us? His arguments advance and retreat, open and close: no sooner is the stately music set forth than licentious tunes follow. All this is merely to seek favor by devious means. So far can a shallow scholar go in courting the age and winning favor! Is this why discerning men regard Ji Changru’s words, “Within, you have many desires, while outwardly you practice benevolence and righteousness,” as bitter medicine, and Dong Zhongshu’s few words, “Rectify your heart in order to rectify the court,” as an argument for rectifying the ruler’s heart? Alas, the emperor failed to understand and merely regretted having met Le and the others so late!

Memorial

Draft memorial of thanks for the bestowal upon high ministers of Memorials of Famous Ministers of Successive Dynasties (Lidai mingchen zouyi), set in the fourteenth year of Yongle [1416].

Shu Suyun

Associate Examiner Tang, an Instructor, comments: “Within its parallel prose, this conveys a minister’s heartfelt desire to acknowledge and extol imperial beneficence. It merits inclusion.”

Examiner Zhang, an Instructor, comments: “Appropriate to the form.”

Examiner Ying, an Instructor, comments: “Its four-and-six-character prose surpasses that of others. It merits selection.”

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
具官臣某等兹者伏蒙
聖恩賜臣等歷代名臣奏議各一部謹當表
謝者臣等誠懽誠忭稽首頓首伏以
錄言異代式彰求諫之
盛心
散帙
明庭茂對勸忠之
殊典義存交儆
仁出特
===
恩臣聞上古有治人無治法中古有遺政無遺
言粤稽名世之英迭展匡時之略謀王斷
國代不乏人陳善責難功存致主坐運而
折衝千里立談而成信終身啓心沃心就
事論事言有時而不用忠閱世而愈明尚
有典刑布在方冊受知
明主爰
命儒臣務精選以成書期多聞而建事集訐謨
於羣籍善之善者必收廣忠益於衆思醇
punctuated:
具官臣某等，兹者伏蒙聖恩，賜臣等《歷代名臣奏議》各一部，謹當表謝者。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首。伏以：錄言異代，式彰求諫之盛心；散帙明庭，茂對勸忠之殊典。義存交儆，仁出特恩。
臣聞上古有治人無治法，中古有遺政無遺言。粤稽名世之英，迭展匡時之略。謀王斷國，代不乏人；陳善責難，功存致主。坐運而折衝千里，立談而成信終身。啓心沃心，就事論事。言有時而不用，忠閱世而愈明。尚有典刑，布在方冊。受知明主，爰命儒臣，務精選以成書，期多聞而建事。集訐謨於羣籍，善之善者必收；廣忠益於衆思，醇
translation_en:
Your servants, so-and-so and others, holding their respective offices, have now humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious gift of one copy each of Memorials and Deliberations of Famous Ministers of Successive Dynasties (Lidai mingchen zouyi). We respectfully submit this memorial of thanks. With utmost joy and delight, we bow our heads to the ground and repeatedly kowtow. We humbly reflect: by recording the words of different dynasties, you manifest your exalted resolve to seek remonstrance; by distributing these volumes in your illustrious court, you magnificently bestow an exceptional favor encouraging loyalty. Its righteousness lies in mutual admonition; its benevolence issues in special grace.
Your servants have heard that high antiquity had men who brought order, but no fixed methods of government; middle antiquity left governmental achievements, but no transmitted words. Examining the outstanding men renowned in their ages, we find that each in turn displayed strategies for setting his times aright. No age lacked men who counseled kings and decided affairs of state. By presenting what was good and demanding difficult accomplishments, they rendered service in bringing their rulers to greatness. Seated at their ease, they devised plans that repelled enemies a thousand li away; in a brief conversation, they established trust that lasted a lifetime. They opened their rulers’ hearts and nourished their minds, addressing affairs as circumstances arose. Though their words sometimes went unheeded, their loyalty became ever clearer as generations passed. Their exemplary precedents remain, spread through written volumes. These men have won recognition from our enlightened sovereign, who accordingly commanded his Confucian ministers to make a careful selection and compile a book, intending that broad learning should lead to accomplishments in government. Gathering admonitory counsels [?] from many writings, they invariably included the best of the good; drawing upon many minds to enlarge the benefits of loyal counsel, the pure …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乎醇者悉采上關君德人鑑可徵下切事
情智囊不廢俟
聖敢期乎百世興邦或係乎一言寶鼎千年神
姦洞鑒靈龜五總休咎潜通結書局以告
成登
法宮而
進御蓋宇宙無窮之變舉不出於目前若古
今有異之宜當自得於言外海兼河潤隨
翕闢而有餘星受
===
日光賴
表章而不朽竊為
萃編而心幸俄驚
晉錫之躬逢用藥真方轉圜
深意無功上
答有愧中存欽惟
皇帝陛下
舜德罔愆賓四門之穆穆
啟賢能敬君萬國之元元
punctuated:
乎醇者悉采。上關君德，人鑑可徵；下切事情，智囊不廢。俟聖敢期乎百世，興邦或係乎一言。寶鼎千年，神姦洞鑒；靈龜五總，休咎潜通。結書局以告成，登法宮而進御。蓋宇宙無窮之變，舉不出於目前；若古今有異之宜，當自得於言外。海兼河潤，隨翕闢而有餘；星受日光，賴表章而不朽。竊為萃編而心幸，俄驚晉錫之躬逢。用藥真方，轉圜深意，無功上答，有愧中存。
欽惟皇帝陛下，舜德罔愆，賓四門之穆穆；啟賢能敬，君萬國之元元。
translation_en:
…all that is purest is gathered. Above, it concerns the ruler’s virtue, offering human precedents as mirrors for scrutiny; below, it closely addresses practical affairs, leaving no store of wisdom unused. We dare hope that it may await a sage even a hundred generations hence; the flourishing of a state may depend upon a single utterance. Like a treasured tripod enduring a thousand years, it clearly distinguishes spirits and malign beings; like a numinous tortoise encompassing the five [?], it affords hidden access to auspicious and inauspicious outcomes. The compilation office has concluded its work and announced completion; we ascend the imperial palace to present the work for Your Majesty’s inspection. The inexhaustible changes of the universe are thus all brought before your eyes; as for measures whose suitability differs between ancient and present times, their meaning must be grasped beyond the words. The sea receives the rivers’ bounty and has abundance to spare through every contraction and expansion; the stars receive the sun’s light and, through imperial recognition, attain immortality. Privately rejoicing in this compilation, I was suddenly astonished to find myself the recipient of your generous gifts. Here are genuine prescriptions for administering medicine and profound intentions of responding as readily as turning a circle. Having accomplished nothing with which to repay your favor, I harbor shame within.
Reverently considering Your Majesty the Emperor: possessing Shun’s virtue without fault, you receive guests at the four gates in solemn majesty; possessing Qi’s worthiness and capacity for reverence, you rule the common people of the myriad states…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
合日月以嚮明
整乾坤而立極
兩都並建雄鎮上游七佐叅謀弘開
內閣
皇武旣隆於厎定人文尤篤於化成
實惠潛孚厚栽培之命脉
虛衷未滿廓延攬之規模載輯舊聞藉前言
而
畜德繼
===
頒新命見下濟之
謙光鉅編崇琬琰之陳
大號仰絲綸之渙
蘭臺珎秘
玉版分香蔀屋輝煌牙籤增重非特傳之爲
寶蓋將
宣之使言惟古之遺直旣不忘則今之嘉言
罔攸伏暨
風聲於天下先
punctuated: 合日月以嚮明，整乾坤而立極。兩都並建，雄鎮上游；七佐叅謀，弘開內閣。皇武旣隆於厎定，人文尤篤於化成。實惠潛孚，厚栽培之命脉；虛衷未滿，廓延攬之規模。載輯舊聞，藉前言而畜德；繼頒新命，見下濟之謙光。鉅編崇琬琰之陳，大號仰絲綸之渙。蘭臺珎秘，玉版分香；蔀屋輝煌，牙籤增重。非特傳之爲寶，蓋將宣之使言。惟古之遺直旣不忘，則今之嘉言罔攸伏。暨風聲於天下，先
translation_en:
…You unite the sun and moon in turning toward the light, set Heaven and Earth in order, and establish the supreme standard. The two capitals stand together, powerfully guarding the upper reaches; seven counsellors participate in deliberations, greatly expanding the Grand Secretariat. Your imperial martial achievements have already reached their height in securing peace; your commitment to civilization is still more profound in transforming the people. Substantial benefits quietly inspire trust, nourishing the lifeblood of cultivation; your receptive heart remains unsatisfied, broadening the scope for attracting worthy men. You have now compiled accounts from the past, drawing upon earlier words to cultivate virtue; you have followed this by issuing a new command, displaying the radiance of humility that reaches down to those below.

The great compilation is displayed with the honor accorded precious jade; we look up to the grand proclamation as the imperial words flow forth. Treasures kept secret in the Orchid Terrace archives now share the fragrance of their jade tablets; humble, darkened dwellings shine, and ivory book labels acquire greater distinction. The purpose is not merely to transmit this work as a treasure, but to disseminate it so that people will speak. Since the upright men of antiquity who have passed away are not forgotten, the worthy words of the present will nowhere remain concealed. Your influence reaches throughout the realm, preceding…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
雨澤於
朝端豈知才劣位優自顧
恩深報淺腹心是寄偶血氣之未衰
元首克明何股肱之敢惰願為骨鯁誓勿面從
賢聖可希俛盡平生之學術忠良竝遂仰
酬
今日之
眷懷惟
聖心允執厥中俾臣等順之于外
===
兼聽必歸於獨斷
力行豈在乎多言
見諸事而深切著明
加之意而高明光大
廟謨恢遠永保不二心之臣
國勢尊安增光
大一統之業臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖歡忭感激之至謹稽首頓首奉
punctuated: 雨澤於朝端。豈知才劣位優，自顧恩深報淺。腹心是寄，偶血氣之未衰；元首克明，何股肱之敢惰？願為骨鯁，誓勿面從。賢聖可希，俛盡平生之學術；忠良竝遂，仰酬今日之眷懷。惟聖心允執厥中，俾臣等順之于外。兼聽必歸於獨斷，力行豈在乎多言？見諸事而深切著明，加之意而高明光大。廟謨恢遠，永保不二心之臣；國勢尊安，增光大一統之業。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、歡忭感激之至，謹稽首頓首奉……
translation_en:
…bestow rain-like beneficence upon the imperial court. Yet our abilities are meager and our positions exalted; reflecting upon ourselves, we see that the favor we have received is profound, while our repayment is slight. Entrusted as Your Majesty’s intimate confidants, we happen still to possess undiminished vigor. When the sovereign, as the head, is enlightened, how dare his ministers, as his limbs, be idle? We wish to serve as forthright remonstrants and vow never merely to assent to Your face. The worthies and sages may be emulated: we shall strive to apply all the learning we have acquired throughout our lives. May the loyal and worthy alike fulfill their aspirations, that we may repay the solicitude You show us today. May Your sagely mind truly hold fast to the Mean, enabling us, Your servants, to act in accordance with it in the world beyond.

Hearing all sides must ultimately lead to Your own decision; vigorous action surely does not depend upon plentiful words. Let it manifest itself in deeds, profound, pertinent, clear, and evident; devote Your attention to it, making it lofty, luminous, broad, and great. May the court’s counsels be far-reaching, forever retaining ministers of undivided loyalty; may the state’s standing be exalted and secure, adding glory to the enterprise of great unity. Gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your sagely person, we, Your servants, are overwhelmed with joy and gratitude. Reverently bowing low and knocking our heads upon the ground, we respectfully present…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策五道
第一問
潘大賓
同考試官訓導黃批周制之所以善唐制之所以失而我
國家制作之所以比隆成周而陋有唐於下風者歷歷言之無遺可見子之學識其大者
===
同考試官教諭朱批善揄揚
聖製之盛可錄
同考試官學正李批辭昌而正且其中善加可否有識
之士也
考試官教諭張批此作詳道其實可謂熟於典故矣
考試官教諭應批我
朝諸司職掌會典二書所以垂創演繹後先相輝蓋參之周官周禮而取衷焉唐六典不
足擬矣此策條析精覈其於經世之學將有槩於其中者乎
聖人之制作也有所以定一代之宏規有所以
punctuated:
表稱謝以聞。
第叁場，策五道。第一問，潘大賓。
同考試官訓導黃批：周制之所以善，唐制之所以失，而我國家制作之所以比隆成周而陋有唐於下風者，歷歷言之無遺，可見子之學識其大者。
同考試官教諭朱批：善揄揚聖製之盛，可錄。
同考試官學正李批：辭昌而正，且其中善加可否，有識之士也。
考試官教諭張批：此作詳道其實，可謂熟於典故矣。
考試官教諭應批：我朝諸司職掌、會典二書，所以垂創演繹，後先相輝，蓋參之周官、周禮而取衷焉，唐六典不足擬矣。此策條析精覈，其於經世之學，將有槩於其中者乎？
聖人之制作也，有所以定一代之宏規，有所以
translation_en:
…this memorial expressing thanks, for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third session: five policy questions. First question. Pan Dabin.
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor: “Why the Zhou institutions were good, why the Tang institutions failed, and why the institutions established by our dynasty rival the flourishing Zhou and leave the Tang inferior and far behind—all these you explain distinctly, omitting nothing. Here one can see the greater dimensions of your learning and discernment.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Skillfully extols the magnificence of the sagely institutions. Worth selecting.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “The language is ample and correct; moreover, the judgments of approval and disapproval within it are well made. He is a man of discernment.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “This composition explains the actual circumstances in detail. Its author may indeed be called thoroughly familiar with institutional precedents.”
Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: “Our dynasty’s two books, the Duties of the Various Offices (Zhusi zhizhang) and the Collected Statutes (Huidian), set down the foundations and elaborate upon them, the later and earlier works illuminating one another. They draw upon and compare the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) and the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), taking these as their standard. The Six Statutes of the Tang (Tang liudian) cannot compare. This policy essay analyzes matters systematically, with precision and rigor. Might its author possess within himself a grasp of the learning of statecraft?”
When sages establish institutions, there are means by which they fix the grand framework of a dynasty, and means by which…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
周一代之經制紀綱立於前而後一代之
宏規以定損益明於後而後一代之經制
以周定於前者必極其規模之大周於後
者必盡其節目之詳夫然後治具畢張成
憲罔愆而有以保重熈累洽於無疆也愚
生蓋嘗誦
聖祖之詒謀仰
先皇之繼志上稽成周下迨有唐而後知我
朝之獨盛矣請因明問而陳之三代而上法
===
制莫備於周其可攷者周官周禮而已成
王功成治定董正庶官使帥其屬以舉其
事故周官詳於戒飭之辭而略於分授之
職而金履祥以為周禮之經也周公總領
百揆弼成君德事為之制曲為之防故周
禮詳於六屬之事而未及乎公孤之任而
金履祥以為周官之傳也然周之所以善
者有關睢麟趾之意以行周官之法度考
之二書時巡歲見之有異六服九服之不
punctuated:
周一代之經制。紀綱立於前，而後一代之宏規以定；損益明於後，而後一代之經制以周。定於前者，必極其規模之大；周於後者，必盡其節目之詳。夫然後治具畢張，成憲罔愆，而有以保重熈累洽於無疆也。愚生蓋嘗誦聖祖之詒謀，仰先皇之繼志，上稽成周，下迨有唐，而後知我朝之獨盛矣。請因明問而陳之。
三代而上，法制莫備於周，其可攷者，《周官》《周禮》而已。成王功成治定，董正庶官，使帥其屬以舉其事，故《周官》詳於戒飭之辭，而略於分授之職，而金履祥以為《周禮》之經也。周公總領百揆，弼成君德，事為之制，曲為之防，故《周禮》詳於六屬之事，而未及乎公孤之任，而金履祥以為《周官》之傳也。然周之所以善者，有《關睢》《麟趾》之意，以行《周官》之法度。考之二書，時巡歲見之有異，六服九服之不
translation_en:
…to complete the institutional arrangements of an age. Only once the governing framework has been established at the outset can the grand design of an age be fixed; only once subsequent modifications have been clarified can its institutional arrangements be made complete. What is fixed at the outset must encompass the full breadth of the design; what is completed afterward must exhaust the detail of its provisions. Only then can all the instruments of government be deployed and the established statutes observed without deviation, thereby preserving successive ages of flourishing peace forever. This humble student has recited the plans bequeathed by the Sagely Progenitor and looked up with reverence to the late emperor’s continuation of his purposes. I have investigated the flourishing Zhou above and traced developments down to the Tang, and only then understood the incomparable greatness of our dynasty. Allow me to set this forth in response to your illuminating question.
Among the Three Dynasties and earlier ages, no legal and institutional system was more complete than that of Zhou. The surviving texts through which it can be examined are the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) and the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli). Once King Cheng’s achievements were accomplished and orderly government established, he supervised and regulated the officials, directing them to lead their subordinates in carrying out their duties. Thus the Offices of Zhou is detailed in its admonitions but brief concerning the duties assigned to particular offices. Jin Lüxiang therefore regarded it as the foundational text for the Rites of Zhou. The Duke of Zhou oversaw all affairs of government and assisted in perfecting the ruler’s virtue, establishing regulations for every matter and safeguards for every particular. Thus the Rites of Zhou is detailed concerning the business of the six departmental groupings but does not address the responsibilities of the Three Dukes and Three Junior Guardians. Jin Lüxiang therefore regarded it as a commentary on the Offices of Zhou. Yet what made Zhou’s government good was that it implemented the regulations of the Offices of Zhou in the spirit of “The Ospreys Cry” (Guanju; transcribed here as 關睢 [?]) and “The Qilin’s Hooves” (Linzhi). Examining these two books, we find differences concerning periodic royal inspection tours and annual audiences, and a discrepancy between the six and nine zones of service…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同不過小有損益而何足深疑哉三代而
下法制莫踰於唐其可攷者六典會要而
已六典成於開元盛時而經畫措置最有
法度精密簡要猶有古意故曾鞏以爲得
建官制理之方會要續編於蘇冕崔鉉而
代德以後治少亂多郊禋朝儀食貨苛取
故林駉以爲雖備而無取然唐之所以陋
者大綱不正而萬目徒舉考之六典定於
玄宗而註於李林甫蓋已兆亂階而其餘
===
不足觀也已嗚呼周治隆矣而周禮非全
書唐書備矣而治功無可述若之何其不
獨盛於我
朝乎洪惟
太祖高皇帝以天錫智勇復帝王之中又以天
縱多能恢邦國之遠猷諸司職掌書成於
宸斷見出於
淵衷經綸周至輕重同得自今觀之革丞相以
防專恣陞六部以分事權所以正百官也
punctuated:
同，不過小有損益，而何足深疑哉？三代而下，法制莫踰於唐，其可攷者《六典》《會要》而已。《六典》成於開元盛時，而經畫措置最有法度，精密簡要，猶有古意，故曾鞏以爲得建官制理之方。《會要》續編於蘇冕、崔鉉，而代德以後，治少亂多，郊禋朝儀，食貨苛取，故林駉以爲雖備而無取。然唐之所以陋者，大綱不正而萬目徒舉。考之，《六典》定於玄宗而註於李林甫，蓋已兆亂階，而其餘不足觀也已。
嗚呼！周治隆矣，而《周禮》非全書；唐書備矣，而治功無可述。若之何其不獨盛於我朝乎？洪惟太祖高皇帝以天錫智勇，復帝王之中，又以天縱多能，恢邦國之遠猷。《諸司職掌》書成於宸斷，見出於淵衷，經綸周至，輕重同得。自今觀之，革丞相以防專恣，陞六部以分事權，所以正百官也。
translation_en:
…differ, these are merely minor reductions and additions: why should they give rise to profound doubts? Since the Three Dynasties, no legal and institutional system has surpassed that of the Tang. The sources available for examining it are simply the Six Statutes (Liudian) and the Collected Essentials (Huiyao). The Six Statutes was completed during the flourishing Kaiyuan era. Its planning and arrangements were exceptionally orderly, precise, concise, and essential, still retaining the spirit of antiquity. Thus Zeng Gong considered it to have grasped the proper method of establishing offices and ordering government. The Collected Essentials was compiled and continued by Su Mian and Cui Xuan. Yet from the reigns of Daizong and Dezong onward, periods of order were few and periods of disorder many; suburban sacrifices and court ceremonies, food and monetary matters, and harsh exactions [?]. Thus Lin Jiong judged that, although comprehensive, it offered nothing worth adopting. The Tang’s failing, however, was that its fundamental framework was unsound, so that its myriad detailed provisions were implemented in vain. Upon examination, the Six Statutes was finalized under Xuanzong and annotated by Li Linfu: already this foreshadowed the steps leading to disorder. The rest scarcely merits consideration.
Alas! The Zhou attained great heights of government, yet the Rites of Zhou is not a complete book. The Tang writings are comprehensive, yet their achievements in government offer nothing worthy of recounting. How, then, could such excellence fail to belong uniquely to our dynasty? We reverently reflect that Emperor Taizu Gao, with Heaven-bestowed wisdom and courage, restored the central ideal of the ancient emperors and kings [?]; with his Heaven-given versatility, he also expanded the far-reaching plans of the realm. The Duties of the Various Offices (Zhusi Zhizhang) was completed through his imperial decisions, its insights issuing from his profound mind. Its ordering of affairs was comprehensive and thorough, giving due weight to matters both great and small. Viewed from the present, abolishing the office of Chief Councilor to prevent arbitrary domination, and elevating the Six Ministries to divide administrative authority, were the means by which he set the official establishment in order.

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
農桑有定賦而繼以救荒上供有定額而
裁其經費所以優兆民也羣祀革不經之
號五禮弘復古之規所以治神人也府部
有相維之勢將士皆世業之家所以統六
師也律有畫一之法刑有讞審之詳所以
詰姦慝也工役有一定之員關津無加稅
之擾所以居四民也又立都察院以執法
通政司以納言大理寺以平獄舉百司之
事而括於九卿舉九卿之事而歸之
===
朝廷其與周官不同者司徒之教併於禮部
司空之職分為戶工至其簡明詳悉以立
一代之宏規者蓋未始有異也
先皇繼志載脩會典
今上參校而頒行之豈能有加於職掌之外哉
蓋自百餘年來率遵舊典或繁簡異宜不
能無離合或輕重異勢不能無變遷或草
創有待於後人或事力稍寬於前代其大
者若翰林重
punctuated:
農桑有定賦，而繼以救荒；上供有定額，而裁其經費，所以優兆民也。羣祀革不經之號，五禮弘復古之規，所以治神人也。府部有相維之勢，將士皆世業之家，所以統六師也。律有畫一之法，刑有讞審之詳，所以詰姦慝也。工役有一定之員，關津無加稅之擾，所以居四民也。又立都察院以執法，通政司以納言，大理寺以平獄。舉百司之事而括於九卿，舉九卿之事而歸之朝廷。其與《周官》不同者，司徒之教併於禮部，司空之職分為戶、工。至其簡明詳悉，以立一代之宏規者，蓋未始有異也。
先皇繼志，載脩《會典》；今上參校而頒行之，豈能有加於《職掌》之外哉？蓋自百餘年來，率遵舊典，或繁簡異宜，不能無離合；或輕重異勢，不能無變遷；或草創有待於後人，或事力稍寬於前代。其大者，若翰林重
translation_en:
…Agriculture and sericulture had fixed levies, supplemented by famine relief; supplies offered to the throne had fixed quotas, and expenditure was curtailed: these were the means of caring for the common people. Titles lacking canonical warrant were abolished from the various sacrifices, and the Five Rites extended the rules for restoring ancient practices: these were the means of ordering relations with spirits and people. The military commissions and ministries were positioned to check and support one another, and commanders and soldiers all came from households with hereditary service obligations: these were the means of commanding the six armies. The statutes provided uniform rules, and criminal cases received detailed judicial review: these were the means of investigating wickedness. Labor services had a fixed complement of workers, and customs barriers and ferries imposed no burdensome additional taxes: these were the means of keeping the four classes of the people settled in their occupations. The Censorate was also established to enforce the law, the Office of Transmission to receive communications, and the Court of Judicial Review to ensure fairness in criminal cases. The affairs of all offices were brought together under the Nine Ministers, and those of the Nine Ministers were referred to the imperial court. Where this differed from the Offices of Zhou, the educational duties of the Minister of Education were incorporated into the Ministry of Rites, and the duties of the Minister of Works were divided between the Ministries of Revenue and Works. Yet in its clarity, simplicity, and thoroughness, establishing a grand framework for an entire dynasty, it was never different.
The late emperor carried forward this intention and undertook the compilation of the Collected Statutes (Huidian); the present emperor compared and checked it, then promulgated it. Could it possibly add anything beyond the Duties of the Various Offices (Zhizhang)? For over a hundred years, the old regulations had generally been followed. Yet differing needs for complexity or simplicity inevitably required some separation or consolidation; changing circumstances affecting relative importance inevitably required alterations. Some matters left provisional at the founding awaited later generations; in others, resources for carrying out affairs were somewhat more ample than before. Among the major instances was the Hanlin Academy’s emphasis on…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
內閣之選六科崇七品之階設詹事府以領
坊局之官削回回監以專欽天之職
親藩之禄或隆或殺問刑之條或减或增皆
不可以莫之紀也故揭之以官職制度而
大綱正焉麗之以事物名數儀文等級而
萬目張焉然一以職掌爲主而類以頒降
羣書也附以歷年事例也其與職掌小異
者不過補偏救弊裒多益寡一事之軒輊
一時之彌縫至其奉若欽承以周
一代之經制者乃所以爲大同也我
祖宗良法美意昭垂於百年之前大烈耿光覲
揚於百年之後
聖子神孫佩服而無斁洪基昌祚安固而不搖
其本皆在是矣是豈末世所可彷佛而亦
豈容愚生之名言哉然治久而弊生有大
而孽萌謹持盈守成之道而不忘思患預
防之心端有望於
今日敢以是爲芹曝之
punctuated: 內閣之選，六科崇七品之階，設詹事府以領坊局之官，削回回監以專欽天之職，親藩之禄或隆或殺，問刑之條或减或增，皆不可以莫之紀也。故揭之以官職制度，而大綱正焉；麗之以事物名數、儀文等級，而萬目張焉。然一以職掌爲主，而類以頒降羣書也，附以歷年事例也。其與職掌小異者，不過補偏救弊、裒多益寡，一事之軒輊，一時之彌縫。至其奉若欽承，以周一代之經制者，乃所以爲大同也。我祖宗良法美意，昭垂於百年之前；大烈耿光，覲揚於百年之後。聖子神孫佩服而無斁，洪基昌祚安固而不搖，其本皆在是矣。是豈末世所可彷佛，而亦豈容愚生之名言哉？然治久而弊生，有大而孽萌。謹持盈守成之道，而不忘思患預防之心，端有望於今日。敢以是爲芹曝之
translation_en:
…selection for the Grand Secretariat; the elevation of the Six Offices of Scrutiny to the seventh rank; the establishment of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent to oversee the officials of its secretariats and bureaus; and the abolition of the Muslim Astronomical Office to concentrate astronomical duties in the Directorate of Astronomy. The stipends of imperial princes have sometimes been increased and sometimes reduced, and provisions governing criminal adjudication have sometimes been reduced and sometimes augmented. None of these changes could be left unrecorded. Thus, by setting out official posts and institutional arrangements, the work puts its main framework in order; by attaching the names and numbers of things and affairs, ceremonial forms, and distinctions of rank, it lays out the myriad particulars. Yet throughout it takes the Duties of Offices as its basis, arranging the various imperially promulgated works by category and appending precedents from successive years. Its minor differences from the Duties of Offices amount merely to correcting imbalances and remedying abuses, reducing excess and supplementing deficiency—adjustments in particular matters and temporary repairs. In reverently following and respectfully upholding established practice so as to encompass the governing institutions of the dynasty, however, it remains fundamentally the same.

The excellent laws and beneficent intentions of our imperial ancestors were luminously handed down a hundred years ago; their great achievements and brilliant glory are reverently celebrated a hundred years later. Their sagely sons and divine grandsons cherish and observe them without weariness, and the dynasty’s grand foundations and flourishing fortunes remain secure and unshaken. The basis of all this lies here. How could a declining age even approximate it, and how could an ignorant scholar such as I adequately describe it? Yet prolonged good government gives rise to abuses, and possession of a great realm allows seeds of disorder to sprout. Carefully to follow the way of preserving fullness and maintaining inherited achievements, while never forgetting to anticipate troubles and guard against them—this is precisely what I hope for today. I venture to present these words as my humble offering of celery and the sun’s warmth…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
獻可乎
第二問
汪有執
同考試官教諭蔡批詳言古今賞罰公私之異末復歸之
務學正心知本之論也
考試官教諭張批以至公至正立說最為切當
考試官教諭應批敷答詳明援引曲當敬羨敬羨
人君能秉天下之至公行天下之至正斯
可以運天下之大柄矣天下之善非慶賞
===
無以勸天下之惡非刑罰無以威二者人
君之大柄不可失也天下之心非至公無
以服天下之理非至正無由行二者人君
所以操柄尤不可失也故公正不忒者純
王之心刑賞得宜者純王之政執此以稽
此帝王所以得而後世所以失也愚嘗攷
之詩書矣臯陶言五服五章五刑五用商
頌言不僭不濫不敢怠遑其所以必歸之
天命者天之視聽在民天降災祥在德一
punctuated:
獻，可乎？

第二問
汪有執

同考試官教諭蔡批：詳言古今賞罰公私之異，末復歸之務學正心，知本之論也。
考試官教諭張批：以至公至正立說，最為切當。
考試官教諭應批：敷答詳明，援引曲當，敬羨！敬羨！

人君能秉天下之至公，行天下之至正，斯可以運天下之大柄矣。天下之善，非慶賞無以勸；天下之惡，非刑罰無以威。二者，人君之大柄，不可失也。天下之心，非至公無以服；天下之理，非至正無由行。二者，人君所以操柄，尤不可失也。故公正不忒者，純王之心；刑賞得宜者，純王之政。執此以稽此，帝王所以得而後世所以失也。愚嘗攷之《詩》《書》矣。臯陶言「五服五章，五刑五用」，《商頌》言「不僭不濫，不敢怠遑」。其所以必歸之天命者，天之視聽在民，天降災祥在德，一
translation_en:
…may I present it?

Second Question
Wang Youzhi

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: He explains in detail the differences between impartiality and private interest in rewards and punishments, past and present. At the end he returns to diligent learning and rectifying the mind: an argument that grasps the root of the matter.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: He grounds his argument in utmost impartiality and utmost rectitude. This is especially apt.
Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: The response is detailed and clear, and its citations are appropriate in every particular. Admirable! Admirable!

Only when the ruler can uphold the utmost impartiality in the realm and practice the utmost rectitude can he wield the realm’s great levers of authority. Goodness throughout the realm cannot be encouraged without honors and rewards; evil throughout the realm cannot be deterred without penalties and punishments. These two are the ruler’s great levers of authority and must not be lost. The hearts of all under Heaven cannot be won over without utmost impartiality; the principles governing all under Heaven cannot be put into practice without utmost rectitude. These two are the means by which the ruler controls those levers, and still less may they be lost. Thus, unfailing impartiality and rectitude constitute the mind of a true sage king; appropriately administered punishments and rewards constitute his government. Applying these standards in examining the matter reveals why the ancient emperors and kings succeeded and why later ages failed.

I have examined this in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents. Gao Yao speaks of “the five robes with their five insignia” and “the five punishments with their five applications.” The Hymns of Shang speak of “neither excessive rewards nor indiscriminate punishments” and of “not daring to be idle or take one’s ease.” The reason these invariably refer the matter back to Heaven’s mandate is that Heaven sees and hears through the people, and Heaven’s sending of calamities and auspicious signs depends on virtue—solely …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
公正而已君不法天將何所法君不畏天
將何所畏蓋不特詩書云爾也在易亦然
遏惡揚善順天休命著於大有之象者非
耶又嘗攷之周禮矣八則治都鄙實具刑
賞之條八柄馭羣臣莫非威福之政其所
以必掌之天官者總百官之殿最司四海
之鈞衡亦一公正而已不徇己欲以起愛
憎之端不惑人言以亂是非之實蓋不特
周禮為爾也在舜已然格則庸之否則威
===
之命之百揆之禹者非耶齊威王排左右
之議封即墨而烹阿大夫蓋庶幾其正矣
愚以為正者必如孟子告齊宣之言審之
於眾論而歸之於獨斷也左右之烹僅用
其一言然猶能折姦宄而立數十年之霸
業則夫純乎正者當何如也漢高帝待項
羽之臣斬丁公而官季布蓋庶幾其公矣
愚以公者必如左氏所記周人之言好惡
無容心而刑賞無貳命也季布之購未免
punctuated:
公正而已。君不法天，將何所法？君不畏天，將何所畏？蓋不特詩書云爾也，在易亦然。「遏惡揚善，順天休命」，著於大有之象者，非耶？又嘗攷之周禮矣。八則治都鄙，實具刑賞之條；八柄馭羣臣，莫非威福之政。其所以必掌之天官者，總百官之殿最，司四海之鈞衡，亦一公正而已。不徇己欲以起愛憎之端，不惑人言以亂是非之實。蓋不特周禮為爾也，在舜已然。「格則庸之，否則威之」，命之百揆之禹者，非耶？
齊威王排左右之議，封即墨而烹阿大夫，蓋庶幾其正矣。愚以為正者，必如孟子告齊宣之言，審之於眾論而歸之於獨斷也。左右之烹，僅用其一言，然猶能折姦宄而立數十年之霸業，則夫純乎正者，當何如也？漢高帝待項羽之臣，斬丁公而官季布，蓋庶幾其公矣。愚以公者，必如左氏所記周人之言，好惡無容心而刑賞無貳命也。季布之購，未免
translation_en:
…impartiality and rectitude alone. If the ruler does not take Heaven as his model, what shall he take as his model? If the ruler does not stand in awe of Heaven, what shall he stand in awe of? This is not stated only in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents; it is also so in the Book of Changes. Is this not what is set forth in the Image commentary on the hexagram Great Possession: “Restrain evil and promote good, complying with Heaven’s glorious mandate”? I have also examined the Rites of Zhou. Its eight regulations for governing the domains and settlements contain provisions for punishments and rewards; its eight powers for controlling the assembled ministers all concern the exercise of punitive and beneficent authority. These powers must be held by the Ministry of State because it assesses the relative merits of all officials and holds the balance for all within the four seas: here too, the sole principle is impartiality and rectitude. One must not indulge personal desires and thereby give rise to partial loves and hatreds, nor be misled by others’ words and thereby confuse the truth of right and wrong. This was not so only in the Rites of Zhou; it was already so under Shun.
