Was it not to Yu, as chief of the hundred officials, that he gave the command: “Those who conform, employ; those who do not, awe with punishment”?
King Wei of Qi rejected the opinions of his attendants, enfeoffed the official of Jimo, and boiled the grand master of E to death. He thus came close to rectitude. In my humble view, rectitude must accord with what Mencius told King Xuan of Qi: investigate the opinions of the many, but reserve the final judgment to oneself. In boiling his attendants to death, King Wei applied only one of those statements [?]. Yet he was still able to crush evildoers and establish a hegemony lasting several decades. What, then, might a ruler of unalloyed rectitude achieve? Emperor Gao of Han, in his treatment of Xiang Yu’s ministers, executed Ding Gong but appointed Ji Bu to office. He thus came close to impartiality. In my humble view, impartiality must accord with the words of the men of Zhou recorded in Zuo’s Commentary: allow no private bias into one’s likes and dislikes, and issue no contradictory commands concerning punishments and rewards. Yet the bounty offered for Ji Bu could not escape…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於貳命然尚能聲大義而勵四百載之人
心則夫純乎公者又當何如也漢宣帝所
以致中興之隆者其言曰有功不賞有罪
不誅唐虞不能化天下可不謂知言乎然
趙蓋韓楊何罪而誅許史弘石何功而用
褒霍光之忠而赤族之誅不少貸知王成
之偽而賜爵之命不可回此無他綜核之
過必反眩勵精之銳多不終無怪其偏私
矣唐太宗所以造太平之業者其言曰有
===
功則賞有罪則刑孰敢不盡心力可不謂
善言乎然君羨以讖言而戮無忌以外戚
而封蘇威被責終寛誤國之誅魏徵被褒
或致退朝之怒此無他英武非忠厚之資
仁義非久假之物又無怪其偏私矣由是
觀之帝王所以柄得其用者公正為之本
也後世所以治失其柄者偏私為之累也
蓋確乎其不可易矣而執事猶致疑於臯
陶之論謂其不能無少偏於輕重之間蓋
punctuated: 於貳命，然尚能聲大義而勵四百載之人心，則夫純乎公者又當何如也？漢宣帝所以致中興之隆者，其言曰：「有功不賞，有罪不誅，唐虞不能化天下。」可不謂知言乎？然趙蓋韓楊何罪而誅？許史弘石何功而用？褒霍光之忠，而赤族之誅不少貸；知王成之偽，而賜爵之命不可回。此無他，綜核之過必反眩，勵精之銳多不終，無怪其偏私矣。唐太宗所以造太平之業者，其言曰：「有功則賞，有罪則刑，孰敢不盡心力？」可不謂善言乎？然君羨以讖言而戮，無忌以外戚而封；蘇威被責，終寛誤國之誅；魏徵被褒，或致退朝之怒。此無他，英武非忠厚之資，仁義非久假之物，又無怪其偏私矣。由是觀之，帝王所以柄得其用者，公正為之本也；後世所以治失其柄者，偏私為之累也。蓋確乎其不可易矣。而執事猶致疑於臯陶之論，謂其不能無少偏於輕重之間，蓋
translation_en: …issuing contradictory orders. Yet he could still proclaim the great principle of righteousness and inspire people’s hearts for four hundred years. What, then, might one who was wholly impartial accomplish? Emperor Xuan of Han, who brought about a flourishing restoration, said: “If meritorious service goes unrewarded and crimes go unpunished, even the rulers of Tang and Yu could not transform the realm.” Can he not be said to have understood these words? Yet what crimes had Zhao, Gai, Han, and Yang committed that they were executed? What merit had Xu, Shi, Hong, and Shi earned that they were employed? He praised Huo Guang’s loyalty, yet allowed not the slightest mitigation of the punishment that exterminated his clan; he knew Wang Cheng’s deceit, yet would not revoke the order granting him noble rank. There was no other cause: excessive scrutiny inevitably produces confusion instead, and the keen resolve to devote oneself to government often fails to endure. No wonder he was partial and self-serving. Emperor Taizong of Tang, who established an age of great peace, said: “Reward those who have merit and punish those who have committed crimes: who would dare not devote his whole heart and strength?” Can these not be called fine words? Yet Junxian was executed because of a prophecy, while Wuji was enfeoffed because he was an imperial relative by marriage. Su Wei was censured, yet ultimately spared execution for harming the state; Wei Zheng was praised, yet sometimes provoked the emperor’s anger upon leaving court. There was no other cause: martial prowess is not the disposition of loyalty and generosity, and benevolence and righteousness are not things that can long be borrowed as a guise. Again, no wonder he was partial and self-serving. Viewed in this light, impartiality and rectitude were the foundation that enabled the ancient emperors and kings to wield their powers effectively; partiality and selfishness were the encumbrances that caused later rulers to lose their grasp of the powers of government. Surely this is an incontrovertible principle. Yet you still express doubts about Gao Yao’s argument, saying that it cannot avoid some bias in weighing lighter and heavier penalties. For…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
喜而賞者聖人之所欲怒而刑者聖人之
所惡功罪或有疑似而屈法以伸恩大舜
好生之德也後世若箝勒鞭箠之弛青朱
金紫之濫是則偏之為禍而豈古人之所
謂疑哉執事又疑八柄之目謂其不能不
容私於恩幸之間蓋爵祿者當然之報予
者特厚之恩羣臣或有超異而優賞以示
勸周官鼓舞之機也後世若登少艾於司
馬寵胡兒於宮中是則私之為禍而豈古
人之所謂幸哉嗚呼古昔盛時德化為先
刑賞次之雖極天下之公正而於變時雍
不專待此故曰不賞而民勸畫象而民不
犯後世以法制治天下未嘗不以此為先
務也而又往往狥於偏私而失之然則德
之不脩而徒法果不能以自行乎執事欲
有言以為
當宁之獻亦曰
明君以務學為急
punctuated: 喜而賞者，聖人之所欲；怒而刑者，聖人之所惡。功罪或有疑似，而屈法以伸恩，大舜好生之德也。後世若箝勒鞭箠之弛，青朱金紫之濫，是則偏之為禍，而豈古人之所謂疑哉？執事又疑八柄之目，謂其不能不容私於恩幸之間。蓋爵祿者，當然之報；予者，特厚之恩。羣臣或有超異，而優賞以示勸，周官鼓舞之機也。後世若登少艾於司馬，寵胡兒於宮中，是則私之為禍，而豈古人之所謂幸哉？嗚呼！古昔盛時，德化為先，刑賞次之。雖極天下之公正，而於變時雍，不專待此。故曰：「不賞而民勸，畫象而民不犯。」後世以法制治天下，未嘗不以此為先務也，而又往往狥於偏私而失之。然則德之不脩，而徒法果不能以自行乎？執事欲有言以為當宁之獻，亦曰：「明君以務學為急，
translation_en:
…to reward with joy is what the sage desires; to punish in anger is what the sage dislikes. When merit or guilt is uncertain, bending the law to extend kindness exemplifies the great Shun’s virtue of cherishing life. In later ages, however, the loosening of restraints and whippings, and the indiscriminate bestowal of blue and vermilion robes, gold seals and purple ribbons, were calamities caused by partiality. How could these be what the ancients meant by cases of doubt?

You also question the categories of the eight instruments of authority, suggesting that they inevitably leave room for private favoritism in the granting of kindness and favor. Rank and emoluments are recompense properly due; gifts are an especially generous kindness. When ministers display exceptional qualities, rewarding them lavishly to encourage others is the means of inspiration described in the Offices of Zhou. In later ages, however, elevating handsome youths to the office of Minister of War and favoring a non-Han lad within the palace were calamities caused by private favoritism. How could these be what the ancients meant by favor?

Alas! In the flourishing ages of antiquity, transformation through virtue came first, and punishments and rewards second. Even when punishments and rewards attained the utmost impartiality throughout the realm, the people’s transformation into harmony did not depend upon these alone. Thus it is said: “Without rewards, the people were encouraged; with only pictorial representations of punishments, the people committed no offenses.” In later ages, rulers governed the realm through laws and regulations, invariably making these their foremost concern. Yet they repeatedly yielded to partiality and private favoritism and thereby went astray. If virtue is left uncultivated, then, is it indeed true that laws alone cannot put themselves into effect? If you wish to offer words of counsel to the reigning sovereign, say simply: “An enlightened ruler takes diligent learning as his most urgent task…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
大學以正心爲要
第三問
周孚先
同考試官教諭林批以經權爲
建儲之法而歸之於豫忠愛之意溢於言表
考試官教諭張批觀子此策可謂先天下之憂而憂者矣
考試官教諭應批答無遺而中有區處非徒以演問目也
建天下之大本者必以豫濟天下之常經
者必以權建儲天下之大本也與子天下
===
之常經也根本久虛則天下之大計不可
忽經常或變則天下之大慮不可忘天下
雖有難處之事古人亦有善處之方亦惟
定之豫而已矣濟之權而已矣執事惓惓
忠愛之心發於策問而及
社稷之大計愚生不敏何足以知之然嫠不恤
緯而憂王室其敢不述所懷以復明問之
萬一乎夫卜世歷年之遠者莫如三代貽
謀燕翼之善者亦莫如三代蓋經權竝用
punctuated:
大學以正心爲要。

第三問
周孚先

同考試官教諭林批：以經權爲建儲之法，而歸之於豫，忠愛之意溢於言表。
考試官教諭張批：觀子此策，可謂先天下之憂而憂者矣。
考試官教諭應批：答無遺，而中有區處，非徒以演問目也。

建天下之大本者，必以豫；濟天下之常經者，必以權。建儲，天下之大本也；與子，天下之常經也。根本久虛，則天下之大計不可忽；經常或變，則天下之大慮不可忘。天下雖有難處之事，古人亦有善處之方，亦惟定之豫而已矣，濟之權而已矣。執事惓惓忠愛之心發於策問，而及社稷之大計。愚生不敏，何足以知之？然嫠不恤緯而憂王室，其敢不述所懷，以復明問之萬一乎？夫卜世歷年之遠者，莫如三代；貽謀燕翼之善者，亦莫如三代。蓋經權竝用
translation_en:
…The Great Learning takes rectifying the heart as essential.

Third Policy Question
Zhou Fuxian

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: He takes constant principles and discretionary judgment as the means of establishing an heir apparent, and makes advance preparation their ultimate basis. His loyal devotion is evident beyond the words themselves.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Reading this policy essay of yours, one may indeed call you someone who worries before all others under Heaven worry.

Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: The answer omits nothing and offers considered solutions throughout; it does more than merely elaborate on the topics in the question.

To establish the great foundation of the realm, one must prepare in advance; to sustain the realm’s enduring principles, one must exercise discretionary judgment. Establishing an heir apparent is the great foundation of the realm; transmitting the throne to one’s son is its enduring principle. When the foundation remains vacant for long, the realm’s great affairs cannot be neglected; when established norms undergo change, the realm’s grave concerns cannot be forgotten. Though there are matters in the world that are difficult to handle, the ancients also had ways of handling them well: simply to settle them through advance preparation and manage them through discretionary judgment.

Your earnest loyal devotion finds expression in this policy question and extends to the great affairs of the state. Dull-witted as this humble student is, how could I understand them adequately? Yet even a widow worries about the royal house rather than the weft of her weaving. How, then, could I dare refrain from setting forth what is in my heart, to answer even a small part of your discerning question?

For the long span of generations and years allotted to their rule, none equaled the Three Dynasties; for the excellence of their plans bequeathed to their descendants to secure their well-being, none equaled the Three Dynasties either. For they employed constant principles and discretionary judgment together…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而豫則行乎其間故論治者必以三代為
法程也自其經而言之則啓之敬承繼禹
成王之審訓命釗凡豫教養之法見於保
傅傳者詳矣自其權而言之則盤庚繼兄
陽甲而三篇敷告以後子弟更立而十世
無爭此則及王之功著於大紀論者昭矣
漢唐而下教養漸疎然漢自孝文初年豫
建太子傅至成帝雖非令主猶知擇立定
陶此漢之所以得也唐自穆宗以後定策
===
禁中其間文武號為賢君而皆不能正始
此唐之所以失也宋儒朱熹以賈誼所謂
太子正而天下定為天下之至言非論其
經乎宋臣范鎮以真宗故事養宗子於宮
中為天下之大慮非論其權乎然非獨鎮
言之司馬光之判并州蓋外官也當仁宗
嘉祐之前已上三章欲選宗室為繼嗣迨
知諫院復進極言然非宰臣韓琦等之盡
力贊襄則帝亦未遽決也卒之英宗入繼
punctuated: 而豫則行乎其間，故論治者必以三代為法程也。自其經而言之，則啓之敬承繼禹，成王之審訓命釗，凡豫教養之法，見於保傅傳者詳矣。自其權而言之，則盤庚繼兄陽甲，而三篇敷告以後，子弟更立，而十世無爭，此則及王之功，著於大紀論者昭矣。漢唐而下，教養漸疎。然漢自孝文初年豫建太子傅，至成帝雖非令主，猶知擇立定陶，此漢之所以得也。唐自穆宗以後，定策禁中，其間文武號為賢君，而皆不能正始，此唐之所以失也。宋儒朱熹以賈誼所謂太子正而天下定為天下之至言，非論其經乎？宋臣范鎮以真宗故事養宗子於宮中為天下之大慮，非論其權乎？然非獨鎮言之，司馬光之判并州，蓋外官也，當仁宗嘉祐之前，已上三章，欲選宗室為繼嗣；迨知諫院，復進極言。然非宰臣韓琦等之盡力贊襄，則帝亦未遽決也。卒之英宗入繼
translation_en:
…and advance preparation operates between them. Thus those who discuss government must take the Three Dynasties as their model. In terms of constant principles, there were Qi’s reverent succession to Yu and King Cheng’s carefully considered instructions charging Zhao with the succession. The methods of preparing through education and nurture are recorded in detail in the Account of Protectors and Tutors (Baofu zhuan). In terms of expedient measures, Pan Geng succeeded his elder brother Yang Jia; after the proclamations contained in the three chapters, sons and younger brothers succeeded in turn, with no contention for ten reigns. The achievement of the king [?] is clearly set forth in the Discussions on the Great Chronicle (Daji lun).

From the Han and Tang onward, education and nurture gradually received less attention. Yet the Han appointed a Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent in advance, early in Emperor Xiaowen’s reign. Later, although Emperor Cheng was no excellent ruler, he still knew to select and establish the Prince of Dingtao as his heir. This was where the Han succeeded. Under the Tang, from Emperor Muzong onward, the succession was settled within the palace. Among the subsequent emperors, Wenzong and Wuzong were reputed to be worthy rulers, yet neither could ensure a proper beginning to his reign. This was where the Tang failed.

The Song scholar Zhu Xi regarded Jia Yi’s statement, “When the heir apparent is upright, the realm is secure,” as the most penetrating pronouncement concerning the realm. Was this not a discussion of constant principles? The Song official Fan Zhen regarded nurturing a son of the imperial lineage within the palace, following Emperor Zhenzong’s precedent, as a matter of fundamental concern for the realm. Was this not a discussion of expedient measures? Yet Fan Zhen was not alone in saying this. When Sima Guang administered Bingzhou, he was an official serving outside the capital. Even before Emperor Renzong’s Jiayou era, he had submitted three memorials requesting that a member of the imperial lineage be selected as heir. Upon taking charge of the Remonstrance Bureau, he again presented the strongest arguments. Yet without the chief councilor Han Qi and others doing their utmost to assist, the emperor would still not have reached a decision promptly. In the end, Yingzong entered the palace to succeed to the throne…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
治平無事則司馬韓范之功豈可少哉抑
非獨光爲然婁寅亮之丞上虞蓋末秩也
當高宗紹興之初乃能倡議乞選藝祖之
諸孫慷慨一書足以悟主然非樞密李回
等之同心將順則帝能無疑乎已而孝宗
嗣立付託得人則婁李亦不爲無助矣是
諸臣者功在社稷夫孰以爲罪名垂後世
亦孰以爲非抑愚又有進於是者濟經以
權非惟三代之君爲然也昔者聖莫如堯
===
舜治莫逮唐虞堯擇嗣而得舜於同宗之
下舜擇嗣而得禹於同祖之下蓋太善處
天下之變耳
建儲以豫亦非徒三代之君爲然也我
朝
聖祖開基
神宗紹統必先
國本肇建
元良或以
punctuated:
治平無事，則司馬、韓、范之功豈可少哉！抑非獨光爲然，婁寅亮之丞上虞，蓋末秩也。當高宗紹興之初，乃能倡議乞選藝祖之諸孫，慷慨一書，足以悟主。然非樞密李回等之同心將順，則帝能無疑乎？已而孝宗嗣立，付託得人，則婁、李亦不爲無助矣。是諸臣者，功在社稷，夫孰以爲罪？名垂後世，亦孰以爲非？抑愚又有進於是者：濟經以權，非惟三代之君爲然也。昔者聖莫如堯舜，治莫逮唐虞。堯擇嗣而得舜於同宗之下，舜擇嗣而得禹於同祖之下，蓋太善處天下之變耳。
建儲以豫，亦非徒三代之君爲然也。我朝聖祖開基，神宗紹統，必先國本，肇建元良，或以
translation_en:
…and the Zhiping era passed without incident. How, then, could the contributions of Sima Guang, Han Qi, and Fan Zhen be considered slight? Nor was Guang alone in acting thus. Lou Yinliang, as Assistant Magistrate of Shangyu, held only a low-ranking post. Yet at the beginning of Gaozong’s Shaoxing era, he took the initiative in requesting that a successor be selected from among the descendants of the founding emperor. A single impassioned letter sufficed to awaken his sovereign’s understanding. But without the united support of Li Hui, Commissioner of Military Affairs, and others in carrying this forward, could the emperor have remained free of doubts? Subsequently, Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, and the realm was entrusted to a worthy man. Lou and Li, therefore, cannot be said to have rendered no assistance. These ministers performed meritorious service for the altars of soil and grain: who could regard it as a crime? Their names have endured for later generations: who could judge their conduct wrong?
Yet I would venture a further point: supplementing constant principles with expedient measures was not confined to the rulers of the Three Dynasties. In antiquity, none surpassed Yao and Shun in sageliness, and no government equaled that of Tang and Yu. In choosing a successor, Yao found Shun among those of the same lineage; in choosing a successor, Shun found Yu among those sharing a common ancestor. They were simply exceptionally adept [?] at responding to changing circumstances in the realm.
Establishing an heir in advance, too, was not confined to the rulers of the Three Dynasties. In our dynasty, the sagely progenitor laid the foundations, and Shenzong [?] continued the imperial succession. They invariably gave priority to the foundation of the state by establishing the heir apparent, sometimes by…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
太孫監國或以
親王司香
宗廟皆所以垂萬世之防也
聖天子臨御十有四年矣
英明天縱
神武風行顧以
椒寢未繁
前星未耀久虛天下之仰瞻再孽强藩之構
逆
===
法宮燕閒之地獨不念及是乎伏望體
祖宗之心以為心
法帝王之德以為德選建
親賢置諸
左右縱未入
承華之宮亦可任
司香之典庶幾上慰
九廟在天之靈下奠四海蒼生之枕也狂愚不
識忌諱率爾妄言惟進而教之
punctuated:
太孫監國，或以親王司香宗廟，皆所以垂萬世之防也。
聖天子臨御十有四年矣，英明天縱，神武風行。顧以椒寢未繁，前星未耀，久虛天下之仰瞻，再孽强藩之構逆。法宮燕閒之地，獨不念及是乎？伏望體祖宗之心以為心，法帝王之德以為德，選建親賢，置諸左右。縱未入承華之宮，亦可任司香之典。庶幾上慰九廟在天之靈，下奠四海蒼生之枕也。狂愚不識忌諱，率爾妄言，惟進而教之。
translation_en:
…the imperial grandson to act as regent, or a prince of the blood to oversee incense offerings in the ancestral temples: all these were means of providing safeguards for ten thousand generations.
The sagely Son of Heaven has now occupied the throne for fourteen years. His brilliance and discernment are Heaven-bestowed; his divine martial might sweeps abroad like the wind. Yet the consorts’ chambers have not been fruitful, and the star of the heir apparent has not shone. The hopes of all under Heaven have long remained unfulfilled, and twice powerful princely fiefs have bred rebellious plots [?]. In the hours of quiet leisure within the imperial palace, does Your Majesty alone give no thought to this? I humbly hope that you will take the intentions of your ancestors as your own and model your virtue upon that of the ancient sovereigns, selecting and establishing a worthy imperial kinsman and keeping him at your side. Even if he has not yet entered the Chenghua Palace—the residence of the heir apparent—he may still be entrusted with the duty of overseeing incense offerings. Thus you might comfort above the spirits of the ancestors of the nine temples in Heaven, and below enable the common people throughout the realm to rest securely upon their pillows. Rash and foolish, I do not understand what must not be said and have recklessly spoken presumptuous words. I ask only that you advance and instruct me.

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第四問
劉一松
同考試官教諭王批以此策觀子必能進言於
君者矣
考試官教諭張批得納約自牖之意可取
考試官教諭應批詞婉而事實宜冠本房
人君知有一言興邦之效而後可以盡君
道人臣知有片言悟主之機而後可以盡
臣道蓋一言可以興邦者知爲君之難片
===
言可以悟主者因其心之明也昔晏子爲
齊景公陳先王巡狩遊觀之法今時流連
荒亡之行而景公悅之夫晏子一陪臣爾
而知所以畜其君景公一諸侯爾而知所
以悅其臣矧
聖天子在上而有不可以古義陳者乎此執事
發策意也敢不述所聞而敬對之夫虞周
之巡狩年數不同同也然舜之一歲巡四
嶽者兵衛少而徵求寡周之又六年乃□
punctuated:
第四問
劉一松
同考試官教諭王批：「以此策觀，子必能進言於君者矣。」
考試官教諭張批：「得納約自牖之意，可取。」
考試官教諭應批：「詞婉而事實，宜冠本房。」
人君知有一言興邦之效，而後可以盡君道；人臣知有片言悟主之機，而後可以盡臣道。蓋一言可以興邦者，知爲君之難；片言可以悟主者，因其心之明也。昔晏子爲齊景公陳先王巡狩遊觀之法、今時流連荒亡之行，而景公悅之。夫晏子一陪臣爾，而知所以畜其君；景公一諸侯爾，而知所以悅其臣。矧聖天子在上，而有不可以古義陳者乎？此執事發策意也。敢不述所聞而敬對之？夫虞周之巡狩，年數不同，同也。然舜之一歲巡四嶽者，兵衛少而徵求寡；周之又六年乃□
translation_en:
Fourth Policy Question
Liu Yisong
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “Judging by this policy essay, you will surely be able to offer counsel to your ruler.”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “It captures the meaning of ‘offering simple counsel through the window’; it merits acceptance.”
Examiner Ying, Instructor, comments: “Its language is tactful and its substance grounded in fact. It should rank first in this examining room.”
Only when a ruler understands how a single utterance can bring prosperity to a state can he fully discharge the ruler’s duty. Only when a minister understands the opportunity to enlighten his sovereign with a few words can he fully discharge the minister’s duty. A single utterance can bring prosperity to a state by making one understand the difficulty of being a ruler; a few words can enlighten a sovereign by drawing upon the illumination of his mind.
Formerly, Yanzi explained to Duke Jing of Qi the former kings’ practices of inspection tours and excursions, and the present age’s practices of drifting about, lingering, neglecting affairs, and losing all restraint. Duke Jing was pleased. Yanzi was merely the minister of a feudatory lord, yet he knew how to nurture his ruler; Duke Jing was merely a feudatory lord, yet he knew how to take pleasure in his minister’s counsel. How much more so when the sagely Son of Heaven reigns above! Could there be anything that cannot be presented to him through the principles of antiquity? This is your intent in setting this policy question. Dare I fail to recount what I have learned and respectfully answer it?
As for the inspection tours of Yu and Zhou, their intervals in years differed, yet they were the same [?]. Shun toured the Four Sacred Peaks within a single year because his armed escort was small and his requisitions few; under Zhou, only after another six years did □ …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
巡者考制度而明黜陟謂非經世而何哉
夏周之懲觀盛德不廢固也然一遊一豫
為諸侯度為臺為沼民歡樂之夫豈般樂
而然哉神禹之功大固在人爾然甫再傳
而為太康以逸滅德盤遊無度則有夷羿
之距而五子作歌金履祥謂讀是歌知仲
康之宜君也成康之澤深亦未艾爾然甫
再傳而為穆王欲肆其心周行天下遂為
瑶池之宴而祭公矢詩朱子謂不有是詩
===
則徐方御宸極矣是其祖功宗德固有以
維持之而規誦箴戒亦豈無所裨補哉漢
唐以來非復古制名雖巡狩實則遊豫固
不能以盡述也其間如文帝漢之賢主也
乃與豪俊方正而擊兔伐狐其視成帝從
期門私奴而闘雞走馬者亦何以大相逺
耶然文帝聞賈山之至言則嘉納之成帝
雖有班伯之讜言左遷張放而不忍也此
其盛衰之所以殊豈不以聽言之有緩急
punctuated:
巡者，考制度而明黜陟，謂非經世而何哉？夏周之懲觀，盛德不廢，固也。然一遊一豫，為諸侯度；為臺為沼，民歡樂之，夫豈般樂而然哉？神禹之功大，固在人爾。然甫再傳而為太康，以逸滅德，盤遊無度，則有夷羿之距，而五子作歌。金履祥謂讀是歌，知仲康之宜君也。成康之澤深，亦未艾爾。然甫再傳而為穆王，欲肆其心，周行天下，遂為瑶池之宴，而祭公矢詩。朱子謂不有是詩，則徐方御宸極矣。是其祖功宗德，固有以維持之，而規誦箴戒，亦豈無所裨補哉？
漢唐以來，非復古制，名雖巡狩，實則遊豫，固不能以盡述也。其間如文帝，漢之賢主也，乃與豪俊方正而擊兔伐狐，其視成帝從期門私奴而闘雞走馬者，亦何以大相逺耶？然文帝聞賈山之至言，則嘉納之；成帝雖有班伯之讜言，左遷張放而不忍也。此其盛衰之所以殊，豈不以聽言之有緩急
translation_en:
…to conduct a tour was to examine institutions and regulations and make clear the grounds for demotion and promotion. How could this be called anything other than ordering the realm? As for the inspection tours [?] of Xia and Zhou, it is certainly true that their splendid virtue was not abandoned. Yet every excursion and recreation served as a standard for the feudal lords; when they built terraces and ponds, the people delighted in them. Surely this was not done merely for pleasure! The achievements of the divine Yu were great and certainly remained in the people’s memory. Yet after only two successions came Taikang, who destroyed his virtue through ease and indulged in excursions and hunting without restraint. Consequently, Yi Yi barred his return, and the five sons composed their song. Jin Lüxiang said that reading this song showed why Zhongkang deserved to be ruler. The profound beneficence of Kings Cheng and Kang likewise had not yet come to an end. Yet after only two successions came King Mu, who wished to indulge his desires and travel throughout the realm. He eventually held his banquet at Yaochi, and the Duke of Zhai presented a poem. Master Zhu said that, had it not been for this poem, the ruler of Xu would have occupied the imperial throne. Thus, although ancestral achievements and virtue certainly helped sustain the dynasty, how could admonitory recitations and warnings have failed to contribute as well?
From the Han and Tang onward, the ancient institutions were no longer followed. Although called inspection tours, these journeys were actually excursions for pleasure; they cannot all be recounted here. Among these rulers, Emperor Wen was a worthy sovereign of the Han, yet he went striking hares and hunting foxes with men of outstanding talent and upright character. How greatly did he differ from Emperor Cheng, who took Gate Attendants and private slaves along for cockfighting and horse racing? Yet when Emperor Wen heard Jia Shan’s earnest words, he welcomed and accepted them. Emperor Cheng, despite Ban Bo’s forthright counsel, could not bear to demote Zhang Fang. Was not the difference between the flourishing of one reign and the decline of the other due to their differing degrees of urgency in heeding counsel…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
歟太宗唐之英主也乃欲遊南山嚴裝已
辦而不行其視彼斥欲幸驪山銳意一往
而遽還者亦何以遽相異耳然太宗畏魏
徵之直諫故中輟焉敬宗雖有張權輿之
叩頭欲身自試禍而不信也此其禍福之
所以異豈不以聞言之有從違歟觀於成
帝敬宗而知樂不可極觀於文帝太宗而
知言為有益亦彰彰矣洪惟我
朝
===
皇祖芟夷僭偽
太宗逐北腥羶當時櫛風沐雨於行陣之間
駐蹕汗馬於沙漠之外非不勞矣寔也以
憂勤成
大業安逸
貽子孫耳
累朝宅中而圖大
列聖恭己而垂裳鼎祚凝
景命於穆清乾坤奠於磐石非不可講時巡
punctuated:
歟？太宗，唐之英主也，乃欲遊南山，嚴裝已辦而不行。其視彼斥欲幸驪山，銳意一往而遽還者，亦何以遽相異耳？然太宗畏魏徵之直諫，故中輟焉；敬宗雖有張權輿之叩頭，欲身自試禍而不信也。此其禍福之所以異，豈不以聞言之有從違歟？觀於成帝、敬宗而知樂不可極，觀於文帝、太宗而知言為有益，亦彰彰矣。
洪惟我朝，皇祖芟夷僭偽，太宗逐北腥羶。當時櫛風沐雨於行陣之間，駐蹕汗馬於沙漠之外，非不勞矣。寔也以憂勤成大業，安逸貽子孫耳。累朝宅中而圖大，列聖恭己而垂裳，鼎祚凝，景命於穆清，乾坤奠於磐石，非不可講時巡
translation_en:
…was it not? Taizong, an outstanding ruler of the Tang, wished to make an excursion to Nanshan. Though all preparations for departure were complete, he did not go. Compared with that other ruler who wished to visit Lishan [?], determined to go but abruptly returning, how was he so very different? Yet Taizong feared Wei Zheng’s forthright remonstrance and therefore abandoned his journey. Jingzong, despite Zhang Quanyu’s knocking his head against the ground in remonstrance, wished to expose himself to disaster and would not believe him. Was not the difference in their misfortune and good fortune due to whether they accepted or rejected the counsel they heard? From Chengdi and Jingzong we learn that pleasure must not be pursued to excess; from Wendi and Taizong we learn that counsel is beneficial. This is abundantly clear.
We reverently reflect that, in our dynasty, the August Progenitor cut down the usurpers and pretenders, while Taizong pursued the fleeing foes, those reeking of flesh and mutton. In those days, combed by the wind and bathed by the rain amid the ranks of battle, they halted the imperial carriage and sweated their warhorses beyond the deserts. Their labors were indeed great. In truth, through anxious diligence they accomplished the great enterprise, leaving ease and repose to their descendants. Successive reigns have occupied the center and planned for greatness; successive sage sovereigns have reverently composed themselves and let their robes hang down in effortless rule. The dynastic succession stands firm, the glorious Mandate abides in the august purity of the court, and Heaven and Earth are established upon solid rock. It is not that periodic tours of inspection could not be undertaken…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也以
宗社不可離
大寶不可曠耳比者
皇上北狩西征驅馳關塞于以肅羌胡飭邊鄙
盖
法
祖之銳心然而臣子長慮卻顧激切肺肝以爲
不乗危不徼倖乃古人之深戒邇聞
聖心毅然復欲南巡言者相繼得罪遠近莫不
惕息而臣子惓惓忠愛之心終不能以自
已也故執事發策諸生而亦詢之以是豈
非欲收千慮之一得乎愚以爲
巡遊之利害
廷臣類能言之顧左右之言未可信也諸大
夫之言未可信也國人言之然後察之而
芻蕘之言聖人擇焉今嶺海之士自視猶
國人之疎而疎拙之言亦豈非芻蕘之倫
歟執事倘與其進而厠之鄉書進之
punctuated: 也，以宗社不可離，大寶不可曠耳。比者，皇上北狩西征，驅馳關塞，于以肅羌胡，飭邊鄙，盖法祖之銳心。然而臣子長慮卻顧，激切肺肝，以爲不乗危、不徼倖，乃古人之深戒。邇聞聖心毅然復欲南巡，言者相繼得罪，遠近莫不惕息，而臣子惓惓忠愛之心終不能以自已也。故執事發策諸生，而亦詢之以是，豈非欲收千慮之一得乎？愚以爲巡遊之利害，廷臣類能言之。顧左右之言未可信也，諸大夫之言未可信也，國人言之，然後察之，而芻蕘之言，聖人擇焉。今嶺海之士，自視猶國人之疎，而疎拙之言，亦豈非芻蕘之倫歟？執事倘與其進，而厠之鄉書，進之
translation_en:
…; it was simply because the ancestral temples and altars of state could not be left behind, and the imperial throne could not be left vacant. Recently, His Majesty has hunted in the north and campaigned in the west, riding through frontier passes and fortresses to subdue the Qiang and Hu and put the borderlands in order. This surely springs from his ardent resolve to emulate his ancestors. Yet his servants and subjects, considering the long term and looking back with concern, feel this deeply in their hearts: not exposing oneself to danger and not courting good fortune were solemn admonitions of the ancients. Recently we have heard that His Majesty is firmly resolved to make another tour, this time to the south. Those who have spoken out have incurred punishment one after another; far and near, all hold their breath in fear. Yet his servants and subjects cannot still their earnest feelings of loyalty and love.

Thus, when you, the examining officials, set policy questions for the students, you also asked about this matter. Was this not in the hope of gleaning one sound thought among a thousand reflections? In my humble view, the court officials can generally explain the benefits and harms of imperial tours. Yet the words of those close to the ruler cannot necessarily be trusted, nor can those of the high officials. Only after the people of the realm have spoken should the matter be examined; and the sage selects what is useful even from the words of grass cutters and wood gatherers. We scholars of Linghai regard ourselves as among the more distant of the realm’s people. Are not our unpolished, clumsy words likewise comparable to those of grass cutters and wood gatherers? If you should approve our advancement, include us in the provincial recommendation register, and present us to…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天府少經
睿覽未必不加察於此也不識以爲何如
第五問
舒素蘊
同考試官教諭唐批能原其法之弊而善爲之制有用之學也
考試官教諭張批議所以救弊之方不失立法本意子非
但善處一方之務者
考試官教諭應批該博之學超邁之識宏濟之才皆於
此策見之矣
===
有畫一之定法有變通之時宜法立於前
必有以守之則無弊弊生於後不有以變
之則不通守
國家經常之法酌地方變通之宜其不在於
得人矣乎蓋不得其人或因循以長弊或
更張而反常皆非所以善治也執事以時
務策諸生蓋以俊傑待之而□□其人也
何足以言遠姑以廣東之利病陳之可乎
以軍伍言之我
punctuated:
天府，少經睿覽，未必不加察於此也。不識以爲何如？
第五問
舒素蘊
同考試官教諭唐批：能原其法之弊，而善爲之制，有用之學也。
考試官教諭張批：議所以救弊之方，不失立法本意，子非但善處一方之務者。
考試官教諭應批：該博之學，超邁之識，宏濟之才，皆於此策見之矣。
有畫一之定法，有變通之時宜。法立於前，必有以守之，則無弊；弊生於後，不有以變之，則不通。守國家經常之法，酌地方變通之宜，其不在於得人矣乎？蓋不得其人，或因循以長弊，或更張而反常，皆非所以善治也。執事以時務策諸生，蓋以俊傑待之，而□□其人也。何足以言遠？姑以廣東之利病陳之，可乎？以軍伍言之，我
translation_en:
…to the imperial repository. Should it receive even a brief imperial perusal, His Majesty might well give this matter consideration. I do not know what you think of this.
Fifth Question
Shu Suyun
Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: He can trace the sources of abuses in the regulations and aptly devise measures to address them. This is learning of practical use.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: His discussion of remedies for abuses preserves the original intent of the legislation. You are capable of more than merely managing the affairs of a single locality well.
Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: Broad learning, outstanding discernment, and the talent to accomplish much for the public good are all evident in this policy essay.
There are established laws that provide uniform rules, and there are measures adapted to the needs of the time. Once laws have been established, there must be means of upholding them so that abuses do not arise. When abuses subsequently emerge, unless there are means of adapting the laws, they cannot function effectively. Does not upholding the state's regular laws while weighing the adaptations appropriate to local circumstances depend upon obtaining the right people? Without the right people, some merely follow precedent and allow abuses to grow, while others introduce changes that violate established norms. Neither makes for good government. In questioning us students on current affairs, you evidently regard us as men of outstanding ability and [?] such men. How could I be adequate to discussing distant matters? May I provisionally set forth Guangdong's benefits and problems? To speak of the military ranks, our…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
朝設立衛所管領隊伍以衛郡邑大約以五
千六百名爲一衛一千一百二十名爲一
千戶所而分之爲十百戶所隨分軍數或
有多寡而千百戶所統則一固定制也然
承平日久而廣東之軍伍不能以不耗其
何也番戍於廣西而往者多斃役占於權
門而勞者弗息在衛者不勝其剥削而逃
亡解補者又多以姦賄而脫免欲其不耗
得乎是其清查追究固有任其責者而愚
===
則有說焉充軍事例極重者定發煙瘴廣
東州縣多係煙瘴地面而其犯法之民乃
發別省充軍顧不可少通其變乎誠建言
于
朝量其犯法輕重俱發本省遠近衛分庶幾
上伸其恩下安其土而軍伍之空缺有所
填補矣以屯田言之我
朝就於衛所度閑曠土以立屯堡大約以十
分為率三分守城七分屯耕每軍受田納
banxin: 廣東鄉試錄 七十四
punctuated:
朝設立衛所，管領隊伍，以衛郡邑。大約以五千六百名爲一衛，一千一百二十名爲一千戶所，而分之爲十百戶所。隨分軍數，或有多寡，而千百戶所統則一，固定制也。然承平日久，而廣東之軍伍不能以不耗，其何也？番戍於廣西，而往者多斃；役占於權門，而勞者弗息；在衛者不勝其剥削而逃亡，解補者又多以姦賄而脫免。欲其不耗，得乎？是其清查追究，固有任其責者，而愚則有說焉。充軍事例，極重者定發煙瘴。廣東州縣多係煙瘴地面，而其犯法之民乃發別省充軍，顧不可少通其變乎？誠建言于朝，量其犯法輕重，俱發本省遠近衛分，庶幾上伸其恩，下安其土，而軍伍之空缺有所填補矣。
以屯田言之，我朝就於衛所，度閑曠土，以立屯堡。大約以十分為率，三分守城，七分屯耕。每軍受田納
translation_en:
…dynasty established guards and battalions to command the troops and defend the prefectures and counties. In general, 5,600 men constitute one guard, and 1,120 men constitute one battalion, which is divided into ten companies. The numbers of troops allotted may vary, but the command structure of the battalions and companies is uniform: this is an established regulation. Yet after a long period of peace, the ranks in Guangdong have inevitably dwindled. Why is this? Many of those sent on rotating garrison duty to Guangxi die there; those appropriated for service by powerful households toil without respite. Those serving in the guards cannot endure the exactions imposed upon them and desert, while many of those escorted there as replacements evade service through fraud and bribery. Can one expect the ranks not to dwindle? There are certainly officials responsible for investigating and pursuing these matters, but I have a suggestion to offer. Under the precedents governing penal military service, those guilty of the gravest offenses are assigned to malarial regions. Many prefectures and counties in Guangdong lie in such regions, yet their inhabitants who break the law are sent to other provinces for penal military service. Could this practice not be adjusted somewhat? If a proposal were submitted to the court that offenders all be assigned to guards within this province, nearer or farther away according to the gravity of their offenses, then imperial benevolence might be extended from above, the people below might remain settled in their own land, and vacancies in the ranks could be filled.
As for military agricultural colonies, our dynasty surveyed vacant land around the guards and battalions to establish agricultural settlements and forts. As a general proportion, three-tenths of the troops defend the cities and seven-tenths cultivate the colonies. Each soldier receives land and pays…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
糧六石而餘丁所耕亦然蓋良法也然承
行既□身□屯糧不能以不乏矣何
也正軍撤調而田失故主姦豪欺隱而糧
去舊額耕種有利者或擅於本管之官舍
荒廢無收者乃派之虛陪之軍餘欲其不
乏可乎是其督□考求固有司其事者而
愚抑有說焉民田則例最輕者頃收三石
軍所屯種乃民元所不耕而所收之租額
乃十倍民田獨不可變而通之乎請建議
===
干
朝以某地利腴瘠定爲徵收輕重則例庶幾
人效其力官省其勞而屯糧之虧乏可以
足納矣戎伍之外又有民壯之設蓋古民
兵也然必精差擇而時訓練乃可以用之
昔者量免丁糧官給鞍馬器械而今鮮是
恩矣私役民壯罪同私役軍人而今慢是
令矣毋恠乎有其名而無其實也糧儲之
外又有鹽利之興亦今軍餉也然必禁私
punctuated:
糧六石，而餘丁所耕亦然，蓋良法也。然承行既□身□，屯糧不能以不乏矣。何也？正軍撤調而田失故主，姦豪欺隱而糧去舊額。耕種有利者，或擅於本管之官舍；荒廢無收者，乃派之虛陪之軍餘。欲其不乏，可乎？是其督□考求，固有司其事者，而愚抑有說焉。民田則例，最輕者頃收三石；軍所屯種，乃民元所不耕，而所收之租額乃十倍民田，獨不可變而通之乎？請建議干朝，以某地利腴瘠，定爲徵收輕重則例。庶幾人效其力，官省其勞，而屯糧之虧乏可以足納矣。

戎伍之外，又有民壯之設，蓋古民兵也。然必精差擇而時訓練，乃可以用之。昔者量免丁糧，官給鞍馬器械，而今鮮是恩矣。私役民壯，罪同私役軍人，而今慢是令矣。毋恠乎有其名而無其實也。

糧儲之外，又有鹽利之興，亦今軍餉也。然必禁私
translation_en:
…six shi of grain; the same applies to land cultivated by supplementary males in military households. This was surely a sound arrangement. Yet in its implementation, [text damaged and unclear], shortages in the grain from military agricultural colonies have become inevitable. Why? Regular soldiers are withdrawn or transferred, and the fields lose their former cultivators; unscrupulous powerful men conceal holdings by fraud, and grain receipts fall below their former quotas. Fields profitable to cultivate are sometimes monopolized by the sons of officers in the responsible command; abandoned fields yielding nothing are assigned to surplus men of military households, who must make good the assessments without any actual proceeds [?]. Can shortages possibly be avoided? There are, of course, officials responsible for supervision [one character illegible] and investigation, yet I, in my ignorance, also have something to propose. Under the assessment schedules for civilian fields, the lowest levy is three shi per qing. The land cultivated in military colonies is land that civilians originally did not cultivate, yet its assessed rent is ten times that of civilian fields. Could this arrangement alone not be modified to meet circumstances? I request that a proposal be submitted to the court to establish higher or lower assessment schedules according to the productivity and fertility or barrenness of each tract. Then people might exert their strength, officials might be spared labor, and the shortfalls in military-colony grain could be made good, with payment rendered in full.

Besides the military ranks, there is also the institution of local militiamen, corresponding to the citizen soldiers of antiquity. They can be put to use, however, only if carefully selected and regularly trained. Formerly, they received measured exemptions from poll and grain levies, while the authorities supplied saddles, horses, weapons, and equipment. Today, such favors are rare. Employing local militiamen for private service carries the same penalty as employing soldiers for private service, yet today this ordinance is treated lightly. No wonder the institution exists in name but lacks substance.

Besides grain reserves, there is also the development of salt revenues, which likewise provide funds for military expenses today. Yet it is necessary to prohibit illicit…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
鹽而革官埠乃可以專之頃者便宜許帶
六引盛行其私而官引皆不行矣豈夾帶
私鹽之法不可嚴於是地乎勢要盤據諸
埠得擅其利而商賈亦不行矣豈侵奪民
利之令不可明於是時乎毋惑乎有其害
而無其利也洗心以四者爲廣東之切要
信矣然得人其尤切要歟誠得其人以理
之則興利而除害也扶偏而補弊也柔不
失之因循剛不失之更張而天下豈有不
===
舉之事哉管見區區未知是否惟進而教
之
punctuated: 鹽而革官埠，乃可以專之。頃者便宜許帶六引，盛行其私，而官引皆不行矣。豈夾帶私鹽之法不可嚴於是地乎？勢要盤據諸埠，得擅其利，而商賈亦不行矣。豈侵奪民利之令不可明於是時乎？毋惑乎有其害而無其利也。洗心以四者爲廣東之切要，信矣。然得人其尤切要歟？誠得其人以理之，則興利而除害也，扶偏而補弊也，柔不失之因循，剛不失之更張，而天下豈有不舉之事哉？管見區區，未知是否，惟進而教之。
translation_en:
…salt and abolish the official depots; only then can this source of revenue be secured. Recently, an expedient concession allowed the carriage of six salt certificates’ worth of salt, greatly encouraging illicit trade, while salt covered by official certificates ceased to circulate altogether. Can the law against carrying illicit salt among authorized cargo not be strictly enforced here? Powerful and influential men occupy the various depots and monopolize their profits, while merchants, too, can no longer conduct their trade. Can the prohibitions against usurping the people’s profits not be clearly enforced at this time? It is no wonder that this brings harm without benefit.

With a cleansed mind [?], I regard these four matters as Guangdong’s urgent concerns: this is indeed so. Yet is securing the right men not more urgent still? If truly suitable men are obtained to manage them, they will promote benefits and eliminate harms, correct imbalances and remedy abuses. Their gentleness will not lapse into complacent adherence to precedent, nor their firmness into excessive alteration. What undertaking in the realm could then remain unaccomplished? These are merely my limited views; I do not know whether they are correct. I ask only that you guide and instruct me.

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
聖天子臨御十有四年令天下開科
矣巡按廣東監察御史毛鳳暨
藩臬諸臣如故事奉行惟謹務
期得士以副
上德意八月庚寅事竣錄成僉謂畝
當序其末簡夫廣東北距五嶺
南負重溟秦漢以來視為荒徼
唐韓愈嘗謂中州清淑之氣至
嶺而窮氣之所窮盛而不過必
蜿嬗扶輿磅礴而鬱積而物不
能獨當柳宗元則疑陽德之炳
耀獨發於紛葩瑰麗而不鍾乎
人至宋歐陽脩猶言廣南進士
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

聖天子臨御十有四年，令天下開科矣。巡按廣東監察御史毛鳳暨藩臬諸臣，如故事奉行惟謹，務期得士，以副上德意。八月庚寅，事竣錄成，僉謂畝當序其末簡。

夫廣東北距五嶺，南負重溟，秦漢以來視為荒徼。唐韓愈嘗謂中州清淑之氣至嶺而窮，氣之所窮，盛而不過，必蜿嬗扶輿，磅礴而鬱積，而物不能獨當。柳宗元則疑陽德之炳耀，獨發於紛葩瑰麗，而不鍾乎人。至宋歐陽脩猶言廣南進士
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the fourteenth year of the sagely Son of Heaven’s reign, he commanded that examinations be held throughout the realm. Mao Feng, the Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Guangdong, together with the officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, most scrupulously carried out the command according to established precedent. They strove to obtain worthy scholars and thus fulfill His Majesty’s benevolent intentions. On the gengyin day of the eighth month, the proceedings concluded and the record was completed. All agreed that I, Mu, should write a postface for its closing pages.

Guangdong reaches north to the Five Ranges and has the vast seas at its southern back. Since the Qin and Han dynasties, it has been regarded as a remote frontier. Han Yu of the Tang once said that the pure and refined vital energy of the Central Region reaches the ranges and comes to its limit. Where this energy reaches its limit, it flourishes but cannot pass beyond; it must wind and spread [?], surge expansively, and accumulate densely, so that material things alone cannot contain it. Liu Zongyuan, however, wondered whether the brilliant radiance of yang’s potency manifested itself only in abundant blossoms and magnificent beauty, without concentrating in human beings. Even in the Song, Ouyang Xiu still said that the metropolitan graduates (jinshi) of Guangnan …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
例無舉業諸州但據數解發其
人亦自知無藝一記名試而歸
冀作攝官爾乃今故也應聘而
不濫竿校文之任左顧右盼應
接不暇而限於
制額汰於什一止收如千人行其文
之優者錄之蔚乎豐潤而非有
===
餘也渾乎簡素而非不足也庸
非
國家道洽政治禮陶樂鎔天日開
明山川軒豁以故清淑之氣之
蜿嬗扶輿磅礴而鬱積者至是
盡發為人才而陽明之光耀者
亦至是始煥為文章歟不然何
punctuated: 例無舉業，諸州但據數解發，其人亦自知無藝，一記名試而歸，冀作攝官爾。乃今故也，應聘而不濫竿校文之任，左顧右盼，應接不暇，而限於制額，汰於什一，止收如千人行，其文之優者錄之。蔚乎豐潤而非有餘也，渾乎簡素而非不足也。庸非國家道洽政治，禮陶樂鎔，天日開明，山川軒豁，以故清淑之氣之蜿嬗扶輿磅礴而鬱積者，至是盡發為人才，而陽明之光耀者，亦至是始煥為文章歟？不然，何
translation_en:
…as a rule had no preparation for the examinations. The prefectures merely forwarded candidates according to the prescribed numbers. The men themselves also knew that they lacked literary skill; once they had registered their names and sat the examination, they returned home, hoping only to become acting officials.

Yet now [the wording 故也 is doubtful], having accepted the invitation to serve without unworthily occupying the post of Examiner [?], I look to left and right and can scarcely attend to all that comes before me. But the imperially prescribed quota imposes a limit: only one in ten survives elimination, and only about a thousand men [?; 如千人行 is unclear] are accepted. The finest of their compositions are recorded here. They are luxuriant and rich, yet not excessive; rounded and plain, yet not deficient.

Is this not because the dynasty’s Way has spread everywhere and its government is well ordered, with ritual molding and music refining the people, the heavenly sun shining brightly, and the mountains and rivers opening into spacious clarity? Thus the pure and harmonious vital force, winding and gathering, vast and pent up, has now fully manifested itself in talented men; and the radiance of luminous yang has likewise only now begun to shine forth as literary composition. Otherwise, why …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
昔之就省試者冀作攝官而今
之赴南宮者連魁□□雖然
唐得一張文獻而諤諤有大臣
之節宋得一崔清獻而屹然有
大臣之風閩未嘗乏間世之賢
也昔人以二獻竝稱而余安道
不數焉亦非以其文而已今是
===
舉之所錄而獻之
上者其皆懷忠秉正願為若人之儔
歟抑亦操筆弄墨絺章繪句以
苟富貴而與向之無藝業者均
為後世之羞歟知者當知所決
擇矣諸君子其敬念之敢不佞
於諸子有一日雅故錄終以是
punctuated: 昔之就省試者冀作攝官，而今之赴南宮者連魁□□？雖然，唐得一張文獻，而諤諤有大臣之節；宋得一崔清獻，而屹然有大臣之風。閩未嘗乏間世之賢也。昔人以二獻竝稱，而余安道不數焉，亦非以其文而已。今是舉之所錄而獻之上者，其皆懷忠秉正，願為若人之儔歟？抑亦操筆弄墨，絺章繪句，以苟富貴，而與向之無藝業者均為後世之羞歟？知者當知所決擇矣。諸君子其敬念之！敢不佞於諸子有一日雅，故錄終以是
translation_en:
…those who formerly sat the Provincial Examination hoped to become acting officials, whereas those now proceeding to the Metropolitan Examination successively take first place in □□ [illegible]? Nevertheless, the Tang had Zhang Wenxian, whose forthright remonstrances displayed the integrity of a great minister; the Song had Cui Qingxian, whose steadfastness displayed the bearing of a great minister. Min [Fujian; the place-name is doubtful in this Guangdong context] has never lacked worthies such as appear only once in several generations. Earlier writers paired the two men whose posthumous names contained “Xian,” yet did not count Yu Andao among them; their judgment, too, was not based merely on literary accomplishment.

Will those selected in this examination and presented to His Majesty all cherish loyalty and uphold rectitude, aspiring to join the company of such men? Or will they merely wield their brushes and play with ink, embroidering compositions and embellishing phrases to secure wealth and rank by any means, and become, like those earlier men without learning or accomplishment, a disgrace in the eyes of posterity? Those with understanding should know what choice to make. Gentlemen, ponder this with reverence! I venture, unworthy though I am [?], on the strength of my brief acquaintance with you gentlemen, to conclude the record with these words …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
吾十有五而志于學三十而立四十而不
惑五十而知天命六十而耳順七十而
從心所欲不踰矩
王天下有三重焉其寡過矣乎
自得之則居之安居之安則資之深資之
深則取之左右逢其原
易
===
內陽而外陰內健而外順內君子而外小
人
中孚以利貞乃應乎天也
君子之道或出或處或默或語二人同心
其利斷金同心之言其臭如蘭
履和而至謙尊而光
書
允釐百工庶績咸熙
佑賢輔德顯忠遂良
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

吾十有五而志于學，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命，六十而耳順，七十而從心所欲，不踰矩。

王天下有三重焉，其寡過矣乎！

自得之，則居之安；居之安，則資之深；資之深，則取之左右逢其原。

易

內陽而外陰，內健而外順，內君子而外小人。

中孚以利貞，乃應乎天也。

君子之道，或出或處，或默或語。二人同心，其利斷金；同心之言，其臭如蘭。

履和而至，謙尊而光。

書

允釐百工，庶績咸熙。

佑賢輔德，顯忠遂良。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

At fifteen, I set my heart on learning; at thirty, I stood firm; at forty, I was free from perplexity; at fifty, I understood Heaven’s mandate; at sixty, my ear was attuned; at seventy, I followed my heart’s desires without overstepping the bounds.

In ruling all under Heaven, there are three weighty matters. Surely one who attends to them will make few errors!

When one has grasped it for oneself, one dwells in it at ease. Dwelling in it at ease, one draws deeply upon it. Drawing deeply upon it, one encounters its source wherever one turns.

Book of Changes

Yang within and yin without; strength within and compliance without; gentlemen within and petty men without.

Inner Sincerity (Zhongfu), through beneficial steadfastness, accords with Heaven.

The way of the gentleman is sometimes to enter public service and sometimes to remain in retirement, sometimes to remain silent and sometimes to speak. When two people are of one heart, their sharpness can cut through metal. Words spoken from united hearts are fragrant as orchids.

Treading (Lü) is harmonious and reaches its goal; Modesty (Qian) is honored and radiant.

Book of Documents

He truly set the hundred offices in order, and all their achievements flourished.

Support the worthy and assist the virtuous; bring the loyal to prominence and advance the good.

text:
租之入以為贍軍之需其立法善矣承
平日久民田之賦不減於
國初而屯田之入常不及十之五焉
朝廷乃專
命憲臣以提督其事親歴衛所考求利弊嚴侵
削之禁急逋負之追征斂有期出納有
數宜其漸復舊規也然行之已久漫無
成功而糧儲益見其虧乏何耶民壯之
設所以補軍伍之不足州邑之下在在
===
有之宜可以備用矣然比年以來是役
悉為虚設倉卒有警輒以雇募為事有
其人而無其用救弊之策將安施耶鹽
利之興所以濟軍餉之不給藩省之地
無處無之宜可以資用矣然比年以來
歲課減於往昔尋常利市多為勢要所
據無其利而有其害救弊之方將安出
耶凡此利病皆天下所同有而在東廣
尤為切要諸士子生長是邦得於聞見
punctuated:
租之入，以為贍軍之需，其立法善矣。承平日久，民田之賦不減於國初，而屯田之入常不及十之五焉。朝廷乃專命憲臣以提督其事，親歴衛所，考求利弊，嚴侵削之禁，急逋負之追，征斂有期，出納有數，宜其漸復舊規也。然行之已久，漫無成功，而糧儲益見其虧乏，何耶？
民壯之設，所以補軍伍之不足。州邑之下，在在有之，宜可以備用矣。然比年以來，是役悉為虚設，倉卒有警，輒以雇募為事。有其人而無其用，救弊之策將安施耶？
鹽利之興，所以濟軍餉之不給。藩省之地，無處無之，宜可以資用矣。然比年以來，歲課減於往昔，尋常利市，多為勢要所據。無其利而有其害，救弊之方將安出耶？
凡此利病，皆天下所同有，而在東廣尤為切要。諸士子生長是邦，得於聞見，
translation_en:
…the receipts from rents, to provide for the army’s needs: the system as established was sound. After a long period of peace, the taxes on civilian farmland have not diminished from those at the dynasty’s founding, yet revenues from military agricultural colonies often fall short of half their original amount. The court therefore specially commissioned censorial officials to supervise these affairs: personally visiting the guards and battalions, investigating advantages and abuses, strictly enforcing prohibitions against encroachment and exaction, pressing for the recovery of arrears, setting deadlines for collections, and keeping accounts of receipts and disbursements. One would expect the former arrangements gradually to be restored. Yet these measures have long been in force without any appreciable success, while grain reserves show ever greater shortfalls. Why is this?
The civilian militia was established to make up for deficiencies in the army’s ranks. Such men are found everywhere in the subprefectures and counties, and should be available for service. Yet in recent years this service has become entirely nominal. Whenever an emergency suddenly arises, the authorities invariably resort to hiring recruits. The men exist, but serve no purpose: what policy can be put into effect to remedy this abuse?
Salt revenues were instituted to make up for insufficient military funding. They exist throughout the provinces and should provide resources for expenditure. Yet in recent years annual receipts have declined from former levels, while ordinary trading profits have largely been appropriated by the powerful and influential. With the benefits lost and the harms remaining, where is a remedy to be found?
All these benefits and problems are shared throughout the realm, but they are particularly pressing in Guangdong. You examination candidates were born and raised in this region, and through what you have heard and seen have gained knowledge…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
吾十有五而志于學三十而立四十而不
惑五十而知天命六十而耳順七十而
從心所欲不踰矩
潘六賓
同考試官訓導黃批發揮聖學之妙殆盡必能用心於內者
同考試官教諭朱批說理之文自是如此
同考試官學正李批作此題者辭愈繁而孔子謙已誨
人之心愈晦是篇簡明可取
===
考試官教諭張批辭理兼到佳士也
考試官教諭應批說明聖人之心殆能以聖人為則者
聖人自名其學一終身經歷之次第焉蓋聖學
無積累之漸而自名其經歷之次第如此寧非
獨覺其進因其近似者而寓夫勉人之深意哉
昔夫子之意謂夫為學之功固不敢廢學造其
極又豈無其漸哉吾年十有五也功收近小而
篤志于大學之道察夫義理措諸事業心在是
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

吾十有五而志于學，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命，六十而耳順，七十而從心所欲，不踰矩。

潘六賓

同考試官訓導黃批：發揮聖學之妙殆盡，必能用心於內者。

同考試官教諭朱批：說理之文，自是如此。

同考試官學正李批：作此題者，辭愈繁，而孔子謙已誨人之心愈晦。是篇簡明可取。

考試官教諭張批：辭理兼到，佳士也。

考試官教諭應批：說明聖人之心，殆能以聖人為則者。

聖人自名其學，一終身經歷之次第焉。蓋聖學無積累之漸，而自名其經歷之次第如此，寧非獨覺其進，因其近似者而寓夫勉人之深意哉？昔夫子之意謂夫為學之功固不敢廢，學造其極，又豈無其漸哉？吾年十有五也，功收近小，而篤志于大學之道，察夫義理，措諸事業，心在是
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“At fifteen, I set my heart on learning; at thirty, I stood firm; at forty, I was free from doubts; at fifty, I understood Heaven’s mandate; at sixty, my ear was attuned; at seventy, I followed my heart’s desires without overstepping the bounds.”

Pan Liubin

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor: He brings out almost fully the subtleties of the sage’s learning. He must be someone capable of inward application of the mind.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: This is just how an essay expounding principle should be written.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Those who write on this topic become ever more verbose, while Confucius’s intention of humbling himself and instructing others becomes ever more obscure. This essay is commendable for its brevity and clarity.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Both expression and reasoning are accomplished. A fine scholar.

Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: He elucidates the sage’s mind and seems capable of taking the sage as his model.

The sage describes his own learning as a sequence of stages experienced throughout his life [?]. The sage’s learning has no gradual process of accumulation, yet he describes the sequence of his experiences in this way. Surely this means that he alone perceived his advance and, through descriptions approximating it, conveyed his profound intention to encourage others?

The Master’s meaning was this: “I certainly dare not neglect the work of learning. And if learning is to reach its utmost attainment, how could it lack a gradual progression? When I was fifteen, my efforts bore fruit in what was immediate and small [?], and I firmly set my heart on the Way of the Great Learning. I examined moral principles and put them into practice in my undertakings. My heart was set on this …”

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而爲之不厭矣及年乎三十也體極高明而自
立於斯道之中天理爲主人心聽命守之固而
無所事志矣自三十而四十焉玩索涵養益加
夫致知之功於事物之所當然皆無所疑是蓋
知之明而守復何所事乎自四十而五十焉窮
理盡性自造夫至命之地於事物所以當然之
故皆達其奥是蓋知極其精而不惑何足云乎
及夫年躋六十則人言一入於耳吾心卽無不
通知之之至不思而得也學至於此殆不知老
===
之將至耶迨於年登七十則隨其心之所欲自
不過於法度行之之妙不勉而中也學至於此
又豈知甚矣吾衰耶吁此固夫子自謙之詞而
至誠無息之意亦可見矣雖然謂夫子必待於
學而循其序非也謂無事於學雖學矣而必無
經歷之次第亦非也蓋聖人有聖人之學而日
用之間必有獨覺其進而人不及知者故自名
其近似者以示人非心實自聖而姑爲是退託
也學者固不可於志學之初遽有是心又不可
punctuated: 而爲之不厭矣。及年乎三十也，體極高明，而自立於斯道之中，天理爲主，人心聽命，守之固而無所事志矣。自三十而四十焉，玩索涵養，益加夫致知之功，於事物之所當然皆無所疑。是蓋知之明，而守復何所事乎？自四十而五十焉，窮理盡性，自造夫至命之地，於事物所以當然之故皆達其奥。是蓋知極其精，而不惑何足云乎？及夫年躋六十，則人言一入於耳，吾心卽無不通，知之之至，不思而得也。學至於此，殆不知老之將至耶？迨於年登七十，則隨其心之所欲，自不過於法度，行之之妙，不勉而中也。學至於此，又豈知「甚矣吾衰」耶？吁！此固夫子自謙之詞，而至誠無息之意亦可見矣。雖然，謂夫子必待於學而循其序，非也；謂無事於學，雖學矣而必無經歷之次第，亦非也。蓋聖人有聖人之學，而日用之間必有獨覺其進而人不及知者，故自名其近似者以示人，非心實自聖而姑爲是退託也。學者固不可於志學之初遽有是心，又不可
translation_en:
…and pursued it without weariness. By the age of thirty, my embodied understanding had attained the utmost loftiness and clarity, and I stood independently within this Way. Heavenly principle was master, and the human mind obeyed its commands. I held to it firmly and no longer needed to exert myself in setting my resolve. From thirty to forty, through reflective inquiry and inner cultivation, I further applied myself to extending knowledge, until I had no doubts about what was right in affairs and things. This was clarity of knowledge: what further need was there to exert myself in holding fast? From forty to fifty, I investigated principle and fully realized my nature, reaching the realm of comprehending Heaven’s mandate. I penetrated the depths of the reasons why affairs and things ought to be as they are. This was knowledge refined to its utmost: how could merely being free from perplexity suffice to describe it? By the age of sixty, as soon as another’s words entered my ears, there was nothing my mind did not comprehend. This was the utmost attainment of knowing—understanding without deliberation. With learning advanced to this point, might I scarcely have known that old age was approaching? By the age of seventy, I followed my heart’s desires and naturally did not overstep the bounds of proper conduct. This was the marvelous perfection of practice—hitting the mark without effort. With learning advanced to this point, how could I have felt, “Great indeed is my decline!”?

Ah! These were indeed the Master’s words of modesty, yet in them one can also perceive the meaning of utmost sincerity that never ceases. Nevertheless, it is wrong to say that the Master necessarily depended upon learning and followed its successive stages. It is equally wrong to say that he had no need for learning, or that, even if he learned, his experience necessarily had no successive stages. For a sage has the learning proper to a sage, and in daily life there must be advances that he alone perceives and that others cannot recognize. Thus he himself named those approximations to his experience in order to instruct others. It was not that he inwardly regarded himself as a sage and merely used these words as a modest pretext for disclaiming that status. Those who learn certainly must not presume to adopt such a state of mind when first setting their hearts upon learning, nor may they…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其等使器用章服之分別者有不易之式焉其
考文耶稽多寡於點畫訂異同於形象必求其
精當也不容於損益焉所以新天下之耳目者
在是所以一天下之心志者在是而何民之不
寡過乎將見國不同也而政□□於國家不一
也而俗不殊於家禮之所議者民皆從而不違
以言天下之行殆同倫矣寧有作聰明而越於
範圍者哉度之所制者民皆守而勿失以言天
下之車殆同軌矣寧有逞私智而出於規矩者
===
哉文之所考者方策無點畫之差契券無形象
之失而書又同文矣奚有倍上者哉遵道遵路
而民定于一會極歸極而民協于中吁德位時
兼全於一人禮度文流行於天下居上不驕固
如是夫嗟夫三重固一天下之制作而又有所
謂不信民弗從者是可以見制作之不可徒為
也唐虞三代尚矣秦漢而下未嘗無制作者然
而不驕之道果能知乎無恠乎治之不古若也
先儒謂作禮樂者必聖人在天子之位信然
punctuated:
其等，使器用章服之分別者有不易之式焉。其考文耶，稽多寡於點畫，訂異同於形象，必求其精當也，不容於損益焉。所以新天下之耳目者在是，所以一天下之心志者在是，而何民之不寡過乎？將見國不同也，而政□□於國；家不一也，而俗不殊於家。禮之所議者，民皆從而不違，以言天下之行，殆同倫矣，寧有作聰明而越於範圍者哉？度之所制者，民皆守而勿失，以言天下之車，殆同軌矣，寧有逞私智而出於規矩者哉？文之所考者，方策無點畫之差，契券無形象之失，而書又同文矣，奚有倍上者哉？遵道遵路，而民定于一；會極歸極，而民協于中。吁！德、位、時兼全於一人，禮、度、文流行於天下，居上不驕，固如是夫！

嗟夫！三重固一天下之制作，而又有所謂不信民弗從者，是可以見制作之不可徒為也。唐虞三代尚矣，秦漢而下，未嘗無制作者，然而不驕之道果能知乎？無恠乎治之不古若也。先儒謂作禮樂者必聖人在天子之位，信然。
translation_en:
…their gradations, so that the distinctions in implements, ceremonial dress, and insignia have unalterable standards. As for his standardization of writing, he checks the number of dots and strokes and determines similarities and differences in the forms of characters, insisting on precision and correctness and allowing neither subtraction nor addition. Herein lies the means of renewing what all under Heaven hear and see; herein lies the means of unifying their hearts and aspirations. How could the people then fail to commit fewer errors? We shall see that, although the states differ, their governance … [?]; although households are many, their customs do not differ from household to household. The people all follow the ritual prescriptions he deliberates upon without departing from them. Thus, conduct throughout the realm may be said to follow the same norms. Could anyone then parade his cleverness and overstep these bounds? The people all uphold the standards he establishes without deviation. Thus, carriages throughout the realm may be said to have the same axle gauge. Could anyone then indulge his private ingenuity and go beyond these rules? As for the writing he standardizes, written records contain no discrepancies in dots and strokes, and contracts contain no errors in character forms. Writing, too, thus uses the same script. How could anyone turn against those above? Following the Way and its paths, the people become settled in unity; converging upon and returning to the supreme standard, they accord with the mean. Ah! Virtue, position, and the proper time are all fully united in one person, while rites, standards, and writing prevail throughout the realm. Such indeed is occupying a high position without arrogance!

Alas! The three weighty matters are indeed institutions for unifying all under Heaven. Yet there is also the saying, “Without trust, the people will not follow.” From this we can see that establishing institutions cannot be merely an empty undertaking. The ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties are remote indeed. From the Qin and Han onward, there have never been lacking those who established institutions; yet did they truly understand the way of avoiding arrogance? No wonder their governance did not equal that of antiquity. Earlier Confucian scholars said that one who creates rites and music must be a sage occupying the position of the Son of Heaven. Truly so.

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
所藉者淵泉如淵而靜深莫測有以爲時出之
地溥博如天而廣遠無際有以爲敦化之基資
之何其深哉夫惟資之既深則日用之間探討
之力不必加也尋繹之功不必事也取之於左
適値其所資之本非體周於用矣乎取之於右
卽逢其所藉之原非一應於萬矣乎夫自得之
中有無窮之妙如此此君子之學所以欲其自
得而必加夫深造以道之功也歟大抵時至戰
國聖道蓁蕪人心陷溺類馳騖於刑名功利而
===
不知學爲何物而出口入耳者又不知所以爲
學也故孟子倡爲自得之說正以續夫格致誠
正之緖欲人求之於身心體用之間耳學者其
毋以之藉口而以徑超頓悟爲事芒芒於虛空
佛老之歸使孟氏之意晦而不明而其爲害又
甚於戰國焉嗚呼此又不可不知也
易
中孚以利貞乃應乎天也
江有執
punctuated:
所藉者淵泉，如淵而靜深莫測，有以爲時出之地；溥博，如天而廣遠無際，有以爲敦化之基。資之何其深哉！夫惟資之既深，則日用之間，探討之力不必加也，尋繹之功不必事也。取之於左，適値其所資之本，非體周於用矣乎？取之於右，卽逢其所藉之原，非一應於萬矣乎？夫自得之中有無窮之妙如此，此君子之學所以欲其自得，而必加夫深造以道之功也歟！大抵時至戰國，聖道蓁蕪，人心陷溺，類馳騖於刑名功利，而不知學爲何物；而出口入耳者，又不知所以爲學也。故孟子倡爲自得之說，正以續夫格致誠正之緖，欲人求之於身心體用之間耳。學者其毋以之藉口，而以徑超頓悟爲事，芒芒於虛空，佛老之歸，使孟氏之意晦而不明，而其爲害又甚於戰國焉。嗚呼！此又不可不知也。

易
中孚以利貞，乃應乎天也。
江有執
translation_en:
…What one draws upon is deep as a spring: still and unfathomable as an abyss, it provides a source from which to issue forth at the proper times; expansive and vast, broad and boundless as Heaven, it provides a foundation for profound transforming influence. How deeply one draws upon it! Only when these resources are deep does one, in daily life, need no additional effort of investigation or further labor of tracing things through. Drawing upon the left, one encounters precisely the foundation on which one relies: does this not mean that substance pervades function? Drawing upon the right, one immediately meets the source on which one depends: does this not mean that the one responds to the myriad? Such are the inexhaustible subtleties within understanding attained for oneself. Is this not why the gentleman, in learning, desires to attain understanding for himself and must therefore devote effort to advancing deeply in accordance with the Way?

By the Warring States period, the Way of the sages had become overgrown, and human hearts had sunk into error. People generally pursued administrative techniques and penal methods, achievement and profit, without knowing what learning was. Those whose learning merely passed from mouth to ear likewise did not know how to pursue it. Thus Mengzi advocated attaining understanding for oneself precisely to carry forward the tradition of investigating things, extending knowledge, making intentions sincere, and rectifying the mind. He wished people to seek it within their own persons and minds, in substance and function. Students must not use this teaching as a pretext for pursuing direct transcendence and sudden enlightenment, wandering aimlessly in emptiness and ending in the teachings of the Buddha and Laozi. This would obscure Mengzi’s meaning, leaving it unclear, and cause harm even greater than that of the Warring States period. Alas! This, too, must be understood.

Book of Changes

“Inner Sincerity: through beneficial perseverance in correctness, it accords with Heaven.”

Jiang Youzhi

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭蔡批利貞應天處作者類多發揮不明
獨子言之縝密透徹非深於易者
考試官教諭張批理致之文自別
考試官教諭應批易義依此作良是
惟所信得乎理之當然者則所信合乎理之從
出者此彖傳之旨也蓋天者理之所從出本自
至正也人而信得其正則天人一理豈有不相
合哉昔夫子傳中孚之彖及此吾想其意蓋以
人而無信則為詐為偽吾固不知其可也信而
===
不正則為固為諒又非所以為信也中孚之辭
而以利貞者是必端謹於心術之微決擇於趨
向之初以至誠不欺之心而裁之以大中至正
之道固不失之詐亦不至於固也念之實不妄
之發而度之以當然不易之理固不失於偽亦
不至於諒也或以己而為信也必以義自許非
徒決死生以自誓而已或與人而相信也必以
道相規非徒傾肝腑以相示而已若然其不足
以應乎天哉誠以天之為天固無不正之信但
punctuated:
同考試官教諭蔡批：利貞應天處，作者類多發揮不明，獨子言之縝密透徹，非深於易者？
考試官教諭張批：理致之文自別。
考試官教諭應批：易義依此作，良是。
惟所信得乎理之當然者，則所信合乎理之從出者，此彖傳之旨也。蓋天者，理之所從出，本自至正也。人而信得其正，則天人一理，豈有不相合哉？昔夫子傳中孚之彖及此，吾想其意，蓋以人而無信，則為詐為偽，吾固不知其可也；信而不正，則為固為諒，又非所以為信也。中孚之辭而以利貞者，是必端謹於心術之微，決擇於趨向之初，以至誠不欺之心，而裁之以大中至正之道，固不失之詐，亦不至於固也；念之實不妄之發，而度之以當然不易之理，固不失於偽，亦不至於諒也。或以己而為信也，必以義自許，非徒決死生以自誓而已；或與人而相信也，必以道相規，非徒傾肝腑以相示而已。若然，其不足以應乎天哉？誠以天之為天，固無不正之信，但
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: Most writers fail to explain clearly the passage on how being beneficial to remain correct accords with Heaven. You alone discuss it with meticulous care and penetrating clarity. Surely you are deeply versed in the Changes? [?]
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Writing that conveys the import of principle is distinctive in itself.
Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: This is indeed a fine model for composing essays on the meaning of the Changes.
Only when one’s trustworthiness accords with what principle requires does it accord with that from which principle issues: this is the purport of the Commentary on the Judgments. Heaven is that from which principle issues, and is inherently supremely correct. If a person’s trustworthiness attains correctness, Heaven and humanity share a single principle: how could they fail to accord? When the Master, in commenting on the judgment of Inner Truth, reached this point, I conceive his meaning to have been this: if a person lacks trustworthiness, he becomes deceitful and false, and I truly do not know how that could be acceptable. Yet if his trustworthiness lacks correctness, it becomes obstinacy and petty fidelity, which likewise do not constitute true trustworthiness. The statement in Inner Truth that it is beneficial to remain correct means that one must be upright and circumspect in the subtlest workings of the heart and make discriminating choices at the outset of one’s course. One must regulate a heart of utmost sincerity, free from deception, by the Way of supreme centrality and correctness. Thus one neither lapses into deceit nor falls into obstinacy. When genuine thoughts arise without falsity, one must measure them against the immutable principle of what ought to be. Thus one neither lapses into falsehood nor falls into petty fidelity. In practicing trustworthiness oneself, one must pledge oneself to righteousness, rather than merely swear an oath committing oneself to life or death. In maintaining mutual trust with others, one must admonish one another according to the Way, rather than merely lay bare one’s innermost feelings. If this is so, would it not suffice to accord with Heaven? Indeed, Heaven, in being Heaven, possesses no trustworthiness that is not correct; yet…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人之信往往有出於正之外今中孚而以利貞
則質之於天者此理也反之於我者亦此理也
在天在人脗合而無間天之信無不正也吾之
信亦無不正也人道天道默契而爲一雖曰維
天之命於穆不已難乎以測之也然正之所在
則於穆不已者在是矣苟或失於固□其心雖
誠其理則非烏能與天合哉雖曰天道流行誠
一不二難乎以燮之也然正之所存則誠一不
二者在斯矣苟或至於諒焉其事雖實而道則
===
悖烏能與天應哉夫既知乎此則知中孚之辭
所謂利貞之意矣以此垂訓其明且盡而後世
顧有如尾生之行召忽之死里克之忠何哉豈
夫子所謂好信不好學其蔽也愚者歟然學尤
貴於知要否則本原不得以澄澈是非終至於
混淆是以君子必大居敬而貴窮理也
履和而至謙尊而光
廖珦
同考試官教諭蔡 批〔朱子語錄云秦人尊君卑臣〕
punctuated:
人之信，往往有出於正之外。今中孚而以利貞，則質之於天者此理也，反之於我者亦此理也。在天在人，脗合而無間；天之信無不正也，吾之信亦無不正也。人道天道，默契而爲一。雖曰「維天之命，於穆不已」，難乎以測之也，然正之所在，則於穆不已者在是矣。苟或失於固□，其心雖誠，其理則非，烏能與天合哉？雖曰天道流行，誠一不二，難乎以燮之也，然正之所存，則誠一不二者在斯矣。苟或至於諒焉，其事雖實，而道則悖，烏能與天應哉？夫既知乎此，則知中孚之辭所謂利貞之意矣。以此垂訓，其明且盡，而後世顧有如尾生之行、召忽之死、里克之忠，何哉？豈夫子所謂「好信不好學，其蔽也愚」者歟？然學尤貴於知要，否則本原不得以澄澈，是非終至於混淆。是以君子必大居敬而貴窮理也。

履和而至，謙尊而光。
廖珦
同考試官教諭蔡批〔朱子語錄云：秦人尊君卑臣。〕
translation_en:
…human trustworthiness often falls outside what is correct. Now, in Inner Truth (Zhongfu), the stipulation that “it is beneficial to be steadfast and correct” means that the principle tested against Heaven is the very same principle found when one turns back to oneself. In Heaven and in human beings, they accord without any gap. Heaven’s trustworthiness is invariably correct, and my trustworthiness is likewise invariably correct. The human Way and Heaven’s Way tacitly accord and become one. Although it is said, “Heaven’s mandate—oh, profound and unceasing!” and it is difficult to fathom, wherever correctness resides, there too resides that which is profound and unceasing. If one should err through stubbornness □ [?], then, though one’s heart is sincere, one’s principle is wrong: how could one accord with Heaven? Although Heaven’s Way moves ceaselessly, wholly sincere and undivided, and it is difficult to harmonize with it [?], wherever correctness resides, there too resides that which is wholly sincere and undivided. If one should lapse into petty fidelity, then, though one’s deeds are genuine, one’s way is perverse: how could one respond to Heaven? Once this is understood, one understands the meaning of “it is beneficial to be steadfast and correct” in the judgment on Inner Truth. The instruction thus handed down is clear and exhaustive. Yet why did later ages nevertheless produce conduct like Wei Sheng’s, a death like Shao Hu’s, and loyalty like Li Ke’s? Were these instances of what the Master meant when he said, “To love trustworthiness without loving learning leads to the failing of foolishness”? In learning, however, what matters especially is knowing the essentials. Otherwise, the source cannot be clarified, and right and wrong ultimately become confused. Thus the gentleman must place great weight on abiding in reverence and value the investigation of principle.

“Treading is harmonious and reaches its goal; Modesty is honored and radiant.”
Liao Xiang

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
雖尊而不光惟謙則尊而光則此句與履和而至以下
數句明是一例作者往往以尊光二字對至字講殊失本
㫖惟此作得之
考試官敎諭張批〔明白簡當〕
考試官敎諭應批〔發明大傳抑揚之意可錄〕
大傳陳易卦之德有順乎世而不可及者有高
乎世而不可掩者夫順而未至者以其非禮高
而不光者以其非謙也大傳於履謙之卦而抑
揚其辭以陳之正以明其可處憂患也歟且履
===
之爲卦上天下澤定分不易卽人之禮也是禮
也何以和而至哉誠以和不本於禮者則流蕩
忘返不足以言至也惟履之爲禮其本則原於
民之性凡行之者安之也初無扞格不勝之患
其制則順於民之情凡由之者便之也初無勉
強難行之病和則和矣然皆天理民彝之極致
或損或益皆不可得也天經地義之當然亘古
亘今皆不能外也其至極也何如謙之爲卦地
中有山以卑蘊高卽人之謙也是謙也何以尊
punctuated:
雖尊而不光，惟謙則尊而光，則此句與履和而至以下數句明是一例。作者往往以尊光二字對至字講，殊失本㫖，惟此作得之。
考試官敎諭張批〔明白簡當〕
考試官敎諭應批〔發明大傳抑揚之意可錄〕
大傳陳易卦之德，有順乎世而不可及者，有高乎世而不可掩者。夫順而未至者，以其非禮；高而不光者，以其非謙也。大傳於履謙之卦，而抑揚其辭以陳之，正以明其可處憂患也歟？且履之爲卦，上天下澤，定分不易，卽人之禮也。是禮也，何以和而至哉？誠以和不本於禮者，則流蕩忘返，不足以言至也。惟履之爲禮，其本則原於民之性，凡行之者安之也，初無扞格不勝之患；其制則順於民之情，凡由之者便之也，初無勉強難行之病。和則和矣，然皆天理民彝之極致，或損或益，皆不可得也；天經地義之當然，亘古亘今，皆不能外也。其至極也何如？謙之爲卦，地中有山，以卑蘊高，卽人之謙也。是謙也，何以尊
translation_en:
…though exalted, they lacked radiance. Only with modesty can one be exalted and radiant. Thus this phrase plainly follows the same pattern as “Treading is harmonious and reaches the utmost” and the several phrases that follow it. Writers often explain the two words “exalted” and “radiant” together as corresponding to “reaches the utmost,” thereby seriously missing the original meaning. This essay alone grasps it.

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Clear, concise, and apt.”

Examiner Ying, Instructor, comments: “It elucidates the Great Commentary’s intent in its qualifying and praising language; it merits inclusion.”

In setting forth the virtues of the hexagrams of the Changes, the Great Commentary describes one that accords with the world yet cannot be equaled, and another that rises above the world yet cannot be obscured. For those who accord with the world but fail to reach the utmost do so because they lack ritual propriety; those who stand high but lack radiance do so because they lack modesty. In describing the hexagrams Treading (Lü) and Modesty (Qian), does the Great Commentary not qualify and praise them in its wording precisely to show how they enable one to cope with anxiety and adversity?

Now, the hexagram Treading has Heaven above and Lake below: their allotted positions are fixed and unchanging. This is ritual propriety among human beings. How is this propriety harmonious yet capable of reaching the utmost? Truly, harmony that is not rooted in ritual propriety drifts unrestrained and forgets to return; it cannot be said to reach the utmost. But the ritual propriety embodied in Treading has its foundation in the people’s nature. All who practice it find ease in it, without any trouble from obstruction or inability to bear it. Its regulations accord with the people’s feelings. All who follow them find them convenient, without any difficulty arising from coercion or impracticability. Harmonious it certainly is; yet it also represents the utmost realization of Heaven’s principle and the constant human norms, admitting neither diminution nor addition. It is what necessarily accords with the enduring patterns of Heaven and the right order of Earth; throughout antiquity and the present, nothing can fall outside it. How consummate is its attainment of the utmost!

The hexagram Modesty has a mountain within the earth: what is low contains what is high. This is modesty among human beings. How does this modesty bring exaltation…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而光哉誠以尊不本於謙者則驕矜自肆難乎
其有光也惟謙以自卑雖位居崇高首出乎庶
物也而不操上人之心雖身處盛滿禮絕乎百
僚也而恒存下人之念尊則尊矣然人之望之
也益見其道德之盛光輝發越自有不容掩矣
人之仰之也愈見其事業之隆光明俊偉自有
不可遏矣其光顯也何如夫履和而至可見履
德之妙謙尊而光可見謙德之妙以之而處憂
患也何有哉所以然者蓋有禮則安無禮則危
===
謙則受益滿則招損其理有固然者故羑里之
囚引躬自咎卒之能脫禍患者得非禮謙所致
哉雖然大傳於此亦自處憂患者而言耳要之
人身自不可一日而無禮亦不可一日而不謙
也此學易者之所當知
書
允釐百工庶績咸熙
周孚先
同考試官教諭林批發允釐意思最爲切當且筆力
punctuated:
而光哉？誠以尊不本於謙者，則驕矜自肆，難乎其有光也。惟謙以自卑，雖位居崇高，首出乎庶物也，而不操上人之心；雖身處盛滿，禮絕乎百僚也，而恒存下人之念。尊則尊矣，然人之望之也，益見其道德之盛，光輝發越，自有不容掩矣；人之仰之也，愈見其事業之隆，光明俊偉，自有不可遏矣。其光顯也何如！夫履和而至，可見履德之妙；謙尊而光，可見謙德之妙。以之而處憂患也，何有哉？所以然者，蓋有禮則安，無禮則危；謙則受益，滿則招損，其理有固然者。故羑里之囚，引躬自咎，卒之能脫禍患者，得非禮謙所致哉？雖然，《大傳》於此亦自處憂患者而言耳。要之，人身自不可一日而無禮，亦不可一日而不謙也。此學《易》者之所當知。
書
允釐百工，庶績咸熙。
周孚先
同考試官教諭林批：發允釐意思，最爲切當，且筆力
translation_en:
…and radiant? Truly, when honor is not grounded in modesty, one becomes arrogant and unrestrained; it is difficult for such honor to possess radiance. Only through modesty does one humble oneself: though occupying an exalted position, standing foremost among all beings, one harbors no desire to place oneself above others; though enjoying the fullness of eminence, with ceremonial honors surpassing those of all officials, one constantly retains the intention of placing oneself below others. Honored one certainly is; yet the more people look toward such a person, the more they perceive the abundance of his moral virtue, its radiance shining forth with a brilliance that cannot be concealed. The more people look up to him, the more they perceive the grandeur of his accomplishments, splendid and magnificent, with a brilliance that cannot be checked. How manifest is that radiance!
That Treading is harmonious and reaches perfection reveals the subtle excellence of the virtue of Treading; that Modesty is honored and radiant reveals the subtle excellence of the virtue of Modesty. What difficulty could there be in facing adversity through these virtues? The reason is that ritual propriety brings security, while its absence brings danger; modesty brings benefit, while self-satisfaction invites loss. These principles are inherent and unchanging. Thus the prisoner at Youli examined himself and accepted the blame, and ultimately escaped calamity: was this not brought about by ritual propriety and modesty? Nevertheless, the Great Commentary here speaks specifically from the standpoint of one facing adversity. Fundamentally, a person cannot pass a single day without ritual propriety, nor a single day without modesty. This is what students of the Book of Changes ought to know.
Book of Documents
“He faithfully regulated the hundred officials, and all achievements flourished.”
Zhou Fuxian

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
老成佳士也
考試官敎諭張批詞不煩而理自足獨見此篇
考試官敎諭應批說允釐咸熈宏贍渾融宛然唐虞氣象

不本於是乎昔帝堯命羲和之意若曰授時莫
先於作曆正曆莫要於置閏閏置則四時可定
矣歲功可成矣由是內而以此昭示于朝廷使
百揆四岳以及乎庶尹率屬興事皆有定志焉
===
外而以此頒告于邦國使州牧侯伯以達乎諸
侯導民赴功均有常期焉時始乎春春之月不
入于夏治民事者得以協乎天時無慢令也歲
在乎子子之月不入于丑亮天工者得以偕乎
天運無忒政也夫然後天之所以示乎人者有
所考寒暑不至於反易而凡對時而育萬物者
亹亹乎其有成作訛成易吾知其畢舉矣人之
所以合乎天者無所違名實不至於乖戾而凡
惟時而撫五辰者循循乎其有序禮樂刑政吾
punctuated:
老成，佳士也。
考試官敎諭張批：詞不煩而理自足，獨見此篇。
考試官敎諭應批：說允釐咸熈，宏贍渾融，宛然唐虞氣象。

Examiner Zhang, an Instructor, comments: “Only in this essay do I find language that is economical yet fully expresses the underlying principles.”
Examiner Ying, an Instructor, comments: “Its explanation of ‘duly ordering’ and ‘all flourishing’ is expansive, rich, and thoroughly integrated, vividly evoking the age of Tang and Yu.”
To implement the method of intercalation and thereby bring the achievements of government to completion—this was the purpose of the sage ruler’s charge to his calendrical officials. Once intercalation is implemented, undertakings can proceed at their proper times. Can it be said that the completion of good government’s achievements is not grounded in this? The intent of Emperor Yao’s charge to Xi and He in ancient times was as though he had said:
“In giving the people their seasons, nothing takes precedence over making a calendar; in correcting the calendar, nothing is more essential than inserting intercalary months. Once these are inserted, the four seasons can be fixed and the year’s work completed. Accordingly, make this clearly known within the court, so that the Chief Minister, the Four Mountains, and all the chief officers below them may lead their subordinates in undertaking their duties, each with a settled purpose. Promulgate it outward to the states, so that the regional governors and leaders of the lords, down to all the regional lords, may guide the people in their work, all with regular appointed times.
“The seasons begin with spring. If the months of spring do not encroach upon summer, those who administer the people’s affairs can accord with Heaven’s seasons, with no dilatory commands. The year is reckoned by zi [?]. If the month of zi does not encroach upon chou, those who assist in Heaven’s work can keep pace with Heaven’s movement, with no errors in government. Only then can what Heaven reveals to humanity be verified, and cold and heat will not be reversed. All who nurture the myriad things in accordance with the seasons will diligently bring their work to fruition. Initiation, transformation, maturation, and rest—I know that all will be duly accomplished. Humanity’s conformity with Heaven will then suffer no deviation, and names and realities will not fall into discord. All who attend to the seasons and regulate the five celestial markers will proceed in orderly sequence. As for rites, music, punishments, and government, I…”

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
知其四達矣春而春夏而夏莫不以時而卽敘
先時後時之典有或干乎子而子丑而丑莫不
以歲而質成三載九載之績有弗庸乎吾之所
以欲汝置閏者有如此羲和當知舉其職矣嗟
夫曆象者聖人治天下之重務也蓋曆象立而
後天人合天人合而法制一法制一而政事脩
道化成矣今觀虞史堯典不數百言而命羲和
者乃居其半焉豈敬天勤民之政固有不可後
者歟及帝舜受終卽書在璿璣玉衡以齊七政
===
益可見矣故曰堯舜之知急先務也
何擇非人何敬非刑何度非及
黃鶴齡
同考試官教諭林批穆王訓刑本意發明殆盡
考試官教諭張批寫出穆王仁厚之心可取
考試官教諭應批說盡穆王訓刑安民之心周家仁厚
猶可想見
啓安民之端而著安民之實賢王告諸侯祥刑
然也蓋擇人敬刑而度所及所以安民也於是
punctuated:
知其四達矣。春而春，夏而夏，莫不以時而卽敘，先時後時之典有或干乎？子而子，丑而丑，莫不以歲而質成，三載九載之績有弗庸乎？吾之所以欲汝置閏者有如此，羲和當知舉其職矣。嗟夫！曆象者，聖人治天下之重務也。蓋曆象立而後天人合，天人合而法制一，法制一而政事脩，道化成矣。今觀虞史《堯典》，不數百言，而命羲和者乃居其半焉，豈敬天勤民之政固有不可後者歟？及帝舜受終，卽書「在璿璣玉衡，以齊七政」，益可見矣。故曰：「堯舜之知，急先務也。」

何擇非人？何敬非刑？何度非及？
黃鶴齡

同考試官教諭林批：「穆王訓刑本意，發明殆盡。」
考試官教諭張批：「寫出穆王仁厚之心，可取。」
考試官教諭應批：「說盡穆王訓刑安民之心，周家仁厚猶可想見。」

啓安民之端，而著安民之實，賢王告諸侯祥刑然也。蓋擇人、敬刑而度所及，所以安民也。於是
translation_en:
…I know that they will prevail in all four directions. Spring is observed as spring, and summer as summer; everything takes its proper place according to the season. Could anyone then incur the penalties for anticipating or falling behind the proper time? The zi month is observed as zi, and the chou month as chou; accomplishments are assessed according to the year. Could achievements over three years and nine years then go unrewarded? Such are my reasons for wishing you to intercalate months. Xi and He should understand how to discharge their offices.

Ah! Calculating the calendar and observing the heavens are weighty responsibilities in the sage’s governance of the world. Only when these are established do Heaven and humanity accord. When Heaven and humanity accord, laws and institutions are unified; when laws and institutions are unified, governmental affairs are put in order, and transformation through the Way is accomplished. Now consider the “Canon of Yao” in the historical records of Yu: it contains no more than a few hundred words, yet the commands to Xi and He occupy half of it. Surely this is because policies that revere Heaven and diligently care for the people cannot be postponed? When Emperor Shun received the succession, the text immediately records that he “examined the jewel-adorned celestial mechanism and jade transverse tube, to bring the seven celestial governors into accord.” This makes the point still clearer. Thus it is said: “The wisdom of Yao and Shun lay in attending urgently to the foremost duties.”

“What is to be selected, if not men? What is to be treated with reverence, if not punishments? What is to be weighed, if not their consequences?”
By Huang Heling.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The original intent of King Mu’s instructions on punishments is elucidated almost exhaustively.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “It brings out King Mu’s benevolent and generous heart; this is commendable.”
Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: “It fully explains King Mu’s intention to bring peace to the people through his instructions on punishments. The benevolence and generosity of the house of Zhou can still be envisioned.”

To open the way toward bringing peace to the people and to make manifest its actual realization—such was the worthy king’s purpose in instructing the feudal lords on the beneficent use of punishments. For selecting men, treating punishments with reverence, and weighing their consequences are the means of bringing peace to the people. In these matters…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而能盡心焉祥刑之道備矣昔穆王訓刑及此
意謂凡我有邦有土旣知祥刑在於安百姓矣
可不盡心於所事乎是故遇物而辨擇之謂也
今則何者在所擇歟亦曰任官以司法若士師
若鄉士若遂士莫非人也始必詢之於眾察之
於獨豈弟每得以登庸苛薄不容於雜進可也
不然官將具而弗稱矣所謂當擇者非人乎臨
事而謹敬之謂也今則何者在所敬歟亦曰制
法以齊民若墨劓若剕宮若大辟孰非刑也始
===
必上嚴天命下恤民生悉聰明於參聽之始致
忠愛於論斷之時可也不然刑將縱而弗平矣
所謂當敬者非刑乎若夫因情以求其類度之
謂也今則何者在所度歟亦曰治獄以懲惡或
以詞證或以援據恒有所及也又必審其出入
量其取舍有罪不得以輕宥無辜不敢以濫及
可也不然刑將僭而無節矣所謂當度者非及
乎夫盡心以擇人則民親上敬刑則民愛生度
所及則民勸善信乎百姓安而刑祥矣抑於是
punctuated: 而能盡心焉，祥刑之道備矣。昔穆王訓刑及此，意謂凡我有邦有土，旣知祥刑在於安百姓矣，可不盡心於所事乎？是故遇物而辨，擇之謂也。今則何者在所擇歟？亦曰任官以司法，若士師，若鄉士，若遂士，莫非人也。始必詢之於眾，察之於獨，豈弟每得以登庸，苛薄不容於雜進，可也。不然，官將具而弗稱矣。所謂當擇者，非人乎？臨事而謹，敬之謂也。今則何者在所敬歟？亦曰制法以齊民，若墨劓，若剕宮，若大辟，孰非刑也？始必上嚴天命，下恤民生，悉聰明於參聽之始，致忠愛於論斷之時，可也。不然，刑將縱而弗平矣。所謂當敬者，非刑乎？若夫因情以求其類，度之謂也。今則何者在所度歟？亦曰治獄以懲惡，或以詞證，或以援據，恒有所及也。又必審其出入，量其取舍，有罪不得以輕宥，無辜不敢以濫及，可也。不然，刑將僭而無節矣。所謂當度者，非及乎？夫盡心以擇人，則民親上；敬刑，則民愛生；度所及，則民勸善。信乎百姓安而刑祥矣！抑於是
translation_en:
…and if one can devote one's whole mind to these matters, the way of making punishments beneficent is complete. When King Mu reached this point in his instructions on punishments, his meaning was: “All of you who possess states and territories already know that making punishments beneficent consists in bringing peace to the common people. Can you fail to devote your whole minds to your duties?” Thus, to distinguish among things as one encounters them is what is meant by selection. What, then, is to be selected? It is a matter of appointing officials to administer the law: judicial officers (shishi), district judicial officers (xiangshi), and outer-district judicial officers (suishi) are all people. At the outset, one must consult others about them and examine their conduct in private, so that the kindly and amiable may always be raised to office, while the harsh and ungenerous are not allowed to slip in among them. Otherwise, the offices will be filled, but their occupants will not be equal to their duties. Are not people, then, what must be selected?

To act cautiously when confronting affairs is what is meant by reverence. What, then, is to be treated with reverence? It is a matter of establishing laws to bring the people into order: tattooing and cutting off the nose, amputation of the foot and castration, and execution—are these not all punishments? At the outset, one must revere Heaven's mandate above and show compassion for the people's lives below, bringing all one's powers of hearing and discernment to bear when first weighing the testimony, and exercising the utmost conscientiousness and benevolence when deliberating and passing judgment. Otherwise, punishments will be applied without restraint or equity. Are not punishments, then, what must be treated with reverence?

As for seeking comparable cases in light of the circumstances, this is what is meant by weighing. What, then, is to be weighed? It is a matter of adjudicating cases to punish wrongdoing: whether proceeding through testimony and corroboration or through cited grounds, punishment invariably reaches someone. One must also scrutinize the grounds for acquittal or conviction and weigh what to accept or reject, so that the guilty are not lightly pardoned and one does not dare indiscriminately to implicate the innocent. Otherwise, punishments will exceed their proper bounds and lack moderation. Is not the reach of punishment, then, what must be weighed?

If one devotes one's whole mind to selecting people, the people will feel affection for their superiors; if one treats punishments with reverence, the people will cherish life; if one weighs whom punishment reaches, the people will be encouraged toward goodness. Truly, the common people will enjoy peace and punishments will be beneficent! Moreover, from this…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而知穆王訓刑之善焉何者用刑之不善者法
立未嘗不善也用心之不善耳故私心間而小
人進怠心生而天德微忮心行而民命蹙反是
而求盡心焉穆王之善訓也雖其制刑有非先
王之舊而欽恤之遺意猶若未泯嗚呼孔子所
以不得不錄其書也
詩
葛之覃兮施于中谷維葉萋萋黃鳥于飛
集于灌木其鳴喈喈
鄧直卿
同考試官訓導黃批能分葛葉黃鳥輕重而文體整齊
場中無如此者
同考試官教諭朱批能玩味傳中黃鳥鳴于其上而為文是
可錄矣
同考試官學正李批后妃既成絺綌而追叙葛方盛時乃
以黃鳥附之必有說矣此作獨能知之
考試官教諭張批文不重疊而理亦明白錄之
考試官教諭應批講葛葉黃鳥得后妃本意可取
punctuated:
而知穆王訓刑之善焉。何者？用刑之不善者，法立未嘗不善也，用心之不善耳。故私心間而小人進，怠心生而天德微，忮心行而民命蹙。反是而求盡心焉，穆王之善訓也。雖其制刑有非先王之舊，而欽恤之遺意猶若未泯。嗚呼！孔子所以不得不錄其書也。

詩

葛之覃兮，施于中谷，維葉萋萋。黃鳥于飛，集于灌木，其鳴喈喈。

鄧直卿

同考試官訓導黃批：能分葛葉黃鳥輕重，而文體整齊，場中無如此者。

同考試官教諭朱批：能玩味傳中黃鳥鳴于其上而為文，是可錄矣。

同考試官學正李批：后妃既成絺綌，而追叙葛方盛時，乃以黃鳥附之，必有說矣。此作獨能知之。

考試官教諭張批：文不重疊，而理亦明白，錄之。

考試官教諭應批：講葛葉黃鳥，得后妃本意，可取。
translation_en:
…and thus we recognize the excellence of King Mu’s instructions on punishments. Why is this?
