When punishments are badly administered, it is not that the laws as established were bad, but merely that the intentions governing their application are bad. Thus, when selfish motives intrude, petty men advance; when indolence arises, heavenly virtue wanes; when malice prevails, the people’s lives are imperiled. To reverse these tendencies and seek to exert one’s heart to the utmost: this is the excellence of King Mu’s instruction. Although his penal institutions departed in some respects from the ancient practices of the former kings, the spirit of reverence and compassion they had bequeathed seems not yet to have vanished. Ah! This is why Confucius could not but include this document.

Book of Odes

“How the kudzu vines extend,
Spreading through the valley’s midst!
Their leaves are lush and thick.
Yellow birds fly about,
Alighting on the bushy trees;
Their calls are harmonious.”

Deng Zhiqing

Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “He distinguishes the relative importance of the kudzu leaves and the yellow birds, and the composition is orderly and balanced. No other essay in this examination matches it.”

Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “He has pondered the commentary’s statement that the yellow birds sing above them and developed his essay from it. This merits selection.”

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “After completing the fine and coarse kudzu cloth, the queen consort looked back to the time when the kudzu was flourishing and included the yellow birds in her account. There must be a reason for this. This essay alone understands it.”

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The composition is not repetitive, and its reasoning is clear. Select it.”

Examiner Ying, Instructor, comments: “Its discussion of the kudzu leaves and the yellow birds captures the queen consort’s original intent. It merits acceptance.”

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
賢妃追敘植物方盛而致動物之適情以見女
工之所自也夫葛葉方盛則女工將有所施而
黃鳥來鳴又因葛而知其所止者也旣成女工
者得不追敘以爲言哉昔后妃旣成絺綌而賦
其事其追敘之意若曰葛雖成於盛夏而實始
於前時當夫初夏之際有葛生焉布濩覃延旣
引夫不絕之蔓纏綿依附且移于中谷之間觀
其葉則萋萋然挹雨露之霑濡而發榮滋長之
性何其茂也飽土膏之饒洽而憔悴隕籜之形
===
未之見焉是葛葉也刈濩之具絺綌之資不已
權輿於此乎適夫葛生之時有黃鳥焉熠燿其
羽載飛于陽和之天翔而後集斂翼于灌木之
上聽其鳴則喈喈然肆求友之聲而地之向遠
者無乎不達也調如簧之舌而人之有耳者皆
所共聞焉是黃鳥也安於所寓得其所止不因
葛葉而來乎夫以植物方盛則絺綌之功固有
以知其端動物來鳴則葛葉之生因有以驗其
盛后妃旣成女工而追敘及此豈非不忘所自
punctuated: 賢妃追敘植物方盛，而致動物之適情，以見女工之所自也。夫葛葉方盛，則女工將有所施；而黃鳥來鳴，又因葛而知其所止者也。旣成女工者，得不追敘以爲言哉？昔后妃旣成絺綌而賦其事，其追敘之意若曰：「葛雖成於盛夏，而實始於前時。當夫初夏之際，有葛生焉，布濩覃延，旣引夫不絕之蔓；纏綿依附，且移于中谷之間。觀其葉，則萋萋然，挹雨露之霑濡，而發榮滋長之性，何其茂也！飽土膏之饒洽，而憔悴隕籜之形，未之見焉。是葛葉也，刈濩之具，絺綌之資，不已權輿於此乎？適夫葛生之時，有黃鳥焉，熠燿其羽，載飛于陽和之天；翔而後集，斂翼于灌木之上。聽其鳴，則喈喈然，肆求友之聲，而地之向遠者，無乎不達也；調如簧之舌，而人之有耳者，皆所共聞焉。是黃鳥也，安於所寓，得其所止，不因葛葉而來乎？」夫以植物方盛，則絺綌之功，固有以知其端；動物來鳴，則葛葉之生，因有以驗其盛。后妃旣成女工而追敘及此，豈非不忘所自
translation_en:
The worthy consort recalls the flourishing of plant life and evokes the contentment of animal life, thereby showing the origins of women’s textile work. When the kudzu leaves flourish, women’s work will soon find its material; and the orioles that come singing likewise find, through the kudzu, the place in which to settle. Having completed her textile work, could she fail to recall these things and put them into words?

In former times, when the queen-consort had finished making fine and coarse kudzu cloth, she composed a poem about the undertaking. The meaning of her recollection was as though she said: “Although kudzu matures in high summer, its beginnings lie earlier. At the onset of summer, kudzu grows, spreading and extending, sending out unbroken vines; twining and clinging, it reaches into the midst of the valley. Look at its leaves: how luxuriant they are! Drinking in the moisture of rain and dew, they express their nature in flowering and growth—how abundant! Nourished fully by the rich fertility of the soil, they show no sign of withering or shedding their sheaths. In these kudzu leaves, have not the materials to be cut and boiled, the resources for fine and coarse cloth, already had their beginnings?

“Just when the kudzu grows, orioles appear, their feathers gleaming as they fly through the mild, sunny sky. After wheeling about, they alight, folding their wings atop the shrubs. Listen to their harmonious calls! They freely send forth their voices in search of companions, reaching even the distant places [?]. They tune their reed-like tongues, and all who have ears can hear them. These orioles, at ease in their abode and having found a place to settle—have they not come because of the kudzu leaves?”

Thus, from the flourishing of plant life, one can discern the beginnings of the work of making fine and coarse kudzu cloth; and from the arrival and song of animal life, one can in turn confirm the luxuriance of the kudzu leaves. When the queen-consort, having completed her textile work, recalled matters as far back as these, was it not that she did not forget its origins …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
者哉抑考葛覃之詩后妃所自作而無贊美之
詞然其勤儉孝敬之德悉具焉宜其配至尊而
爲宗廟主也桃夭兔罝芣苢之風漢廣汝墳之
化曾謂無所本哉嗚呼文王身脩家齊之效亦
可見矣雖然內有賢妃所以助之者深虞之二
女夏之塗山殷之有娀周之太姒其致一也讀
是詩者又當知周之所以興乎
明明天子令聞不已
潘大賓
===
同考試官訓導黃批不已處得穆公之心可謂善說詩者
同考試官教諭朱批講不已最是
同考試官學正李批令聞不已含下文矢文德洽四國之
意此作得之
考試官教諭張批說明君穆公愛君之心錄之
考試官教諭應批穆公以文德望其君此作發揚盡矣
大臣贊中興之賢君益中興之善譽蓋善譽固
難而益之尤可尚也古人於君美而進之如此
忠愛之心何如哉昔宣王命召穆公平淮南之
punctuated:
者哉？抑考《葛覃》之詩，后妃所自作，而無贊美之詞，然其勤儉孝敬之德悉具焉，宜其配至尊而爲宗廟主也。《桃夭》《兔罝》《芣苢》之風，《漢廣》《汝墳》之化，曾謂無所本哉？嗚呼！文王身脩家齊之效，亦可見矣。雖然，內有賢妃，所以助之者深。虞之二女，夏之塗山，殷之有娀，周之太姒，其致一也。讀是詩者，又當知周之所以興乎！
明明天子，令聞不已。
潘大賓
同考試官訓導黃批：「不已處得穆公之心，可謂善說詩者。」
同考試官教諭朱批：「講不已最是。」
同考試官學正李批：「令聞不已，含下文矢文德、洽四國之意，此作得之。」
考試官教諭張批：「說明君穆公愛君之心，錄之。」
考試官教諭應批：「穆公以文德望其君，此作發揚盡矣。」
大臣贊中興之賢君，益中興之善譽。蓋善譽固難，而益之尤可尚也。古人於君，美而進之如此，忠愛之心何如哉！昔宣王命召穆公平淮南之
translation_en:
…was she not such a person? Moreover, examining the poem “The Spreading Kudzu” (Ge tan), we find that the queen composed it herself, with no words of praise for herself; yet her diligence, frugality, filial devotion, and reverence are all embodied in it. Fittingly, she became the consort of the supreme sovereign and presided over the ancestral temple. Could the moral influence seen in “The Peach Tree” (Tao yao), “The Rabbit Nets” (Tu ju), and “Plantain” (Fu yi), and the transforming influence seen in “The Broad Han” (Han guang) and “The Banks of the Ru” (Ru fen), possibly have had no source? Ah! Here too we can see the results of King Wen’s cultivation of himself and ordering of his household. Nevertheless, within the palace he had a worthy consort whose assistance was profound. The two daughters of Yu, Tushan of Xia, Yousong of Yin, and Tai Si of Zhou were alike in this respect. Those who read this poem should also understand why Zhou rose to power!

“Illustrious is the Son of Heaven; his good renown never ceases.”
Pan Dabin

Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The treatment of ‘never ceases’ captures Duke Mu’s intention. He may be called a skilled interpreter of the Poetry.”

Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “The explanation of ‘never ceases’ is particularly apt.”

Associate Examiner Li, School Instructor, comments: “‘His good renown never ceases’ contains the meaning of the subsequent words about displaying civil virtue and bringing harmony to the states of the four quarters. This composition captures it.”

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “It explains the enlightened ruler and Duke Mu’s love for his ruler [?]. Selected for inclusion.”

Examiner Ying, Instructor, comments: “Duke Mu expected civil virtue of his ruler. This composition brings out that meaning fully.”

A great minister praises the worthy ruler who has restored the dynasty, encouraging him to enhance the good renown of that restoration. For good renown is certainly difficult to attain, and enhancing it is still more worthy of esteem. The ancients praised their rulers and urged them onward in this way: how great was their loyal affection! Formerly, King Xuan commanded Duke Mu of Shao to pacify the peoples south of the Huai…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
夷詩人美之至此則述穆公美其君而進之之
詞若曰王業必底於大成治道不貴於自足我
明明之天子也遠紹文武之顯承而煥重明於
五位近纘成康之熈洽而炳離照於九重旁燭
無疆誠不世出之主光被四表實大有爲之君
誠以興師江漢則跋扈來歸而乾坤有再造之
績赫赫厥聲洋溢遐邇可謂有令聞矣且將如
日方升有隆而未艾用兵淮夷則桀驁內附而
日月啓重光之運濯濯厥靈流布夷夏是固有
===
善譽矣殆必如川方至有增而不已圖關長治
之謀而充拓光前之業頌於今而曰興衰者播
揚於後日則曰中國之聖人焉慮切乂安之計
而恢弘裕後之規稱於今而曰撥亂者膾炙於
方來則曰太平之令主焉是則致令聞者固在
於武功之成益令聞者又出於武功之外也吾
王庶幾以文德而加之意哉考之舞干羽而有
苗格退脩教而崇侯降聖帝明王雖用兵之際
猶以文德爲本况武功旣成之後而可不濟之
punctuated: 夷，詩人美之。至此，則述穆公美其君而進之之詞，若曰：「王業必底於大成，治道不貴於自足。我明明之天子也，遠紹文武之顯承，而煥重明於五位；近纘成康之熈洽，而炳離照於九重。旁燭無疆，誠不世出之主；光被四表，實大有爲之君。誠以興師江漢，則跋扈來歸，而乾坤有再造之績，赫赫厥聲，洋溢遐邇，可謂有令聞矣；且將如日方升，有隆而未艾。用兵淮夷，則桀驁內附，而日月啓重光之運，濯濯厥靈，流布夷夏，是固有善譽矣；殆必如川方至，有增而不已。圖關長治之謀，而充拓光前之業，頌於今而曰興衰者，播揚於後日，則曰中國之聖人焉；慮切乂安之計，而恢弘裕後之規，稱於今而曰撥亂者，膾炙於方來，則曰太平之令主焉。是則致令聞者，固在於武功之成；益令聞者，又出於武功之外也。吾王庶幾以文德而加之意哉！考之，舞干羽而有苗格，退脩教而崇侯降。聖帝明王，雖用兵之際，猶以文德爲本；况武功旣成之後，而可不濟之
translation_en:
…the Yi peoples, and the poet praised him for it. At this point, however, the poem recounts the words with which Duke Mu praised his ruler and urged him onward, as though saying: “The royal enterprise must attain its full accomplishment; the way of government does not prize self-satisfaction. O our illustrious Son of Heaven! Looking far back, you continue the glorious heritage of Kings Wen and Wu, making renewed brilliance shine from the sovereign’s fifth position; looking to the nearer past, you carry on the flourishing harmony of Kings Cheng and Kang, casting radiant illumination from the ninefold palace. Your light shines in every direction without limit: truly you are a ruler rarely seen in any age. Your radiance reaches beyond the four bounds: indeed you are a sovereign capable of great achievements.

“When you raised armies in the Jiang and Han regions, the unruly submitted, and you achieved the re-creation of heaven and earth. Your resounding renown spread far and near: this may well be called an excellent reputation. Moreover, like the sun just rising, it will grow in splendor without yet reaching its limit. When you campaigned against the Huai Yi, the recalcitrant pledged allegiance, and the sun and moon inaugurated an era of renewed brilliance. Your manifest majesty spread among both the Yi peoples and the Xia: this surely constitutes a fine reputation. Like a river whose waters are just arriving, it must surely increase without cease.

“Devise plans that secure lasting good government, and expand the achievements that bring glory to your predecessors. Those who praise you today as one who revives what has declined will spread your fame in later days, calling you the sage of the Central States. Give earnest thought to measures for peace and order, and enlarge the designs that provide abundantly for posterity. Those who commend you today as one who puts down disorder will celebrate you in the future as the excellent ruler of an age of great peace.

“Thus, winning an excellent reputation certainly depends upon the accomplishment of military achievements; increasing that reputation, however, extends beyond military achievements. May our king give thought to augmenting it through civil virtue! Consider the precedents: when shields and feather plumes were wielded in a dance, the Youmiao submitted; when the ruler withdrew and cultivated moral instruction, the Marquis of Chong surrendered. Sagely emperors and enlightened kings took civil virtue as their foundation even while employing armies. How much more, once military achievements have been completed, could one fail to complement them …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以文以消其窮黷之心以衍太平之業乎此忠
愛之穆公所以拳拳於令聞不已進其君而必
繼之以矢其文德洽此四國也嗚呼宣王卒爲
有周中興之賢主者謂召穆公無少助焉可乎
春秋
盟于召陵齊人執陳轅濤塗秋及江
人黃人伐陳冬十有二月公孫玆帥
師會齊人宋人衛人鄭人許人曹人侵
陳〔俱僖公四年〕
===
劉一松
同考試官教諭王批太傅於齊桓服楚虐陳得失
自見此作援引曲制明白有學之士也
考試官教諭張批通暢可取
考試官教諭應批得謹嚴之體可錄
霸事有近於王者春秋序其績霸德有歉於王
者春秋重其譏此桓公不戰以服楚庶幾王者
之事而逞威以虐陳殊無王者之德也春秋予
奪之宜哉且屈完觀師結盟而退則桓之伐楚
punctuated:
以文，以消其窮黷之心，以衍太平之業乎？此忠愛之穆公所以拳拳於令聞，不已進其君，而必繼之以矢其文德，洽此四國也。嗚呼！宣王卒爲有周中興之賢主者，謂召穆公無少助焉，可乎？

春秋

盟于召陵。齊人執陳轅濤塗。秋，及江人、黃人伐陳。冬，十有二月，公孫玆帥師，會齊人、宋人、衛人、鄭人、許人、曹人侵陳。〔俱僖公四年〕

劉一松

同考試官教諭王批：「太傅於齊桓服楚虐陳，得失自見。此作援引曲制，明白有學之士也。」

考試官教諭張批：「通暢可取。」

考試官教諭應批：「得謹嚴之體，可錄。」

霸事有近於王者，春秋序其績；霸德有歉於王者，春秋重其譏。此桓公不戰以服楚，庶幾王者之事；而逞威以虐陳，殊無王者之德也。春秋予奪之宜哉！且屈完觀師，結盟而退，則桓之伐楚
translation_en:
…with civil virtue, to dispel his inclination toward exhausting his resources in incessant warfare and to extend the achievement of great peace? This is why Duke Mu, in his loyalty and affection, was so deeply concerned for his ruler’s good reputation: he never ceased urging his ruler onward, and insisted on following this with the injunction to display his civil virtue and bring harmony to the states throughout the four quarters. Ah! King Xuan ultimately became the worthy ruler who restored the fortunes of Zhou. Could one say that Duke Mu of Shao contributed nothing to this?

Spring and Autumn Annals

They concluded a covenant at Shaoling. The men of Qi seized Yuan Taotu of Chen. In autumn, together with the men of Jiang and Huang, they attacked Chen. In winter, in the twelfth month, Gongsun Ci led an army and joined the men of Qi, Song, Wei, Zheng, Xu, and Cao in invading Chen. 〔All these entries are from the fourth year of Duke Xi.〕

Liu Yisong

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The Grand Preceptor [?]: in Duke Huan of Qi’s subduing Chu and maltreating Chen, the merits and faults are evident of themselves. This composition’s citations and construction [?] clearly show that its author is a man of learning.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Fluent and clear; worthy of acceptance.”

Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: “It achieves a careful and rigorous style; fit for selection.”

When a hegemon’s deeds approach those of a true king, the Spring and Autumn Annals records his achievements; when a hegemon’s virtue falls short of that of a true king, the Spring and Autumn Annals censures him severely. Thus Duke Huan’s subduing Chu without battle came close to the deeds of a true king; yet in flaunting his might to maltreat Chen, he showed none of a true king’s virtue. How fitting are the praise and blame bestowed by the Spring and Autumn Annals! Moreover, Qu Wan inspected the army, concluded a covenant, and withdrew; thus Duke Huan’s expedition against Chu…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
固未大挫也春秋予之何耶誠以脩德來遠王
者之事也伐楚之役語兵力則已强矣語敵國
則已服矣在常情孰不欲一戰以取捷也而桓
也從容退舍盟好是脩兵雖强也以律用之而
不暴敵已服也以禮下之而不驕其心必曰善
爲國者不師善師者不陣善陣者不戰吾何以
勝楚爲哉噫舞干而苗格者舜也因壘而崇降
者文王也桓之服楚殆庶幾乎故春秋特書盟
于召陵所以序其績者如此迨夫齊欲徑陳陳
===
不果納則桓之怒陳似未爲過也春秋奪之何
耶誠以敬愼不渝王者之德也召陵之盟語其
志則已得矣語其功則已盛矣在君子必將益
脩德以保終也而桓也驕心一生舉動頓異執
濤塗未已也復合兵以伐其國伐其國未足也
復潛師以掠其境曾不思曰愛人不親反其仁
治人不治反其智禮人不答反其敬吾何以責
陳爲哉噫勝夏而慄慄危懼成湯也東征而四
國是皇周公也桓之虐陳寧無歉乎故春秋始
punctuated:
固未大挫也，春秋予之何耶？誠以脩德來遠，王者之事也。伐楚之役，語兵力則已强矣，語敵國則已服矣。在常情，孰不欲一戰以取捷也？而桓也從容退舍，盟好是脩。兵雖强也，以律用之而不暴；敵已服也，以禮下之而不驕。其心必曰：「善爲國者不師，善師者不陣，善陣者不戰，吾何以勝楚爲哉？」噫！舞干而苗格者，舜也；因壘而崇降者，文王也。桓之服楚，殆庶幾乎！故春秋特書「盟于召陵」，所以序其績者如此。
迨夫齊欲徑陳，陳不果納，則桓之怒陳似未爲過也，春秋奪之何耶？誠以敬愼不渝，王者之德也。召陵之盟，語其志則已得矣，語其功則已盛矣。在君子，必將益脩德以保終也。而桓也驕心一生，舉動頓異。執濤塗未已也，復合兵以伐其國；伐其國未足也，復潛師以掠其境。曾不思曰：「愛人不親，反其仁；治人不治，反其智；禮人不答，反其敬。吾何以責陳爲哉？」噫！勝夏而慄慄危懼，成湯也；東征而四國是皇，周公也。桓之虐陳，寧無歉乎？故春秋始
translation_en:
…had certainly not inflicted a major defeat [on Chu?]. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals accord him approval? It is because cultivating virtue to attract those from afar is the work of a true king. In the campaign against Chu, his military strength was already formidable, and the opposing state had already submitted. According to ordinary human feelings, who would not have wished to win a victory in battle? Yet Duke Huan calmly withdrew his army and cultivated amicable relations through a covenant. Though his forces were strong, he employed them with discipline and without violence; though his enemy had submitted, he humbly treated it with ritual propriety and without arrogance. In his heart he must have said: “One skilled in governing a state does not resort to armies; one skilled in employing armies does not draw up battle formations; one skilled in battle formations does not fight. What need have I to defeat Chu?” Ah! It was Shun whose shield dance brought the Miao to submit; it was King Wen whose use of the existing siege works brought Chong to surrender. Duke Huan’s subjugation of Chu came close to these achievements! Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals expressly records, “They made a covenant at Shaoling.” Such is the way it records his accomplishment.
When Qi wished to pass through Chen, and Chen ultimately did not admit its forces, Duke Huan’s anger at Chen seemed not excessive. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals withhold its approval? It is because unwavering reverence and caution are the virtues of a true king. At the covenant of Shaoling, his ambition had already been fulfilled, and his achievement was already splendid. A gentleman would surely have cultivated his virtue still further to preserve a worthy conclusion. Yet once arrogance arose in Duke Huan’s heart, his conduct abruptly changed. Not content with seizing Taotu, he again assembled troops to attack Taotu’s state; not content with attacking that state, he again secretly dispatched troops to plunder its territory. He never thought to say: “If I love others and they do not draw close to me, I should examine my own benevolence; if I govern others and they remain ungoverned, I should examine my own wisdom; if I treat others with ritual propriety and they do not reciprocate, I should examine my own respectfulness. What grounds have I to blame Chen?” Ah! It was Cheng Tang who, after defeating Xia, trembled with apprehension; it was the Duke of Zhou whose eastern campaign awed the four states. Could Duke Huan’s mistreatment of Chen have been without shortcomings? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals first…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而稱人繼而書侵所以重其譏者又如此嗟夫
莫貴於王莫賤於霸王者之可貴規模宏大而
憂樂吉凶不足以動其方寸也霸者之可賤識
量淺狹而勝負得喪足以移其常心也王霸之
分大率如此然究其歸則在誠與僞之間耳故
曰以德行仁者王以力假仁者霸假之一字深
得春秋誅心之法
楚子伐鄭晉郤缺帥師救鄭宣公九年楚
子伐鄭宣公十年
===
周舜卿
同考試官教諭王批謹夷夏之防明君臣之義爲主能
玩詞同意異之傳是可錄矣
考試官教諭張批得春秋屬比之意
考試官教諭應批合傳可取
春秋貶外夷虐貳而錄內救以見意不貶外夷
虐貳而削內救以示義觀于楚兩伐鄭而詞同
意異有以見聖人謹大防明大倫也慨昔中國
之霸緒寖微外夷之虐焰漸熾有曰楚莊崛起
punctuated:
而稱人，繼而書侵，所以重其譏者又如此。嗟夫！莫貴於王，莫賤於霸。王者之可貴，規模宏大，而憂樂吉凶不足以動其方寸也；霸者之可賤，識量淺狹，而勝負得喪足以移其常心也。王霸之分，大率如此。然究其歸，則在誠與僞之間耳。故曰：「以德行仁者王，以力假仁者霸。」假之一字，深得《春秋》誅心之法。
楚子伐鄭，晉郤缺帥師救鄭。宣公九年。楚子伐鄭。宣公十年。
周舜卿
同考試官教諭王批：「謹夷夏之防，明君臣之義爲主，能玩詞同意異之傳，是可錄矣。」
考試官教諭張批：「得《春秋》屬比之意。」
考試官教諭應批：「合傳，可取。」
《春秋》貶外夷虐貳，而錄內救以見意；不貶外夷虐貳，而削內救以示義。觀于楚兩伐鄭，而詞同意異，有以見聖人謹大防、明大倫也。慨昔中國之霸緒寖微，外夷之虐焰漸熾，有曰楚莊崛起。
translation_en:
…and designated them as “men,” then wrote “invaded”: this too was how it intensified its censure. Alas! Nothing is more estimable than true kingship, nothing more contemptible than hegemony. What makes the true king estimable is the breadth of his designs: sorrow and joy, good fortune and ill cannot disturb his heart. What makes the hegemon contemptible is the narrowness of his understanding and capacity: victory and defeat, gain and loss suffice to unsettle his constancy. Such, broadly speaking, is the distinction between kingship and hegemony. Yet traced to its ultimate basis, it lies simply between sincerity and pretence. Hence the saying: “One who practices benevolence through virtue becomes a true king; one who uses force to make a pretence of benevolence becomes a hegemon.” That single word “pretence” profoundly captures the Spring and Autumn Annals’ method of condemning underlying intentions.

“The Viscount of Chu attacked Zheng. Xi Que of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng.” Ninth year of Duke Xuan. “The Viscount of Chu attacked Zheng.” Tenth year of Duke Xuan.

Zhou Shunqing

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The principal concern is to maintain carefully the boundary between the non-Chinese peoples and the Chinese states, and to clarify the proper relationship between ruler and minister. The author can ponder the commentary’s explanation of identical wording with different meanings. This merits inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “It grasps the significance of juxtaposing related entries in the Spring and Autumn Annals.”

Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: “It accords with the commentary and is worthy of acceptance.”

The Spring and Autumn Annals censures an outside, non-Chinese power for oppressing a state of divided allegiance, and records relief by a Chinese state to reveal its intent; elsewhere it does not censure that outside power for such oppression, and omits the Chinese relief effort to disclose its judgment. In the two attacks by Chu on Zheng, the wording is identical but the meaning differs. This shows how the Sage carefully maintained the great boundary and clarified the fundamental human relationships. Alas, in those days the tradition of hegemony among the central states was gradually declining, while the flames of violence among the outside peoples grew ever fiercer. There was King Zhuang of Chu, who rose abruptly to prominence…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
爭衡魯宣九年興師伐鄭斯時也鄭無可討之
罪而楚以僭竊之夷惟欲肆其强暴以服鄭爲
事非義舉矣幸而晉成畏此簡書特遣卻缺將
兵救鄭奏凱栁棼則誠攘夷狄安諸夏之兵也
春秋欲彰楚之罪得不錄晉之善乎故於楚之
伐鄭特稱爵者傳曰貶詞也若曰國君自將恃
强壓弱憑陵中夏之稱也知然者以下書晉卻
缺帥師救鄭則貶楚可知矣聖人謹夷夏之防
蓋如此嗣是南北之干戈日尋鄭人之玉帛兩
===
事楚莊憤怒力爭經營魯宣十年復駕伐鄭斯
時也陳有弑逆之惡而晉主中夏之盟苟能奉
行天討以風示天下斯盡職矣夫何晉景舍此
大義顧命士會舉兵爭鄭宣威潁北則失誅亂
臣討賊子之義也春秋欲著晉之罪得不沒其
救乎故於楚之伐鄭亦稱爵者傳曰直詞也若
曰以實屬詞書其重者而意不以楚爲罪也知
然者以傳書晉士會救鄭而經削之則責晉可
知矣聖人明君臣之義又如此嗟夫躬天下之
punctuated:
爭衡。魯宣九年，興師伐鄭。斯時也，鄭無可討之罪，而楚以僭竊之夷，惟欲肆其强暴以服鄭爲事，非義舉矣。幸而晉成畏此簡書，特遣卻缺將兵救鄭，奏凱栁棼，則誠攘夷狄、安諸夏之兵也。《春秋》欲彰楚之罪，得不錄晉之善乎？故於楚之伐鄭特稱爵者，傳曰：「貶詞也。」若曰，國君自將，恃强壓弱，憑陵中夏之稱也。知然者，以下書晉卻缺帥師救鄭，則貶楚可知矣。聖人謹夷夏之防，蓋如此。
嗣是，南北之干戈日尋，鄭人之玉帛兩事。楚莊憤怒，力爭經營。魯宣十年，復駕伐鄭。斯時也，陳有弑逆之惡，而晉主中夏之盟，苟能奉行天討以風示天下，斯盡職矣。夫何晉景舍此大義，顧命士會舉兵爭鄭，宣威潁北，則失誅亂臣、討賊子之義也。《春秋》欲著晉之罪，得不沒其救乎？故於楚之伐鄭亦稱爵者，傳曰：「直詞也。」若曰，以實屬詞，書其重者，而意不以楚爲罪也。知然者，以傳書晉士會救鄭而經削之，則責晉可知矣。聖人明君臣之義，又如此。
嗟夫！躬天下之
translation_en:
…contended for supremacy. In the ninth year of Duke Xuan of Lu, he raised an army to attack Zheng. At that time, Zheng had committed no offense deserving punishment. Yet Chu, a barbarian state that had usurped royal authority, sought only to unleash its violence and force Zheng into submission. This was no righteous undertaking. Fortunately, Duke Cheng of Jin respected the obligations conveyed in the bamboo-strip summons and specially dispatched Que Que [?] to lead troops to Zheng’s rescue. They returned victorious from Liufen [?]; this was truly an army that repelled the barbarians and secured the Chinese states. If the Spring and Autumn Annals wished to expose Chu’s guilt, could it fail to record Jin’s good deed? Thus, when recording Chu’s attack on Zheng, it specifically designates its ruler by his noble rank. The commentary says: “This is wording of censure.” It is as though the designation says: the ruler commanded in person, relying on strength to oppress the weak and overbearing the central Chinese states. We know this because the subsequent entry records that Que Que of Jin led an army to rescue Zheng; the censure of Chu is therefore evident. Such was the sage’s care in maintaining the boundary between the barbarians and the Chinese states.
Thereafter, warfare between north and south continued daily, and the people of Zheng presented jade and silk in service to both powers. King Zhuang of Chu grew angry and exerted himself in contention and military preparations. In the tenth year of Duke Xuan of Lu, he again set out to attack Zheng. At that time, Chen was guilty of regicide and rebellion, while Jin presided over the covenant of the central Chinese states. Had Jin carried out Heaven’s punishment as an admonitory example to all under Heaven, it would have fulfilled its duty. Why, then, did Duke Jing of Jin abandon this great obligation and instead order Shi Hui to raise troops to contest possession of Zheng and display his might north of the Ying River? In doing so, he failed in the duty to execute rebellious ministers and punish treacherous sons. If the Spring and Autumn Annals wished to make Jin’s guilt manifest, could it fail to omit its rescue of Zheng? Thus, when recording Chu’s attack on Zheng, it again designates its ruler by his noble rank. The commentary says: “This is straightforward wording.” It is as though it says: the wording follows the facts and records the weightier matter, without intending to condemn Chu. We know this because the commentary records that Shi Hui of Jin rescued Zheng, whereas the canonical text omits it; the reproach directed at Jin is therefore evident. Such, too, was the sage’s way of making clear the duties between ruler and minister.
Alas! To shoulder personally the world’s…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
大難斯可以成天下之大業桓文所以得諸侯
覇天下以其内獎王室外攘夷狄剪篡鋤兇汲
汲焉躬天下之難耳奈何春秋中葉覇圖不競
靈成景弗克負荷以討賊之大權遺楚莊號令
辰陵噫此中國所以淪於夷狄而世道所以降
爲戰國也安得起桓文於九原以定安攘之計
禮記
致禮以治躬則莊敬莊敬則嚴威
舒素蘊
===
同考試官教諭唐批莊敬嚴威處至字意無所遺此卷説
理詳明措詞整潔直嘗究心於禮者
考試官教諭張批簡明可錄
考試官教諭應批得旨
君子窮禮以脩身則禮之驗著於外矣蓋禮所
以管攝乎人情者也君子以之而脩身則莊敬嚴
威之驗豈容已乎記樂者謂夫子禮之不可斯須
去身者正以禮可以脩外焉耳彼經禮三百至
理所存也誠能研窮其要領以爲檢身之準繩
punctuated:
大難，斯可以成天下之大業。桓文所以得諸侯、覇天下，以其内獎王室，外攘夷狄，剪篡鋤兇，汲汲焉躬天下之難耳。奈何春秋中葉，覇圖不競，靈成景弗克負荷，以討賊之大權遺楚莊，號令辰陵。噫！此中國所以淪於夷狄，而世道所以降爲戰國也。安得起桓文於九原，以定安攘之計？

禮記
致禮以治躬則莊敬，莊敬則嚴威。
舒素蘊

同考試官教諭唐批：莊敬嚴威處，至字意無所遺。此卷説理詳明，措詞整潔，直嘗究心於禮者。
考試官教諭張批：簡明可錄。
考試官教諭應批：得旨。

君子窮禮以脩身，則禮之驗著於外矣。蓋禮所以管攝乎人情者也。君子以之而脩身，則莊敬嚴威之驗豈容已乎？記樂者謂夫子禮之不可斯須去身者，正以禮可以脩外焉耳。彼經禮三百，至理所存也。誠能研窮其要領，以爲檢身之準繩，
translation_en:
…the great hardships of the world; only then can one accomplish its great undertakings. Dukes Huan and Wen won the allegiance of the feudal lords and became hegemons over the world because they supported the royal house within, repelled the Yi and Di peoples without, suppressed usurpers and rooted out evildoers, earnestly taking the world's hardships upon themselves. Why, then, midway through the Spring and Autumn period, did the enterprise of hegemony lose its strength? Dukes Ling, Cheng, and Jing could not shoulder the responsibility, leaving the great authority to punish rebels to King Zhuang of Chu, who issued commands at Chenling. Alas! This is why the Central States fell under the sway of the Yi and Di, and why the course of the age declined into the Warring States period. How might we raise Dukes Huan and Wen from their graves to establish a plan for securing the realm and repelling outsiders?

Record of Rites
“When one fully applies ritual to governing oneself, one becomes dignified and reverent; being dignified and reverent, one becomes solemn and imposing.”
Shu Suyun

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: In the treatment of dignity, reverence, solemnity, and imposing bearing, nothing of the meaning of the word ‘fully’ [?] is left unexplored. This paper explains principles thoroughly and clearly, and its wording is orderly and polished. Its author is indeed someone who has devoted thought to ritual.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Concise and clear; worthy of inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: Grasps the purport.

When the gentleman thoroughly investigates ritual in order to cultivate himself, its effects become manifest in his outward bearing. Ritual is what regulates and restrains human feelings. When the gentleman cultivates himself through it, how could the resulting dignity, reverence, solemnity, and imposing bearing fail to appear? The writer of the Record of Music speaks of the Master's teaching that ritual must not leave one's person even for an instant [?], precisely because ritual can cultivate one's outward bearing. The three hundred principal rules of ritual are where the highest principles reside. If one can truly investigate their essentials thoroughly and make them the standard for disciplining oneself …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
匪但稽其繁文而已曲禮三千妙道所寓也誠
能推究其旨歸以為脩身之矩度非徒事其末
節而已或視聽也非禮勿視非禮勿聽而省察
克治之必力或言動也言不過辭動不過則而
體驗力行之益至夫然則脩身之功盡而驗之
著於外者當何如哉吾見不矜而莊衣冠自爾
其整齊不動而敬瞻視自爾其尊重出入起居
罔有不欽也動容周旋自中乎禮也不亦莊敬
矣乎旣莊敬矣將見翼翼德容形於謙光之際
===
抑抑威儀見於晉接之頃色足憚貌足畏凜然
有不敢慢者在也威可畏儀可象儼然有不可
犯者存也不其嚴威矣乎君子致禮治躬之驗
如此然則著誠去偽之心其可少有間斷哉嗟
夫心與身相為流通禮與樂不可偏廢君子致
禮以治躬致樂以治心內外交養功夫罔間至
於內和而外順則德輝動於內而民莫不承聽
理發諸外而民莫不承順禮樂之有益於心身
豈細故哉古昔聖帝明王致雍熙悠久之盛治
punctuated: 匪但稽其繁文而已。曲禮三千，妙道所寓也，誠能推究其旨歸，以為脩身之矩度，非徒事其末節而已。或視聽也，非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，而省察克治之必力；或言動也，言不過辭，動不過則，而體驗力行之益至。夫然，則脩身之功盡，而驗之著於外者當何如哉？吾見不矜而莊，衣冠自爾其整齊；不動而敬，瞻視自爾其尊重。出入起居，罔有不欽也；動容周旋，自中乎禮也。不亦莊敬矣乎？旣莊敬矣，將見翼翼德容形於謙光之際，抑抑威儀見於晉接之頃。色足憚，貌足畏，凜然有不敢慢者在也；威可畏，儀可象，儼然有不可犯者存也。不其嚴威矣乎？君子致禮治躬之驗如此，然則著誠去偽之心，其可少有間斷哉？嗟夫！心與身相為流通，禮與樂不可偏廢。君子致禮以治躬，致樂以治心，內外交養，功夫罔間。至於內和而外順，則德輝動於內，而民莫不承聽；理發諸外，而民莫不承順。禮樂之有益於心身，豈細故哉？古昔聖帝明王致雍熙悠久之盛治
translation_en:
…not merely examining its elaborate forms. The three thousand minor rules of ritual embody the subtle Way. One must truly investigate their purport and make them standards for cultivating oneself, rather than merely attending to their incidental details. In looking and listening, one looks at nothing contrary to ritual and listens to nothing contrary to ritual, exerting oneself fully in self-examination and self-mastery. In speech and action, one’s words do not exceed what is fitting and one’s movements do not transgress the rules; one becomes ever more thorough in personally apprehending and earnestly practicing them. When the work of self-cultivation is thus complete, how will its effects appear outwardly? We shall see dignity without affectation, with clothing and cap naturally well ordered; reverence without deliberate effort, with one’s gaze naturally respectful. In going out and coming in, rising and resting, there is nothing lacking in reverence. Every movement and turn naturally accords with ritual. Is this not dignity and reverence? Once these are present, we shall see a circumspect, virtuous bearing manifested in modest radiance, and composed deportment displayed when meeting others. The expression inspires awe, and the appearance commands respect: there is a solemn quality that none dares slight. The authority inspires awe, and the deportment offers a model: there is a gravity that none dares affront. Is this not solemnity and majesty? Such are the effects of the gentleman’s bringing ritual to fulfillment in governing his person. How, then, could his resolve to manifest sincerity and cast out falseness be interrupted even briefly?

Ah! The mind and the person communicate with each other; neither ritual nor music may be neglected. The gentleman brings ritual to fulfillment to govern his person and music to fulfillment to govern his mind. Inward and outward cultivation nourish each other, and the work proceeds without interruption. When inward harmony and outward accord are attained, the radiance of virtue stirs within, and none among the people fails to heed it; order manifests itself outwardly, and none among the people fails to comply. Can the benefits of ritual and music for mind and person be a trifling matter? The sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity brought about splendid government, harmonious, prosperous, and enduring…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
者用此道也故曰致禮樂之道舉而措之天下
無難矣
言而履之禮也行而樂之樂也
陳大韶
同考試官教諭唐批知和序之理本於人君之身且詞不
陳腐宜録之以式後學
考試官教諭張批理明詞暢
考試官教諭應批禮樂重人君說可取
聖人答賢者問政有指所以為序之道者有指
===
所以為和之道者蓋禮樂之道和序而已自非
聖人指其言行之本於吾身者以示子張抑孰
知其然哉且禮樂之道舉而措之固可化成乎
天下遡而求之初非有外於吾身何則言者心
之聲言而不履於理如禮何必也游言不倡所
倡者措之於躬行妄言不發所發者形之於實
踐如言夫閨門也使夫內外之有辨而毋事乎
虛文言夫朝廷也使夫貴賤之有章而務求其
明驗言而履之如此則自然之序得之於我而
punctuated:
者，用此道也。故曰：「致禮樂之道，舉而措之天下，無難矣。」

言而履之，禮也；行而樂之，樂也。

陳大韶

同考試官教諭唐批：知和序之理本於人君之身，且詞不陳腐，宜録之以式後學。
考試官教諭張批：理明詞暢。
考試官教諭應批：禮樂重人君，說可取。

聖人答賢者問政，有指所以為序之道者，有指所以為和之道者。蓋禮樂之道，和序而已。自非聖人指其言行之本於吾身者以示子張，抑孰知其然哉？且禮樂之道，舉而措之，固可化成乎天下；遡而求之，初非有外於吾身。何則？言者，心之聲。言而不履於理，如禮何？必也游言不倡，所倡者措之於躬行；妄言不發，所發者形之於實踐。如言夫閨門也，使夫內外之有辨，而毋事乎虛文；言夫朝廷也，使夫貴賤之有章，而務求其明驗。言而履之如此，則自然之序得之於我，而
translation_en:
…did so by employing this Way. Thus it is said: “Bring the Way of ritual and music to its fullest realization and apply it throughout All-under-Heaven, and there will be no difficulty.”

“To speak and put one's words into practice is ritual; to act and take joy in doing so is music.”

Chen Dashao

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: He understands that the principles of harmony and order are rooted in the ruler's own person. Moreover, his language is not stale. This should be recorded as a model for later students.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The principles are clear and the language flows smoothly.
Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: His explanation that ritual and music place particular weight on the ruler is worthy of acceptance.

In answering a worthy man's question about government, the sage pointed both to the Way by which order is established and to the Way by which harmony is achieved. For the Way of ritual and music consists simply in harmony and order. Had the sage not shown Zizhang how speech and conduct are rooted in one's own person, who would have understood that this was so? Moreover, when taken up and applied, the Way of ritual and music can indeed transform and perfect All-under-Heaven; yet when traced back to its source, it has never lain outside one's own person. Why is this? Speech is the voice of the heart. If one speaks but does not act in accordance with principle, what can one do with ritual? One must refrain from advancing empty words, and personally carry out whatever one advocates; refrain from uttering reckless words, and embody whatever one utters in actual practice. If, for example, one speaks of the household, one must ensure that the inner and outer spheres are distinguished, without pursuing empty formalities. If one speaks of the court, one must ensure that distinctions between high and low rank are manifest, diligently seeking clear evidence of this in practice. When one speaks and puts one's words into practice in this manner, the natural order is realized within oneself, and…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
小大顯微之禮胥此焉備所以一法制而防範
人情者在是所以辨上下而綱維世變者在是
矣若乃几筵之鋪獻酬之交特儀物耳禮云乎
哉行者言之實行而不樂乎理如樂何必也優
而游之凡躬行者脫然而無所累厭而飫之凡
實踐者坦然而無所疑行之閨門而成肅雍和
睦之化無乖戾也行之朝廷而有都俞吁咈之
風何順適也行而樂之如此則自然之和由我
而出而欣喜歡愛之樂於是乎具所以和神人
===
而通天下之志者在是所以移風俗而平天下
之情者在是矣若乃綴兆之行鐘鼓之作特聲
容耳樂云乎哉吁禮樂之道本乎言行如此君
子可不深探其本哉大抵至禮不讓而天下治
至樂無聲而天下和世之人主顧乃不能履中
正而樂和平以先乎天下而徒規規於制度文
為之末以為粉飾太平之具治道之不古若又
何怪哉
第貳場
punctuated:
小大顯微之禮胥此焉備。所以一法制而防範人情者在是，所以辨上下而綱維世變者在是矣。若乃几筵之鋪、獻酬之交，特儀物耳，禮云乎哉？行者，言之實。行而不樂乎理，如樂何？必也優而游之，凡躬行者脫然而無所累；厭而飫之，凡實踐者坦然而無所疑。行之閨門而成肅雍和睦之化，無乖戾也；行之朝廷而有都俞吁咈之風，何順適也！行而樂之如此，則自然之和由我而出，而欣喜歡愛之樂於是乎具。所以和神人而通天下之志者在是，所以移風俗而平天下之情者在是矣。若乃綴兆之行、鐘鼓之作，特聲容耳，樂云乎哉？吁！禮樂之道本乎言行如此，君子可不深探其本哉？大抵至禮不讓而天下治，至樂無聲而天下和。世之人主顧乃不能履中正而樂和平，以先乎天下，而徒規規於制度文為之末，以為粉飾太平之具，治道之不古若，又何怪哉？

第貳場
translation_en:
…and the rites governing great and small, manifest and subtle alike, are all fully present herein. Herein lies the means to unify laws and institutions and restrain human impulses; herein lies the means to distinguish superior from inferior and uphold order amid worldly change. As for setting out armrests and mats and exchanging ritual offerings of wine, these are merely ceremonial furnishings and forms. Can these be called ritual?

Conduct is the substance of words. If one acts without taking delight in principle, what can one do with music? One must dwell in it at ease, so that everything one personally undertakes is free and unencumbered; one must become thoroughly steeped and satisfied in it, so that everything one puts into practice is assured and without doubt. Practised within the household, it brings about a transformation toward reverence, concord, and harmony, without discord. Practised at court, it produces a spirit of approving assent and forthright remonstrance—how harmonious and fitting! When one acts and takes delight in this way, natural harmony issues from oneself, and music expressive of joy, gladness, delight, and affection is thereby complete. Herein lies the means to bring spirits and human beings into harmony and give communication to the aspirations of all under Heaven; herein lies the means to transform customs and bring balance to the feelings of all under Heaven. As for the ranks of dancers in their marked positions and the sounding of bells and drums, these are merely sounds and outward forms. Can these be called music?

Ah! Since the Way of ritual and music is thus rooted in speech and conduct, can the gentleman fail to investigate its foundations deeply? In general, perfect ritual requires no ceremonial yielding, yet all under Heaven is well governed; perfect music has no sound, yet all under Heaven is harmonious. Yet the rulers of this world cannot practise centrality and correctness and delight in peace and harmony, thereby setting an example for all under Heaven. Instead, they merely busy themselves with the incidental details of institutions and ceremonial forms, treating these as instruments for embellishing the appearance of great peace. What wonder, then, that their way of governing does not match that of antiquity?

Second Session

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
論
賢主獨觀萬化之原
潘大賓
同考試官訓導黃批立論甚正而結處見寬裕樂作之意
非深為有見
同考試官敎諭朱批以萬化之原歸之心最是
同考試官學正李批不雕琢浮詞而節節整齊有學之士也
考試官敎諭張批開闔抑揚曲盡賢主獨觀之意
考試官敎諭應批說原字明白可錄
===
天下無心外之治也善治天下者反求諸心而
已矣天下至大也然其理實具於一心一心雖
微也然其用實周乎天下故化行於天下雖萬
殊而原於吾心則至一圖治者自其萬殊而觀
之固紛乎其不齊而難乎其為力也自其一原
而觀之則一以貫之而又何疑焉自心學不明
於天下而世主往往忽之雖有雄才大略上嘉
下樂之志非不好安而惡危好治而惡亂也而
反就其所惡違其所好豈非鹵莽滅裂於本原
punctuated:
論

賢主獨觀萬化之原

潘大賓

同考試官訓導黃批：立論甚正，而結處見寬裕樂作之意，非深為有見。

同考試官敎諭朱批：以萬化之原歸之心，最是。

同考試官學正李批：不雕琢浮詞，而節節整齊，有學之士也。

考試官敎諭張批：開闔抑揚，曲盡賢主獨觀之意。

考試官敎諭應批：說原字明白，可錄。

天下無心外之治也。善治天下者，反求諸心而已矣。天下至大也，然其理實具於一心；一心雖微也，然其用實周乎天下。故化行於天下，雖萬殊，而原於吾心，則至一。圖治者自其萬殊而觀之，固紛乎其不齊，而難乎其為力也；自其一原而觀之，則一以貫之，而又何疑焉？自心學不明於天下，而世主往往忽之，雖有雄才大略、上嘉下樂之志，非不好安而惡危、好治而惡亂也，而反就其所惡，違其所好，豈非鹵莽滅裂於本原
translation_en:
Discourse

“The Worthy Ruler Alone Contemplates the Source of the Myriad Transformations”

Pan Dabin

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor: The argument is thoroughly sound, and the conclusion conveys a spirit of magnanimity and joyful action. “Not deeply insightful” [?].

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: To locate the source of the myriad transformations in the mind is entirely correct.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: He does not embellish empty phrases, yet each successive section is well ordered. He is a man of learning.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Through its opening and closing movements, its restraint and emphasis, the essay fully brings out the meaning of the worthy ruler’s solitary contemplation.

Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: The word “source” is explained clearly. Worthy of inclusion.

There is no ordering of the realm apart from the mind. Those skilled at governing the realm simply turn back and seek within their own minds. The realm is vast indeed, yet its principles are fully contained within a single mind. Though a single mind is subtle, its functioning extends throughout the realm. Thus, although the transformations unfolding throughout the realm differ in myriad ways, their source in my mind is supremely one. If those who seek good government view these transformations in their manifold diversity, they certainly appear bewilderingly disparate and difficult to act upon. If they view them from their single source, however, one principle runs through them all: what uncertainty can remain?

Since the learning of the mind ceased to be clearly understood throughout the realm, rulers have often neglected it. Even when possessed of outstanding ability, great strategic vision, and the aspiration that those above should approve and those below rejoice, it is not that they fail to love security and hate danger, or to love order and hate disorder. Yet they instead approach what they hate and depart from what they love. Is this not because they are careless and negligent at the very source …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之地歟故求治於天下不若求治於吾心泛觀
於萬化不若約觀於一原大原旣正大化自行
天下可以乂安長治而何有意外之虞耶漢徐
樂告武帝以安危之明要而曰賢主獨觀萬化
之原其亦有所見矣請論之夫天以天下畀之
君非徒以崇高富貴之也欲其代天而理物也
合四海九州之民而奉乎君亦非徒以奔走承
順之也欲其爲民而立命也父母君師之責皆
萃於人主之一身不可謂不重矣日有萬幾事
===
有萬變紛至而沓來嬰前而躡後政敎號令之
繁皆歸於人主之獨斷不可謂不煩矣然馭天
下之至博者必以至約制天下之至動者必以
至靜不觀萬化之原而何以爲治於天下乎人
主之於天下導之而欲其樂於善也禁之而欲
其戒於惡也紀綱法度禮樂刑賞之屬雖有萬
不同皆其所以化之之具耳然孰主張是孰綱
維是庸非人主之心乎人主所以制天下事者
固本乎一心而心之所以能應天下事者以具
punctuated:
之地歟？故求治於天下，不若求治於吾心；泛觀於萬化，不若約觀於一原。大原旣正，大化自行，天下可以乂安長治，而何有意外之虞耶？漢徐樂告武帝以安危之明要，而曰：「賢主獨觀萬化之原。」其亦有所見矣。請論之。
夫天以天下畀之君，非徒以崇高富貴之也，欲其代天而理物也。合四海九州之民而奉乎君，亦非徒以奔走承順之也，欲其爲民而立命也。父母君師之責，皆萃於人主之一身，不可謂不重矣。日有萬幾，事有萬變，紛至而沓來，嬰前而躡後，政敎號令之繁，皆歸於人主之獨斷，不可謂不煩矣。然馭天下之至博者，必以至約；制天下之至動者，必以至靜。不觀萬化之原，而何以爲治於天下乎？人主之於天下，導之而欲其樂於善也，禁之而欲其戒於惡也。紀綱法度、禮樂刑賞之屬，雖有萬不同，皆其所以化之之具耳。然孰主張是？孰綱維是？庸非人主之心乎？人主所以制天下事者，固本乎一心，而心之所以能應天下事者，以具
translation_en:
…at the very foundation? Thus, seeking order in the realm is not as effective as seeking order in one's own mind; surveying the myriad transformations broadly is not as effective as focusing on their single source. Once the great source is rectified, the great transforming influence proceeds of itself. The realm can enjoy peace and lasting order: what unforeseen danger could there be? Xu Le of the Han explained to Emperor Wu the clear essentials of security and peril, saying: “The worthy ruler attends solely to the source of the myriad transformations.” He, too, had some insight into this. Allow me to discuss it.
Heaven entrusts the realm to the ruler not merely to exalt him and give him wealth and honor, but because it wishes him to govern all things on Heaven's behalf. The people of the Four Seas and Nine Provinces together serve the ruler not merely to hasten about in obedience to him, but because they wish him to secure their lives. The responsibilities of parent, ruler, and teacher all converge upon the sovereign alone; they cannot be called anything but weighty. Each day brings myriad matters requiring attention, and affairs undergo myriad changes. They arrive in bewildering succession, entangling him before and pressing upon him from behind. The manifold concerns of government and instruction, proclamations and commands, all fall to the sovereign's sole decision; they cannot be called anything but burdensome. Yet to govern the utmost breadth of the realm, one must employ the utmost simplicity; to control its utmost activity, one must employ the utmost stillness. Without attending to the source of the myriad transformations, how could one bring order to the realm? In guiding the people of the realm, the sovereign wishes them to delight in goodness; in imposing prohibitions upon them, he wishes them to guard against evil. Institutions and regulations, rites and music, punishments and rewards, however varied, are all merely instruments by which he transforms the people. Yet what directs these? What holds them together? Is it not the sovereign's mind? The sovereign's means of governing the affairs of the realm are indeed rooted in his single mind, and the mind's ability to respond to the affairs of the realm derives from its possessing…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乎衆理也方寸之小中涵太虛一腔之內畢備
萬物而謂非萬化之原乎然天理雖根於道心
而人欲未嘗不萌於人心苟吾一心之間理欲
並行眞妄錯雜而欲以化天下亦難矣故人主
之心正則天下之事無一不正人主之心不正
則天下之事無一不邪而危微精一之旨所以
丁寧於虞廷授受之間而爲萬世帝王之心法
也世之人主不察於是一心之微衆欲攻之聲
色珍奇馳驅游衍土木之華貨利之殖邊功方
===
技之張皇詭異紛然前陳皆得以入之而君心
荒矣荒則好大勤遠窮奢極欲而無所不至若
武帝是也本原旣失如治化何此民之所以不
安而大勢之所以易動也徐樂以賢主之事啓
之其意善矣然賢主所以觀萬化之原者蓋其
講學以明是心寡欲以養是心以禮而制是心
固皆所以用力於正本端原而爲應變神化之
地也至於燕閒濩濩之時尸居淵默之地一念
之萌尤必謹而察之果天理也則敬以擴之而
punctuated:
乎衆理也。方寸之小，中涵太虛；一腔之內，畢備萬物，而謂非萬化之原乎？然天理雖根於道心，而人欲未嘗不萌於人心。苟吾一心之間，理欲並行，眞妄錯雜，而欲以化天下，亦難矣。故人主之心正，則天下之事無一不正；人主之心不正，則天下之事無一不邪。而危微精一之旨，所以丁寧於虞廷授受之間，而爲萬世帝王之心法也。

世之人主不察於此，一心之微，衆欲攻之：聲色珍奇、馳驅游衍、土木之華、貨利之殖、邊功方技之張皇詭異，紛然前陳，皆得以入之，而君心荒矣。荒則好大勤遠，窮奢極欲，而無所不至，若武帝是也。本原旣失，如治化何？此民之所以不安，而大勢之所以易動也。徐樂以賢主之事啓之，其意善矣。然賢主所以觀萬化之原者，蓋其講學以明是心，寡欲以養是心，以禮而制是心，固皆所以用力於正本端原，而爲應變神化之地也。至於燕閒濩濩之時，尸居淵默之地，一念之萌，尤必謹而察之。果天理也，則敬以擴之，而
translation_en:
… encompassing all principles. Small as the heart is, it contains within it the Great Void; within this single cavity, all things are fully present. Can one say that it is not the source of all transformation? Yet although heavenly principle is rooted in the moral mind, human desires never cease to arise in the human mind. If, within our single mind, principle and desire operate together, and truth and delusion intermingle, it is difficult indeed to seek thereby to transform the realm. Thus, when the ruler’s mind is upright, nothing in the affairs of the realm fails to be upright; when the ruler’s mind is not upright, nothing in the affairs of the realm is free of perversity. Hence the teaching that the human mind is precarious and the moral mind subtle, and that one must be discerning and single-minded, was earnestly repeated when rulership was transmitted at the court of Shun. It became the method of cultivating the mind for emperors and kings throughout the ages.

Rulers who fail to perceive this allow their subtle mind to be assailed by a multitude of desires. Music and sensual pleasures, rare treasures, riding and excursions, splendid buildings, the accumulation of wealth and profit, and the ostentation and extravagance of frontier exploits and esoteric arts crowd before them. All gain entry, and the ruler’s mind falls into neglect. Once it does, he craves grandeur, expends his energies on distant undertakings, pursues luxury and desire to their utmost, and stops at nothing—as was the case with Emperor Wu. Once the fundamental source has been lost, what can be done about orderly government and moral transformation? This is why the people are unsettled and the overall political situation is readily shaken. Xu Le sought to enlighten him through the deeds of worthy rulers, and his intention was good. Yet the means by which a worthy ruler examines the source of all transformation consist in studying and discussing learning to illuminate this mind, diminishing desires to nourish it, and regulating it through ritual propriety. All these are efforts to rectify the root and set the source aright, establishing a basis for responding to change and effecting wondrous transformation. When at ease in private leisure [?], seated motionless like a ritual personator and maintaining profound silence, he must be especially vigilant in examining the emergence of a single thought. If it truly accords with heavenly principle, he must reverently extend it, and …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不使其少有壅閼果人欲也則敬以克之而不
使其少有凝滯此非賢主獨致其决而他人何
所與力哉蓋至此而後道心純爲一身之主矣
然雖獨觀乎此而謹之尤不敢獨恃乎此而遂
已也於是盤有銘几有戒器有箴圖有規而在
輿位宁旅賁官師皆有規典而無地不寓其警
焉前有疑後有丞左納言右納史而侍御僕從
罔非正人以朝夕承弼而靡人不獻其忠焉皆
所以爲此心之防此理之輔而正萬化之本原
===
此其所以居靜制動守約施愽措諸天下國家
無所處而不當化成雍煕泰和之盛亦由此而
可致而武帝何足以知之然樂非能爲是言也
殆先漢儒者之緒論而樂能援之以自售耳方
告以此且曰明於安危之機脩之廟堂之上而
銷未形之患似也而復蠱之以逐走獸射飛鳥
弘遊燕之囿淫縱恣之觀極馳騁之樂自若金
石絲竹之聲不絶於耳帷幄之私俳優侏儒之
笑不乏於前而天下無宿憂何哉繼勉之以天
punctuated:
不使其少有壅閼；果人欲也，則敬以克之，而不使其少有凝滯。此非賢主獨致其决，而他人何所與力哉？蓋至此而後，道心純爲一身之主矣。然雖獨觀乎此而謹之，尤不敢獨恃乎此而遂已也。於是盤有銘，几有戒，器有箴，圖有規；而在輿、位宁，旅賁、官師皆有規典，而無地不寓其警焉。前有疑，後有丞，左納言，右納史，而侍御僕從罔非正人，以朝夕承弼，而靡人不獻其忠焉。皆所以爲此心之防、此理之輔，而正萬化之本原。此其所以居靜制動，守約施愽，措諸天下國家，無所處而不當，化成雍煕泰和之盛，亦由此而可致。而武帝何足以知之？
然樂非能爲是言也，殆先漢儒者之緒論，而樂能援之以自售耳。方告以此，且曰：「明於安危之機，脩之廟堂之上，而銷未形之患。」似也，而復蠱之以逐走獸、射飛鳥，弘遊燕之囿，淫縱恣之觀，極馳騁之樂，自若金石絲竹之聲不絶於耳，帷幄之私，俳優侏儒之笑不乏於前，而天下無宿憂，何哉？繼勉之以天
translation_en:
…and allow it not the slightest obstruction; if it is indeed human desire, he must overcome it through reverent attentiveness and allow it not the slightest lingering hold. Unless the worthy ruler himself exercises his resolve in this, how can anyone else contribute? Only upon reaching this point does the mind of the Way become, in its purity, master of his whole person. Yet although he alone examines this mind and watches over it carefully, he especially dares not rely solely upon this and stop there. Thus his basin bears an inscription, his armrest an admonition, his utensils injunctions, and his pictures counsels. Whether he rides in his carriage or stands at the palace entrance, his guards and officials all have prescribed rules for remonstrance, so that nowhere is he without a warning. Before him is a counselor, behind him an assistant; to his left is a presenter of counsel, and to his right a recording scribe [?]. His attendants and servants are without exception upright men, supporting and assisting him morning and evening, and none fails to offer loyal counsel. All these serve to guard this mind, sustain this principle, and rectify the source of all transformation. This is how he abides in stillness yet governs movement, holds to what is essential yet extends its application broadly. Applied to all under Heaven, to the state, and to the ruling house, it is appropriate in every circumstance. Through this, too, he can bring about the flourishing condition of harmony, prosperity, and great peace that results from perfected moral transformation. How could Emperor Wu have understood this?
Yet Xu Le was not himself capable of originating such words. They were probably the inherited teachings of earlier Han Confucian scholars, which Le could invoke to advance himself. In presenting this advice, he further said: “Understand clearly the incipient causes of security and danger, attend to them in the court, and dispel troubles before they take shape.” This sounds right. Yet he then beguiled the ruler with the prospect of pursuing running beasts and shooting flying birds, enlarging the parks for pleasure and leisure, indulging in unrestrained spectacles, and exhausting the pleasures of riding and hunting. As though nothing were amiss, the sounds of bells, chimes, strings, and pipes would never cease in his ears; in the privacy of his curtained chambers, the laughter of actors and dwarfs would never be lacking before him—and yet all under Heaven would have no enduring troubles. Why did he say this? He next urged him to take all under Heaven…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
下爲務則湯文不難侔而成康之俗可復興亦
是也而復餌之以圖王不成其敝足以安安則
何求而不得何威而不成奚征而不服何哉夫
未有人主縱欲而能安且無憂者也樂之言不
我誣歟蓋其一出一入一捭一闔雅樂方陳而
淫哇卽繼無非詭遇以求合耳陋儒之希世取
寵一至於此此識者所以謂汲長孺內多欲而
外施仁義一語爲苦口之藥董仲舒正心以正
朝廷數言爲格心之論歟惜乎帝之不悟而徒
===
恨樂等相見之晚也
表
擬
賜大臣歷代名臣奏議謝表永樂十四年
舒素蘊
同考試官教諭唐 批駢儷中寫出人臣對揚
休美之心宜錄
考試官教諭張 批得體
考試官教諭應 批四六過人可取
punctuated:
下爲務，則湯文不難侔，而成康之俗可復興，亦是也。而復餌之以圖王不成，其敝足以安，安則何求而不得，何威而不成，奚征而不服，何哉？夫未有人主縱欲而能安且無憂者也。樂之言不我誣歟？蓋其一出一入，一捭一闔，雅樂方陳，而淫哇卽繼，無非詭遇以求合耳。陋儒之希世取寵，一至於此！此識者所以謂汲長孺「內多欲而外施仁義」一語爲苦口之藥，董仲舒「正心以正朝廷」數言爲格心之論歟？惜乎帝之不悟，而徒恨樂等相見之晚也！

表

擬賜大臣《歷代名臣奏議》謝表，永樂十四年。
舒素蘊

同考試官教諭唐 批：駢儷中寫出人臣對揚休美之心，宜錄。
考試官教諭張 批：得體。
考試官教諭應 批：四六過人，可取。
translation_en:
…making the realm his concern, he would find it no great difficulty to equal Tang and Wen, and could revive the customs of the reigns of Cheng and Kang. This, too, was right. Yet he again dangled the bait that, even if the attempt to establish kingly rule failed, its shortcomings would still leave him secure; and, once secure, what could he seek without obtaining it, what display of might could fail, and whom could he campaign against without securing submission? Why say this? No ruler has ever indulged his desires and yet remained secure and free from anxiety. Are Le’s words not deceiving us? His arguments move out and in, opening and closing: scarcely has the refined music begun when licentious tunes follow. All this is merely a departure from the proper course to win the ruler’s favor. That a shallow scholar’s pursuit of worldly favor and patronage should reach such a point! Is this why discerning men call Ji Changru’s words, “Within, you have many desires, while outwardly you practice benevolence and righteousness,” medicine bitter to the taste, and Dong Zhongshu’s words about “rectifying the heart in order to rectify the court” an argument for correcting the ruler’s heart? Alas, the emperor did not awaken to this, but merely regretted having met Le and the others so late!

Memorial

Draft memorial of thanks for the bestowal upon high officials of Memorials of Famous Ministers of Successive Dynasties (Lidai mingchen zouyi), set in the fourteenth year of Yongle [1416].
By Shu Suyun.

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: “Within its parallel prose, it conveys a minister’s desire to acknowledge and extol the sovereign’s gracious goodness. It merits inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Appropriate in form and tone.”

Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: “Its four-and-six-character parallel prose surpasses that of others. It merits acceptance.”

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
具官臣某等兹者伏蒙
聖恩賜臣等歷代名臣奏議各一部謹當表
謝者臣等誠懽誠忭稽首頓首伏以
錄言異代式彰求諫之
盛心
散帙
明庭茂對勸忠之
殊典義存交儆
仁出特
===
恩臣聞上古有治人無治法中古有遺政無遺
言粤稽名世之英迭展匡時之略謀王斷
國代不乏人陳善責難功存致主坐運而
折衝千里立談而成信終身啟心沃心就
事論事言有時而不用忠閱世而愈明尚
有典刑布在方冊受知
明主爰
命儒臣務精選以成書期多聞而建事集訏謨
於羣籍善之善者必收廣忠益於眾思醇
punctuated:
具官臣某等，兹者伏蒙聖恩，賜臣等《歷代名臣奏議》各一部，謹當表謝者。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首。伏以：錄言異代，式彰求諫之盛心；散帙明庭，茂對勸忠之殊典。義存交儆，仁出特恩。
臣聞上古有治人，無治法；中古有遺政，無遺言。粤稽名世之英，迭展匡時之略。謀王斷國，代不乏人；陳善責難，功存致主。坐運而折衝千里，立談而成信終身。啟心沃心，就事論事。言有時而不用，忠閱世而愈明。尚有典刑，布在方冊。受知明主，爰命儒臣，務精選以成書，期多聞而建事。集訏謨於羣籍，善之善者必收；廣忠益於眾思，醇
translation_en:
Your servants, so-and-so and others, holding their respective offices, have now humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious gift of one copy each of the Memorials of Eminent Ministers of Successive Dynasties (Lidai mingchen zouyi). We respectfully submit this memorial of thanks. With heartfelt joy and delight, we bow our heads to the ground and kowtow. We humbly reflect: by recording words from different dynasties, you manifest your great desire to seek remonstrance; by distributing these volumes at your illustrious court, you bestow an exceptional favor encouraging loyalty, which we gratefully acknowledge. Righteousness lies in mutual admonition; benevolence issues in special grace.
Your servants have heard that high antiquity had men who brought good order, but no fixed methods of government; middle antiquity left a legacy of governance, but no surviving words. Examining the outstanding men renowned in their ages, we find that each in turn displayed strategies for setting his times aright. Men who advised kings and decided affairs of state were never lacking in any generation. By setting forth what was good and demanding the difficult, they rendered service in bringing their rulers to the highest attainment. Seated, they devised plans that repelled enemies a thousand li away; in a brief conversation, they established trust that endured a lifetime. They opened and nourished their rulers’ minds, addressing affairs on their merits. Though their words sometimes went unheeded, their loyalty shone ever more clearly through succeeding ages. Exemplary models still survive, preserved in books. These came to the attention of an enlightened ruler, who thereupon commanded his Confucian ministers to make a meticulous selection and compile a book, intending that broad learning should lead to practical accomplishment. Gathering great counsels from many writings, they were sure to include the best of the good; drawing upon many minds to enlarge the benefits of loyal counsel, the pure …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乎醇者悉采上關君德人鑑可徵下切事
情智囊不廢俟
聖敢期乎百世興邦或係乎一言寶鼎千年神
姦洞鑒靈龜五總休咎潜通結書局以告
成登
法宮而
進御蓋宇宙無窮之變舉不出於目前若古
今有異之宜當自得於言外海兼河潤隨
翕闢而有餘星受
===
日光賴
表章而不朽竊焉
萃編而心幸俄驚
晉錫之躬逢用藥真方轉圜
深意無功上
荅有愧中存欽惟
皇帝陛下
舜德罔愆賓四門之穆穆
啓賢能敬君萬國之元元
punctuated:
乎醇者悉采。上關君德，人鑑可徵；下切事情，智囊不廢。俟聖敢期乎百世，興邦或係乎一言。寶鼎千年，神姦洞鑒；靈龜五總，休咎潜通。結書局以告成，登法宮而進御。蓋宇宙無窮之變，舉不出於目前；若古今有異之宜，當自得於言外。海兼河潤，隨翕闢而有餘；星受日光，賴表章而不朽。竊焉萃編而心幸，俄驚晉錫之躬逢。用藥真方，轉圜深意，無功上荅，有愧中存。
欽惟皇帝陛下，舜德罔愆，賓四門之穆穆；啓賢能敬，君萬國之元元。
translation_en:
…all that is purest has been gathered. Above, it concerns the ruler’s virtue, offering human examples that may serve as mirrors; below, it addresses practical affairs, preserving a treasury of wisdom. We venture to hope that it may await a sage even a hundred generations hence; the flourishing of a state may hinge upon a single utterance. Like a precious tripod enduring a thousand years, it clearly discerns spirits and malign beings; like a numinous tortoise encompassing five categories [?], it communicates unseen with good and ill fortune. The compilation office’s work was brought to completion, and the book was taken into the imperial palace and presented to Your Majesty. The inexhaustible changes of the universe are thus all brought before the eyes; as for the different measures appropriate to antiquity and the present, their meaning must be grasped beyond the words. Like the sea receiving the rivers’ bounty, it has abundance through every contraction and expansion; like stars receiving the sun’s light, it depends upon imperial recognition to endure forever. Privately rejoicing at gathering and compiling this work, we were suddenly astonished to find ourselves the recipients of rewards. Here are true prescriptions for healing and profound intentions to turn affairs around; having achieved nothing with which to repay Your Majesty, we harbor shame within.
We reverently consider that Your Majesty the Emperor possesses Shun’s unfailing virtue and his solemn dignity in receiving guests at the four gates; like Qi, worthy and capable of reverence, you rule the common people of the myriad states…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
合日月以嚮明
整乾坤而立極
兩都竝建雄鎮上游七佐叅謀弘開
內閣
皇武旣隆於底定人文尤篤於化成
實惠潛孚厚栽培之命脉
虛衷未滿廓延攬之規模載輯舊聞藉前言
而
畜德繼
===
頒新命見下濟之
謙光鉅編崇琬琰之陳
大號仰絲綸之渙
蘭臺珍秘
玉版分香蔀屋輝煌牙籤增重非特傳之爲
寶蓋將
宣之使言惟古之遺直旣不忘則今之嘉言
罔攸伏暨
風聲於天下先
punctuated: 合日月以嚮明，整乾坤而立極。兩都竝建，雄鎮上游；七佐叅謀，弘開內閣。皇武旣隆於底定，人文尤篤於化成。實惠潛孚，厚栽培之命脉；虛衷未滿，廓延攬之規模。載輯舊聞，藉前言而畜德；繼頒新命，見下濟之謙光。鉅編崇琬琰之陳，大號仰絲綸之渙。蘭臺珍秘，玉版分香；蔀屋輝煌，牙籤增重。非特傳之爲寶，蓋將宣之使言。惟古之遺直旣不忘，則今之嘉言罔攸伏。暨風聲於天下，先
translation_en: …Joining the sun and moon in their radiance, you set Heaven and Earth in order and establish the supreme standard. The two capitals stand together, commanding the upper reaches in majesty; seven assistants participate in deliberations, greatly expanding the Grand Secretariat. Your imperial martial prowess has already brought the realm firmly to peace; your cultivation of civil virtues is still more devoted to transforming the people. Tangible benefits quietly win their trust, nourishing the vital roots of their growth; your receptive mind remains unsatisfied, broadening the scope for attracting worthy men. You have compiled the records of the past, drawing on earlier words to nurture virtue; you have followed this with a new command, revealing the radiance of humility that extends aid downward. The great compilation is exalted like a display of precious jade; we look up in reverence as your great proclamation issues forth like silken threads. Treasures kept secret in the imperial archives now share the fragrance of their jade tablets; humble dwellings shine, and ivory book labels gain new distinction. These writings are not merely to be transmitted as treasures: they are to be made widely known so that men will speak out. Since the upright men of antiquity who have passed away are not forgotten, worthy counsel in the present will nowhere remain concealed. Your inspiring influence reaches all under Heaven, preceding…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
雨澤於
朝端豈知才劣位優自顧
恩深報淺腹心是寄偶血氣之未衰
元首克明何股肱之敢惰願爲骨鯁誓勿面從
賢聖可希俛盡平生之學術忠良竝遂仰
酬
今日之
眷懷惟
聖心允執厥中俾臣等順之于外
===
兼聽必歸於獨斷
力行豈在乎多言
見諸事而深切著明
加之意而高明光大
廟謨恢遠永保不二心之臣
國勢尊安增光
大一統之業臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖歡抃感激之至謹稽首頓首奉
punctuated: 雨澤於朝端。豈知才劣位優，自顧恩深報淺。腹心是寄，偶血氣之未衰；元首克明，何股肱之敢惰？願爲骨鯁，誓勿面從。賢聖可希，俛盡平生之學術；忠良竝遂，仰酬今日之眷懷。惟聖心允執厥中，俾臣等順之于外。兼聽必歸於獨斷，力行豈在乎多言？見諸事而深切著明，加之意而高明光大。廟謨恢遠，永保不二心之臣；國勢尊安，增光大一統之業。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、歡抃感激之至，謹稽首頓首奉
translation_en: …and spread rain-like beneficence through the court. Who could have imagined that our meager talents would receive such exalted positions? Reflecting upon ourselves, we see that Your grace is profound, while our repayment is slight. Entrusted to serve as Your heart and mind, we happen still to possess undiminished vigor; with the sovereign head so enlightened, how could we, its limbs, dare to be indolent? We wish to serve as forthright remonstrants and swear never merely to assent to Your face. Worthiness and sagehood may be aspired to: we shall strive to devote all the learning of our lifetimes to Your service. May loyalty and goodness alike find fulfillment, that we may requite Your present solicitude. May Your sagely mind truly hold fast to the Mean, allowing us, Your servants, to follow it in our outward conduct. Hearing all sides must ultimately lead to Your own sole decision; resolute action surely does not depend upon abundant words. Let it be manifested in deeds, profound, earnest, and clearly evident; apply Your mind to it, making it lofty, enlightened, splendid, and great. May the court’s counsels be expansive and far-reaching, forever retaining ministers of undivided loyalty; may the state’s standing be exalted and secure, adding luster to the undertaking of universal unity. We, Your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sagely Majesty, overcome with joyful applause and the deepest gratitude. Reverently bowing our heads to the ground and kowtowing, we submit…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁塲
策五道
第一問
潘大賓
同考試官訓導黃批周制之所以善唐制之所以失而我
國家制作之所以比隆成周而陋有唐於下風者歷歷言之無遺可見子之學識其大者
===
同考試官敎諭朱批善揄揚
聖製表之盛可錄
同考試官學正李批辭昌而正且其中善加可否有識
之士也
考試官敎諭張批此作詳道其實可謂熟於典故矣
考試官敎諭應批我
朝諸司職掌會典二書所以垂創演繹後先相輝蓋參之周官周禮而取衷焉唐六典不
足擬矣此策條析精覈其於經世之學將有槩於其中者乎
聖人之制作也有所以定一代之宏規有所似
punctuated:
表稱謝以聞。

第叁塲，策五道。第一問。潘大賓。

同考試官訓導黃批：周制之所以善，唐制之所以失，而我國家制作之所以比隆成周而陋有唐於下風者，歷歷言之無遺，可見子之學識其大者。

同考試官敎諭朱批：善揄揚聖製表之盛，可錄。

同考試官學正李批：辭昌而正，且其中善加可否，有識之士也。

考試官敎諭張批：此作詳道其實，可謂熟於典故矣。

考試官敎諭應批：我朝《諸司職掌》《會典》二書，所以垂創演繹，後先相輝，蓋參之《周官》《周禮》而取衷焉，《唐六典》不足擬矣。此策條析精覈，其於經世之學，將有槩於其中者乎？

聖人之制作也，有所以定一代之宏規，有所似
translation_en:
…respectfully submit this memorial to express our gratitude and bring it to Your Majesty’s attention.

Third session: five policy questions. First question. Pan Dabin.

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor: You explain clearly and exhaustively why Zhou institutions were good, why Tang institutions failed, and why the institutions established by our dynasty rival the flourishing Zhou, leaving the Tang far behind as inferior. This reveals the breadth of your learning and discernment.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: You ably extol the magnificence of the imperial institutions [?]. Worth selecting.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: The language is copious yet correct; moreover, the judgments of approval and disapproval within it are well made. You are a man of discernment.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: This composition expounds the facts in detail. You may indeed be called thoroughly versed in institutional precedents.

Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: Our dynasty’s two books, Duties of the Various Offices (Zhusi zhizhang) and Collected Statutes (Huidian), lay down foundational arrangements and elaborate upon them, the earlier and later works illuminating one another. They consult the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) and the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) to arrive at a balanced standard. The Six Statutes of the Tang (Tang liudian) cannot compare with them. This policy essay analyzes its subject systematically, precisely, and rigorously. Might its author have grasped in his mind the essentials of the learning of statecraft?

When sages establish institutions, they have means to determine the grand framework of an age, and have something resembling [?]…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
周一代之經制紀綱立於前而後一代之
宏規以定損益明於後而後一代之經制
以周定於前者必極其規模之大周於後
者必盡其節目之詳夫然後治具畢張成
憲罔愆而有以保重熈累洽於無疆也愚
生蓋嘗誦
聖祖之詒謀仰
先皇之繼志上稽成周下迨有唐而後知我
朝之獨盛矣請因明問而陳之三代而上法
===
制莫備於周其可攷者周官周禮而已成
王功成治定董正庶官使帥其屬以舉其
事故周官詳於戒飭之辭而略於分授之
職而金履祥以為周禮之經也周公總領
百揆弼成君德事為之制曲為之防故周
禮詳於六屬之事而未及乎公孤之任而
金履祥以為周官之傳也然周之所以善
者有關雎麟趾之意以行周官之法度考
之二書時巡歲見之有異六服九服之不
punctuated:
周一代之經制。紀綱立於前，而後一代之宏規以定；損益明於後，而後一代之經制以周。定於前者，必極其規模之大；周於後者，必盡其節目之詳。夫然後治具畢張，成憲罔愆，而有以保重熈累洽於無疆也。愚生蓋嘗誦聖祖之詒謀，仰先皇之繼志，上稽成周，下迨有唐，而後知我朝之獨盛矣。請因明問而陳之。
三代而上，法制莫備於周，其可攷者，《周官》《周禮》而已。成王功成治定，董正庶官，使帥其屬以舉其事，故《周官》詳於戒飭之辭，而略於分授之職，而金履祥以為《周禮》之經也。周公總領百揆，弼成君德，事為之制，曲為之防，故《周禮》詳於六屬之事，而未及乎公孤之任，而金履祥以為《周官》之傳也。然周之所以善者，有《關雎》《麟趾》之意，以行《周官》之法度。考之二書，時巡歲見之有異，六服九服之不
translation_en:
… bring a dynasty’s institutions to completeness. Only when the governing framework has first been established can the dynasty’s grand design be settled; only when subsequent modifications have been clarified can its institutions become complete. What is settled at the outset must attain the fullest breadth of its design; what is completed afterward must exhaust the detail of its provisions. Only then will all the instruments of government be in place and the established statutes remain unbreached, ensuring successive ages of prosperity and enduring harmony without limit. I, an unworthy student, have read with reverence the plans bequeathed by the sagely founder and looked up with admiration to the late emperor’s continuation of his aims. Tracing precedents back to the established Zhou and onward to the Tang, I have come to understand the surpassing greatness of our dynasty. Allow me to set this forth in response to your discerning question.
In the Three Dynasties and earlier, no system of laws and institutions was more complete than that of the Zhou. The sources by which it may be examined are the “Offices of Zhou” (Zhouguan) and the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli). Once King Cheng’s achievements were accomplished and governance was settled, he supervised and rectified the various officials, directing them to lead their subordinates in performing their duties. Thus, the “Offices of Zhou” is detailed in its words of admonition but brief concerning the assignment of offices; Jin Lüxiang accordingly regarded it as the foundational text for the Rites of Zhou. The Duke of Zhou oversaw the hundred offices and assisted in perfecting his ruler’s virtue, establishing regulations for every undertaking and safeguards for every contingency. Thus, the Rites of Zhou is detailed concerning the affairs of the six groups of subordinate officials, but does not extend to the responsibilities of the Three Dukes and Three Junior Dukes; Jin Lüxiang accordingly regarded it as a commentary on the “Offices of Zhou.” Yet what made Zhou government good was that the spirit of “The Ospreys” (Guanju) and “The Qilin’s Hooves” (Linzhi) informed its implementation of the rules and standards of the “Offices of Zhou.” Examining the two texts, one finds differences concerning periodic royal inspection tours and annual audiences, and discrepancies between the six and nine zones of service …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同不過小有損益而何足深疑哉三代而
下法制莫踰於唐其可攷者六典會要而
已六典成於開元盛時而經畫措置最有
法度精密簡要猶有古意故曾鞏以為得
建官制理之方會要續編於蘇冕崔鉉而
代德以後治少亂多郊祀朝儀食貨苛取
故林駉以為雖備而無取然唐之所以陋
者大綱不正而萬目徒舉考之六典定於
玄宗而註於李林甫蓋已兆亂階而其餘
===
不足觀也已嗚呼周治隆矣而周禮非全
書唐書備矣而治功無可述若之何其不
獨盛於我
朝乎洪惟
太祖高皇帝以天錫智勇復帝王之中又以天
縱多能恢邦國之遠猷諸司職掌書成於
宸斷見出於
淵衷經綸周至輕重同得自今觀之革丞相以
防專恣陞六部以分事權所以正百官也
punctuated:
同，不過小有損益，而何足深疑哉？三代而下，法制莫踰於唐，其可攷者，《六典》《會要》而已。《六典》成於開元盛時，而經畫措置最有法度，精密簡要，猶有古意，故曾鞏以為得建官制理之方。《會要》續編於蘇冕、崔鉉，而代德以後，治少亂多，郊祀、朝儀、食貨苛取，故林駉以為雖備而無取。然唐之所以陋者，大綱不正而萬目徒舉。考之，《六典》定於玄宗而註於李林甫，蓋已兆亂階，而其餘不足觀也已。
嗚呼！周治隆矣，而《周禮》非全書；唐書備矣，而治功無可述。若之何其不獨盛於我朝乎？洪惟太祖高皇帝，以天錫智勇復帝王之中，又以天縱多能恢邦國之遠猷。《諸司職掌》書成於宸斷，見出於淵衷，經綸周至，輕重同得。自今觀之，革丞相以防專恣，陞六部以分事權，所以正百官也。
translation_en:
…differences amount to no more than minor additions and reductions; why should they occasion grave doubts? Since the Three Dynasties, no system of laws and institutions has surpassed that of the Tang. The sources through which it can be examined are simply the Six Statutes (Liudian) and the Institutional Digest (Huiyao). The Six Statutes was completed during the flourishing Kaiyuan era. Its planning and arrangements were exceptionally systematic: precise, concise, and essential, they still retained something of the spirit of antiquity. Thus Zeng Gong considered it to have grasped the proper method of establishing offices and ordering government. The Institutional Digest was compiled and continued by Su Mian and Cui Xuan. Yet from the reigns of Daizong and Dezong onward, periods of order were few and periods of disorder many; its accounts of suburban sacrifices, court ceremonial, and economic affairs concerned harsh exactions [?]. Thus Lin Jiong considered it comprehensive but unworthy of adoption. The Tang’s shortcomings lay in its fundamental principles being unsound, so that its myriad detailed provisions were instituted in vain. On examination, the Six Statutes was settled under Xuanzong and annotated by Li Linfu: already this foreshadowed the beginnings of disorder. The rest scarcely merits consideration.
Alas! Government under the Zhou attained great heights, yet the Rites of Zhou is not a complete book. The Tang writings are comprehensive, yet their achievements in government offer nothing worthy of recounting. How, then, could such excellence fail to belong uniquely to our dynasty? We reverently reflect that Emperor Taizu Gao, with Heaven-bestowed wisdom and courage, restored the central position of imperial rule [?], and, with his Heaven-endowed manifold abilities, broadened the state’s far-reaching plans. The Duties of the Various Offices (Zhusi Zhizhang) was completed through his sovereign decisions, its insights issuing from the depths of his mind. Its ordering of affairs was comprehensive and thorough, giving due weight to matters both great and small. Viewed from the present, abolishing the post of Chief Councilor to prevent arbitrary domination, and elevating the Six Ministries to distribute administrative authority, were the means by which he set the hundred officials in proper order.

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
內閣之選六科崇七品之階設詹事府以領
坊局之官削回回監以專欽天之職
親藩之祿或隆或殺問刑之條或減或增皆
不可以莫之紀也故揭之以官職制度而
大綱正焉麗之以事物名數儀文等級而
萬目張焉然一以職掌為主而類以頒降
羣書也附以歷年事例也其與職掌小異
者不過補偏救弊裒多益寡一事之軒輊
一時之彌縫至其奉若欽承以周
===
一代之經制者乃所以為大同也我
祖宗良法美意昭垂於百年之前大烈耿光覲
揚於百年之後
聖子神孫佩服而無斁洪基昌祚安固而不搖
其本皆在是矣是豈末世所可彷彿而亦
豈容愚生之名言哉然治久而弊生有大
而孽萌謹持盈守成之道而不忘思患預
防之心端有望於
今日敢以是為芹曝之
punctuated:
內閣之選，六科崇七品之階，設詹事府以領坊局之官，削回回監以專欽天之職。親藩之祿，或隆或殺；問刑之條，或減或增，皆不可以莫之紀也。故揭之以官職制度，而大綱正焉；麗之以事物名數、儀文等級，而萬目張焉。然一以職掌為主，而類以頒降羣書也，附以歷年事例也。其與職掌小異者，不過補偏救弊、裒多益寡，一事之軒輊，一時之彌縫。至其奉若欽承，以周一代之經制者，乃所以為大同也。
我祖宗良法美意，昭垂於百年之前；大烈耿光，覲揚於百年之後。聖子神孫，佩服而無斁；洪基昌祚，安固而不搖，其本皆在是矣。是豈末世所可彷彿，而亦豈容愚生之名言哉？然治久而弊生，有大而孽萌。謹持盈守成之道，而不忘思患預防之心，端有望於今日。敢以是為芹曝之
translation_en:
…selection for the Grand Secretariat; the Six Offices of Scrutiny were elevated to the seventh rank; the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent was established to oversee the officials of its secretariats and bureaus; and the Muslim Directorate of Astronomy was abolished, concentrating astronomical duties in the Directorate of Astronomy. The stipends of princes of the imperial clan were sometimes increased and sometimes reduced; provisions governing criminal adjudication were sometimes curtailed and sometimes expanded. None of these changes could be left unrecorded. Thus, official posts and institutional arrangements are set forth to establish the main framework; the names and numbers of things and affairs, ceremonial forms, and hierarchical distinctions are attached to it, so that every detail is laid out. Throughout, however, the Administrative Responsibilities (Zhizhang) serves as the basis, with imperially promulgated books grouped by category and precedents from successive years appended. Minor departures from the Administrative Responsibilities amount merely to correcting imbalances and remedying abuses, taking from excess to supplement deficiency: adjustments in a particular matter or makeshift repairs for a particular time. In reverently following and respectfully upholding the established institutions of the dynasty in their entirety, however, they share a fundamental unity.
The excellent laws and fine intentions of our imperial ancestors were clearly handed down a hundred years ago; their great achievements and brilliant glory are displayed and exalted a hundred years later. Their sage sons and divine grandsons cherish and observe them without wearying; the vast dynastic foundations and flourishing imperial fortune remain secure and unshaken. All have their foundation here. How could an age of decline even approximate this, and how could a foolish student such as I adequately describe it? Yet prolonged good government breeds abuses, and possession of greatness allows troubles to sprout [?]. To observe carefully the way of preserving fullness and safeguarding established achievements, while never forgetting to anticipate trouble and take precautions—this is precisely what I hope for today. I venture to present this as my humble offering of celery and warming sunshine …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
獻可乎
第二問
汪有執
同考試官教諭蔡批詳言古今賞罰公私之異末復歸之
務學正心知本之論也
考試官教諭張批以至公至正立說最為切當
考試官教諭應批敷答詳明援引曲當敬羡敬羡
人君能秉天下之至公行天下之至正斯
可以運天下之大柄矣天下之善非慶賞
===
無以勸天下之惡非刑罰無以威二者人
君之大柄不可失也天下之心非至公無
以服天下之理非至正無由行二者人君
所以操柄尤不可失也故公正不忒者純
王之心刑賞得宜者純王之政執此以稽
此帝王所以得而後世所以失也愚嘗攷
之詩書矣皐陶言五服五章五刑五用商
頌言不僭不濫不敢怠遑其所以必歸之
天命者天之視聽在民天降災祥在德一
punctuated:
獻，可乎？

第二問
汪有執

同考試官教諭蔡批：詳言古今賞罰公私之異，末復歸之務學正心，知本之論也。
考試官教諭張批：以至公至正立說，最為切當。
考試官教諭應批：敷答詳明，援引曲當，敬羡敬羡。

人君能秉天下之至公，行天下之至正，斯可以運天下之大柄矣。天下之善，非慶賞無以勸；天下之惡，非刑罰無以威。二者，人君之大柄，不可失也。天下之心，非至公無以服；天下之理，非至正無由行。二者，人君所以操柄，尤不可失也。故公正不忒者，純王之心；刑賞得宜者，純王之政。執此以稽此，帝王所以得，而後世所以失也。愚嘗攷之《詩》《書》矣。皐陶言五服五章、五刑五用，《商頌》言不僭不濫、不敢怠遑。其所以必歸之天命者，天之視聽在民，天降災祥在德，一

Second Policy Question
Wang Youzhi

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: He explains in detail the differences between public impartiality and private interest in rewards and punishments, past and present. At the end he returns to diligent study and rectifying the mind. This is an argument that understands the root of the matter.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: He bases his argument on perfect impartiality and perfect rectitude, which is most apt.

Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: The response is detailed and clear, and its citations are apt in every particular. Admirable, admirable!

If the ruler can uphold perfect impartiality throughout the realm and practice perfect rectitude throughout the realm, he can wield the realm’s great levers of authority. Good conduct in the realm cannot be encouraged without rewards; evil in the realm cannot be deterred without punishments. These two are the ruler’s great levers of authority and must not be relinquished. The hearts of all under Heaven cannot be won over without perfect impartiality; the principles governing all under Heaven cannot be put into practice without perfect rectitude. These two are the means by which the ruler wields those levers and must, above all, not be relinquished. Thus, unfailing impartiality and rectitude constitute the mind of a true king; fitting punishments and rewards constitute the government of a true king. Applying these criteria to examine the matter reveals why the ancient emperors and kings succeeded and why later generations failed.

I have examined this in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents. Gao Yao speaks of the five kinds of ceremonial robes with their five distinctions, and the five punishments with their five applications. The Hymns of Shang speak of neither awarding honors improperly nor imposing punishments excessively, and of not daring to be idle or take one’s ease. The reason these matters must ultimately be attributed to Heaven’s mandate is that Heaven sees and hears through the people, and Heaven sends calamities and auspicious signs according to virtue.
