title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於貳命然尚能聲大義而勵四百載之人
心則夫純乎公者又當何如也漢宣帝所
以致中興之隆者其言曰有功不賞有罪
不誅唐虞不能化天下可不謂知言乎然
趙蓋韓楊何罪而誅許史弘石何功而用
褒霍光之忠而赤族之誅不少貸知王成
之偽而賜爵之命不可回此無他綜核之
過必反眩勵精之銳多不終無怪其偏私
矣唐太宗所以造太平之業者其言曰有
===
功則賞有罪則刑孰敢不盡心力可不謂
善言乎然君羨以讖言而戮無忌以外戚
而封蘇威被責終寛誤國之誅魏徵被褒
或致退朝之怒此無他英武非忠厚之資
仁義非久假之物又無怪其偏私矣由是
觀之帝王所以柄得其用者公正為之本
也後世所以治失其柄者偏私為之累也
蓋確乎其不可易矣而執事猶致疑於臯
陶之論謂其不能無少偏於輕重之間蓋
punctuated: 於貳命，然尚能聲大義而勵四百載之人心，則夫純乎公者又當何如也？漢宣帝所以致中興之隆者，其言曰：「有功不賞，有罪不誅，唐虞不能化天下。」可不謂知言乎？然趙、蓋、韓、楊何罪而誅？許、史、弘、石何功而用？褒霍光之忠，而赤族之誅不少貸；知王成之偽，而賜爵之命不可回。此無他，綜核之過必反眩，勵精之銳多不終，無怪其偏私矣。唐太宗所以造太平之業者，其言曰：「有功則賞，有罪則刑，孰敢不盡心力？」可不謂善言乎？然君羨以讖言而戮，無忌以外戚而封；蘇威被責，終寛誤國之誅；魏徵被褒，或致退朝之怒。此無他，英武非忠厚之資，仁義非久假之物，又無怪其偏私矣。由是觀之，帝王所以柄得其用者，公正為之本也；後世所以治失其柄者，偏私為之累也。蓋確乎其不可易矣。而執事猶致疑於臯陶之論，謂其不能無少偏於輕重之間，蓋
translation_en:
…in a second command [?]. Yet he could still proclaim the great principles of righteousness and inspire people’s hearts for four hundred years. How much more, then, could one whose public-mindedness was pure accomplish?

Emperor Xuan of the Han, who brought about a flourishing restoration, said: “If those with merit are not rewarded and those guilty of crimes are not executed, even the rulers of Tang and Yu could not transform the realm.” Can this not be called an insightful statement? Yet what crimes had Zhao, Gai, Han, and Yang committed that they were executed? What merit had Xu, Shi, Hong, and Shi acquired that they were employed? He praised Huo Guang’s loyalty, yet allowed not the slightest mitigation of the punishment that exterminated his clan. He knew of Wang Cheng’s deception, yet would not rescind the command granting him noble rank. There was no other reason for this: excessive scrutiny inevitably produces confusion instead, and the ardor of strenuous effort seldom endures to the end. It is no wonder that he was partial.

Emperor Taizong of the Tang, who established an age of great peace, said: “Reward those with merit and punish those guilty of crimes: who would dare not devote all his heart and strength?” Can this not be called an excellent statement? Yet Junxian was executed because of a prophecy, while Wuji was enfeoffed because he was an imperial relative by marriage. Su Wei was reproached, but ultimately spared execution for harming the state; Wei Zheng was praised, yet sometimes provoked anger after the emperor withdrew from court. There was no other reason for this: martial prowess is not the disposition of loyalty and generosity, and benevolence and righteousness are not things that can be borrowed indefinitely. Again, it is no wonder that he was partial.

Viewed in this light, emperors and kings could put the powers of government to proper use because impartiality and rectitude formed their foundation. In later ages, government lost its command of those powers because partiality and private interests encumbered it. This is surely an unalterable conclusion. Yet you still raise doubts about Gao Yao’s argument, claiming that it cannot be entirely free of some partiality in weighing lighter and heavier penalties. For…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
喜而賞者聖人之所欲怒而刑者聖人之
所惡功罪或有疑似而屈法以伸恩大舜
好生之德也後世若箝勒鞬輈之弛青朱
金紫之濫是則偏之為禍而豈古人之所
謂疑哉執事又疑八柄之目謂其不能不
容私於恩幸之間蓋爵祿者當然之報予
者特厚之恩羣臣或有超異而優賞以示
勸周官鼓舞之機也後世若登少艾於司
馬寵胡兒於宮中是則私之為禍而豈古
===
人之所謂幸哉嗚呼古昔盛時德化為先
刑賞次之雖極天下之公正而於變時雍
不專待此故曰不賞而民勸畫象而民不
犯後世以法制治天下未嘗不以此為先
務也而又往往徇於偏私而失之然則德
之不脩而徒法果不能以自行乎執事欲
有言以為
當宁之獻亦曰
明君以務學為急
punctuated:
喜而賞者，聖人之所欲；怒而刑者，聖人之所惡。功罪或有疑似，而屈法以伸恩，大舜好生之德也。後世若箝勒鞬輈之弛、青朱金紫之濫，是則偏之為禍，而豈古人之所謂疑哉？執事又疑八柄之目，謂其不能不容私於恩幸之間。蓋爵祿者，當然之報；予者，特厚之恩。羣臣或有超異，而優賞以示勸，周官鼓舞之機也。後世若登少艾於司馬、寵胡兒於宮中，是則私之為禍，而豈古人之所謂幸哉？

嗚呼！古昔盛時，德化為先，刑賞次之。雖極天下之公正，而於變時雍，不專待此。故曰：「不賞而民勸，畫象而民不犯。」後世以法制治天下，未嘗不以此為先務也，而又往往徇於偏私而失之。然則德之不脩，而徒法果不能以自行乎？執事欲有言以為當宁之獻，亦曰：「明君以務學為急，
translation_en:
…To reward with joy is what the sage desires; to punish in anger is what the sage abhors. When merit or guilt is doubtful, bending the law to extend gracious favor exemplifies the great Shun’s virtue of cherishing life. In later ages, however, there were such abuses as the loosening of restraints involving bridles, bow cases, and chariot shafts [?], and the indiscriminate bestowal of blue and vermilion robes, gold seals, and purple seal ribbons. These were the calamities wrought by partiality. How could they be what the ancients meant by cases of doubt?

You further question the categories of the eight instruments of authority, suggesting that they inevitably admit private favoritism in the exercise of grace and favor. Noble rank and emoluments are recompense duly owed; gifts are exceptionally generous acts of grace. When ministers show extraordinary distinction, rewarding them generously to encourage others is the means of inspiration described in the Offices of Zhou. In later ages, however, handsome youths were elevated to the post of Minister of War, and a non-Han lad was favored within the palace. These were the calamities wrought by private favoritism. How could they be what the ancients meant by favor?

Alas! In the flourishing ages of antiquity, moral transformation came first, and punishments and rewards second. Although these were administered with the utmost impartiality and justice, transforming the people into harmonious concord did not depend on them alone. Thus it is said: “Without rewards, the people were encouraged; with punishments merely depicted, the people committed no offenses.” Later ages governed the realm through laws and regulations and invariably made these their foremost concern. Yet they repeatedly yielded to partiality and private favoritism, thereby mishandling them. Is it indeed the case, then, that when virtue is not cultivated, laws alone cannot put themselves into effect? If you wish to offer counsel to the reigning sovereign, one need only say: “An enlightened ruler takes diligent learning as his most urgent task, …

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖學以正心爲要
第三問
周孚先
同考試官教諭林批以經權爲
建儲之法而歸之於豫忠愛之意溢於言表
考試官教諭張批觀子此策可謂先天下之憂而憂者矣
考試官教諭應批答無遺而中有區處非徒以演問目也
建天下之大本者必以豫濟天下之常經
者必以權建儲天下之大本也與子天下
===
之常經也根本乆虛則天下之大計不可
忽經常或變則天下之大慮不可忘天下
雖有難處之事古人亦有善處之方亦惟
定之豫而已矣濟之權而已矣執事惓惓
忠愛之心發於策問而及
社稷之大計愚生不敏何足以知之然嫠不恤
緯而憂王室其敢不述所懷以復明問之
萬一乎夫卜世歷年之遠者莫如三代貽
謀燕翼之善者亦莫如三代蓋經權竝用
punctuated:
聖學以正心爲要。
第三問
周孚先
同考試官教諭林批：以經權爲建儲之法，而歸之於豫，忠愛之意溢於言表。
考試官教諭張批：觀子此策，可謂先天下之憂而憂者矣。
考試官教諭應批：答無遺，而中有區處，非徒以演問目也。
建天下之大本者必以豫，濟天下之常經者必以權。建儲，天下之大本也；與子，天下之常經也。根本乆虛，則天下之大計不可忽；經常或變，則天下之大慮不可忘。天下雖有難處之事，古人亦有善處之方，亦惟定之豫而已矣，濟之權而已矣。執事惓惓忠愛之心發於策問，而及社稷之大計。愚生不敏，何足以知之？然嫠不恤緯而憂王室，其敢不述所懷，以復明問之萬一乎？夫卜世歷年之遠者，莫如三代；貽謀燕翼之善者，亦莫如三代。蓋經權竝用，
translation_en:
…In the learning of the sage, rectifying the mind is essential.
Third Policy Question
Zhou Fuxian
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: He takes adherence to enduring principles and adaptation to circumstances as the methods for establishing an heir apparent, and makes advance preparation their ultimate basis. His loyalty and concern extend beyond what his words express.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Reading this policy essay of yours, one may indeed call you someone who worries before all others under Heaven begin to worry.
Comment by Examiner Ying, Instructor: The answer leaves nothing unaddressed and contains considered arrangements for handling the issues; it does more than merely elaborate upon the points in the question.
To establish the great foundation of the realm, one must prepare in advance; to give effect to the realm’s enduring principles, one must exercise discretion according to circumstances. Establishing an heir apparent is the great foundation of the realm; transmitting the throne to one’s son is its enduring principle. When that foundation has long remained vacant, the great affairs of the realm must not be neglected; when established norms may change, the realm’s gravest concerns must not be forgotten. Although the realm presents matters difficult to manage, the ancients also had ways of managing them well: simply to settle them in advance and to bring them to fruition through discretion. Your devoted loyalty and concern find expression in the policy question and extend to the great affairs of the altars of soil and grain. I, an ignorant student, am slow of understanding: how could I know enough about these matters? Yet even a widow, neglecting her weaving, worried about the royal house. How could I dare not set forth what is in my heart, to answer even a fraction of your illuminating inquiry? For the long succession of generations and years foretold by divination, none equaled the Three Dynasties; for the excellence of plans bequeathed to secure the welfare of descendants, none likewise equaled the Three Dynasties. For they employed both enduring principles and adaptation to circumstances…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而豫則行乎其間故論治者必以三代爲
法程也自其經而言之則啓之敬承繼禹
成王之彝訓命釗凡豫敎養之法見於保
傅傳者詳矣自其權而言之則盤庚繼兄
陽甲而三篇敷告以後子弟更立而十世
無爭此則及王之功著於大紀論者昭矣
漢唐而下敎養漸疎然漢自孝文初年豫
建太子傳至成帝雖非令主猶知擇立定
陶此漢之所以得也唐自穆宗以後定策
===
禁中其間文武號爲賢君而皆不能正始
此唐之所以失也宋儒朱熹以賈誼所謂
太子正而天下定爲天下之至言非論其
經乎宋臣范鎭以眞宗故事養宗子於宮
中爲天下之大慮非論其權乎然非獨鎭
言之司馬光之判并州蓋外官也當仁宗
嘉祐之前已上三章欲選宗室爲繼嗣迨
知諫院復進極言然非宰臣韓琦等之盡
力贊襄則帝亦未遽决也卒之英宗入繼
punctuated: 而豫則行乎其間，故論治者必以三代爲法程也。自其經而言之，則啓之敬承繼禹、成王之彝訓命釗，凡豫敎養之法，見於《保傅傳》者詳矣。自其權而言之，則盤庚繼兄陽甲，而三篇敷告以後，子弟更立，而十世無爭，此則及王之功，著於《大紀》論者昭矣。漢唐而下，敎養漸疎。然漢自孝文初年豫建太子，傳至成帝，雖非令主，猶知擇立定陶，此漢之所以得也。唐自穆宗以後，定策禁中，其間文武號爲賢君，而皆不能正始，此唐之所以失也。宋儒朱熹以賈誼所謂「太子正而天下定」爲天下之至言，非論其經乎？宋臣范鎭以眞宗故事，養宗子於宮中，爲天下之大慮，非論其權乎？然非獨鎭言之，司馬光之判并州，蓋外官也，當仁宗嘉祐之前，已上三章，欲選宗室爲繼嗣；迨知諫院，復進極言。然非宰臣韓琦等之盡力贊襄，則帝亦未遽决也。卒之英宗入繼
translation_en:
…and advance preparation operates between them. Thus those who discuss government must take the Three Dynasties as their model. In terms of constant principles, there were Qi’s reverent assumption of Yu’s succession and King Cheng’s enduring instructions to Zhao. The methods for educating and nurturing an heir in advance are set out in detail in the Account of the Grand Guardian and Grand Mentor (Baofu zhuan). In terms of discretionary measures, Pan Geng succeeded his elder brother Yang Jia; after the proclamations in the three chapters, sons and younger brothers succeeded in turn, and for ten generations there was no contention. The king’s achievement here [?] is clearly set forth in the commentary in the Great Chronicle (Daji).

From the Han and Tang onward, the education and nurture of heirs gradually became neglected. Yet early in the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, the Han established a crown prince in advance. When the succession reached Emperor Cheng, although he was no exemplary ruler, he still knew to select and establish the Prince of Dingtao as heir. This was where the Han succeeded. In the Tang, after Emperor Muzong, decisions about the succession were made within the inner palace. Among the subsequent emperors, Wenzong and Wuzong were reputed to be worthy rulers, yet neither could set matters right at the outset. This was where the Tang failed.

The Song scholar Zhu Xi regarded Jia Yi’s statement, “When the crown prince is upright, all under Heaven is secure,” as a supremely true saying. Was he not discussing constant principles? The Song official Fan Zhen, following the precedent of Emperor Zhenzong, regarded nurturing a son of the imperial clan within the palace as a matter of far-reaching concern for the realm. Was he not discussing discretionary measures? Yet Zhen was not alone in speaking of this. When Sima Guang administered Bingzhou, he was an official serving outside the capital. Even before Emperor Renzong’s Jiayou era, he had submitted three memorials urging the selection of a member of the imperial clan as successor. Once he became Administrator of the Remonstrance Bureau, he again spoke with the utmost urgency. Yet without the wholehearted assistance of Chief Councilor Han Qi and the others, the emperor would still not have reached a decision promptly. In the end, Yingzong entered the palace to succeed to the throne…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
治平無事則司馬韓范之功豈可少哉抑
非獨光爲然婁寅亮之丞上虞蓋末秩也
當高宗紹興之初乃能倡議乞選藝祖之
諸孫慷慨一書足以悟主然非樞密李回
等之同心將順則帝能無疑乎已而孝宗
嗣立付託得人則婁李亦不爲無助矣是
諸臣者功在社稷夫孰以爲罪名垂後世
亦孰以爲非抑愚又有進於是者濟經以
權非惟三代之君爲然也昔者聖莫如堯
===
舜治莫逮唐虞堯擇嗣而得舜於同宗之
下舜擇嗣而得禹於同祖之下蓋亦善處
天下之變耳
建儲以豫亦非徒三代之君爲然也我
朝
聖祖開基
神宗紹統必先
國本肇建
元良或以
punctuated:
治平無事，則司馬、韓、范之功豈可少哉？抑非獨光爲然，婁寅亮之丞上虞，蓋末秩也。當高宗紹興之初，乃能倡議乞選藝祖之諸孫，慷慨一書，足以悟主。然非樞密李回等之同心將順，則帝能無疑乎？已而孝宗嗣立，付託得人，則婁、李亦不爲無助矣。是諸臣者，功在社稷，夫孰以爲罪？名垂後世，亦孰以爲非？抑愚又有進於是者：濟經以權，非惟三代之君爲然也。昔者聖莫如堯舜，治莫逮唐虞。堯擇嗣而得舜於同宗之下，舜擇嗣而得禹於同祖之下，蓋亦善處天下之變耳。
建儲以豫，亦非徒三代之君爲然也。我朝聖祖開基，神宗紹統，必先國本，肇建元良，或以
translation_en:
…the Zhiping reign passed without incident. How, then, could the contributions of Sima, Han, and Fan be considered slight? Nor was Guang alone in this. Lou Yinliang, serving as Assistant Magistrate of Shangyu, held a very low rank. Yet at the beginning of Gaozong’s Shaoxing reign, he took the initiative in proposing that a successor be chosen from among the descendants of the founding emperor. A single impassioned letter sufficed to awaken his sovereign’s understanding. But had Military Affairs Commissioner Li Hui and others not supported and furthered this with one accord, could the emperor have been free of doubt? Subsequently, Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, and the charge was entrusted to the right man. Thus Lou and Li, too, certainly rendered assistance. These ministers performed meritorious service for the altars of soil and grain: who could count it a crime? Their names have endured for later generations: who could judge their actions wrong?
Yet I would venture a further point: supplementing constant principles with expedient judgment was not confined to the rulers of the Three Dynasties. In antiquity, none surpassed Yao and Shun in sageliness, and no government equaled that of Tang and Yu. In choosing a successor, Yao found Shun among the humbler members of his own clan; in choosing a successor, Shun found Yu among those sharing his ancestral descent. They, too, were simply adept at responding to changing circumstances in the realm.
Nor was establishing an heir in advance confined to the rulers of the Three Dynasties. In our dynasty, the Sagely Progenitor laid the foundations, and Shenzong [?] continued the imperial succession. They invariably gave priority to the foundation of the state by establishing the heir apparent, sometimes employing…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
太孫監國或以
親王司香
宗廟皆所以垂萬世之防也
聖天子臨御十有四年矣
英明天縱
神武風行顧以
椒寢未繁
前星未耀久虛天下之仰瞻再孽强藩之搆
逆
===
法宫燕閒之地獨不念及是乎伏望體
祖宗之心以為心
法帝王之德以為德選建
親賢置諸
左右縱未入
承華之宫亦可任
司香之典庶幾上慰
九廟在天之靈下奠四海蒼生之枕也狂愚不
識忌諱率爾妄言惟進而教之
punctuated:
太孫監國，或以親王司香宗廟，皆所以垂萬世之防也。
聖天子臨御十有四年矣，英明天縱，神武風行。顧以椒寢未繁，前星未耀，久虛天下之仰瞻，再孽强藩之搆逆。法宫燕閒之地，獨不念及是乎？伏望體祖宗之心以為心，法帝王之德以為德，選建親賢，置諸左右。縱未入承華之宫，亦可任司香之典，庶幾上慰九廟在天之靈，下奠四海蒼生之枕也。狂愚不識忌諱，率爾妄言，惟進而教之。
translation_en:
…the imperial grandson was entrusted with overseeing the state, or a prince of the blood was charged with offering incense in the ancestral temples: all these measures established safeguards for countless generations.
The sagely Son of Heaven has occupied the throne for fourteen years. His brilliant discernment is Heaven-bestowed, and his divine martial prowess sweeps abroad like the wind. Yet the pepper-scented chambers have not flourished with offspring, and the star that heralds the heir apparent has not shone. The hopes of all under Heaven have long remained unfulfilled, twice breeding rebellious plots among powerful feudatory princes [?]. Amid the leisure of the imperial palace, can Your Majesty alone have given no thought to this?
I humbly hope that you will take the hearts of your ancestors as your own heart and model your virtue upon that of the emperors and kings of old. Select and establish a worthy imperial kinsman, keeping him at your side. Even if he has not yet entered Chenghua Palace, the residence of the heir apparent, he may still be entrusted with the rites of offering incense. Thus you might comfort above the heavenly spirits of the nine ancestral temples and secure below the peaceful repose of the common people throughout the realm.
In my rashness and ignorance, I do not understand what must not be spoken. I have recklessly uttered these presumptuous words; I ask only that you encourage and instruct me.

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第四問
劉一松
同考試官教諭王批以此策觀子必能進言於
君者矣
考試官教諭張批得納約自牖之意可取
考試官教諭應批詞婉而事實宜冠本房
人君知有一言興邦之效而後可以盡君
道人臣知有片言悟主之機而後可以盡
臣道蓋一言可以興邦者知爲君之難片
===
言可以悟主者因其心之明也昔晏子爲
齊景公陳先王巡狩遊觀之法今時流連
荒亡之行而景公悅之夫晏子一陪臣爾
而知所以畜其君景公一諸侯爾而知所
以悅其臣矧
聖天子在上而有不可以古義陳者乎此執事
發策意也敢不述所聞而敬對之夫虞周
之巡狩年數不同固也然舜之一歲巡四
嶽者兵衛少而徵求寡周之又六年乃時
punctuated:
第四問
劉一松
同考試官教諭王批：「以此策觀，子必能進言於君者矣。」
考試官教諭張批：「得納約自牖之意，可取。」
考試官教諭應批：「詞婉而事實，宜冠本房。」
人君知有一言興邦之效，而後可以盡君道；人臣知有片言悟主之機，而後可以盡臣道。蓋一言可以興邦者，知爲君之難；片言可以悟主者，因其心之明也。昔晏子爲齊景公陳先王巡狩遊觀之法、今時流連荒亡之行，而景公悅之。夫晏子一陪臣爾，而知所以畜其君；景公一諸侯爾，而知所以悅其臣。矧聖天子在上，而有不可以古義陳者乎？此執事發策意也。敢不述所聞而敬對之？夫虞周之巡狩，年數不同，固也。然舜之一歲巡四嶽者，兵衛少而徵求寡；周之又六年乃時
translation_en:
Fourth Policy Question
Liu Yisong
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “Judging by this policy essay, you will surely be capable of offering counsel to your ruler.”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “It captures the meaning of ‘presenting a simple offering through the window’—approaching the ruler through what he already understands—and merits acceptance.”
Examiner Ying, Instructor, comments: “The language is tactful and the matters discussed substantial. It should rank first in this examining room.”
Only when a ruler understands that a single utterance can bring prosperity to his state can he fully discharge the duties of a ruler; only when a minister understands that a few words can awaken his sovereign’s understanding can he fully discharge the duties of a minister. A single utterance can bring prosperity to a state because it conveys an understanding of the difficulty of being a ruler; a few words can awaken a sovereign because they work through the understanding already present in his mind.
Formerly, Yanzi explained to Duke Jing of Qi the former kings’ methods of conducting inspection tours and excursions, and the contemporary practices of indulgent wandering and ruinous dissipation. Duke Jing was pleased by this. Yanzi was merely a minister of a regional lord, yet he knew how to guide and restrain his ruler; Duke Jing was merely a regional lord, yet he knew how to take pleasure in his minister’s counsel. How much more so now, with the sagely Son of Heaven above us! Could there be any ancient principle that may not be presented to him? This is your intention in setting this policy question. Dare I fail to relate what I have learned and respectfully reply?
It is certainly true that the inspection tours under Yu and Zhou differed in the number of years between them. Yet Shun toured the Four Sacred Peaks within a single year because his armed escort was small and his requisitions few; under Zhou, only after another six years did the king undertake the seasonal…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
巡者考制度而明黜陟謂非經世而何哉
夏周之戀覲盛德不廢固也然一遊一豫
為諸侯度為臺為沼民歡樂之夫豈般樂
而然哉神禹之功大固在人爾然甫再傳
而為太康以逸滅德盤遊無度則有夷羿
之距而五子作歌金履祥謂讀是歌知仲
康之宜君也成康之澤深亦未艾爾然甫
再傳而為穆王欲肆其心周行天下遂為
瑶池之宴而祭公矢詩朱子謂不有是詩
===
則徐方御宸極矣是其祖功宗德固有以
維持之而規誦箴戒亦豈無所裨補哉漢
唐以來非復古制名雖巡狩實則遊豫固
不能以盡述也其間如文帝漢之賢主也
乃與豪俊方正而擊兔伐狐其視成帝從
期門私奴而闘雞走馬者亦何以大相遠
邪然文帝聞賈山之至言則嘉納之成帝
雖有班伯之讜言左遷張放而不忍也此
其盛衰之所以殊豈不以聽言之有緩急
punctuated: 巡者，考制度而明黜陟，謂非經世而何哉？夏周之戀覲，盛德不廢，固也。然一遊一豫，為諸侯度；為臺為沼，民歡樂之，夫豈般樂而然哉？神禹之功大，固在人爾。然甫再傳而為太康，以逸滅德，盤遊無度，則有夷羿之距，而五子作歌。金履祥謂讀是歌，知仲康之宜君也。成康之澤深，亦未艾爾。然甫再傳而為穆王，欲肆其心，周行天下，遂為瑶池之宴，而祭公矢詩。朱子謂不有是詩，則徐方御宸極矣。是其祖功宗德，固有以維持之，而規誦箴戒，亦豈無所裨補哉？漢唐以來，非復古制，名雖巡狩，實則遊豫，固不能以盡述也。其間如文帝，漢之賢主也，乃與豪俊方正而擊兔伐狐，其視成帝從期門私奴而闘雞走馬者，亦何以大相遠邪？然文帝聞賈山之至言，則嘉納之；成帝雖有班伯之讜言，左遷張放而不忍也。此其盛衰之所以殊，豈不以聽言之有緩急
translation_en:
…made tours to examine institutions and regulations and clarify demotions and promotions. What could this be called if not the ordering of the realm? As for the Xia and Zhou rulers’ attachment to court audiences [?], it is certainly true that their flourishing virtue remained unimpaired. Yet every excursion and recreation set a standard for the feudal lords; when they built terraces and ponds, the people rejoiced in them. Could this have been mere indulgence in pleasure?

The achievements of the divine Yu were great, and certainly lived on among the people. Yet after only two transmissions of the throne came Taikang, who destroyed his virtue through indolence and roamed and hunted without restraint. Thereupon Yi Yi barred his return, and the five sons composed their song. Jin Lüxiang said that reading this song showed that Zhongkang was fit to be ruler. The profound beneficence of Kings Cheng and Kang likewise had not yet run its course. Yet after only two transmissions of the throne came King Mu, who wished to give free rein to his desires and travel throughout the world. He then held the banquet at the Jasper Pool, and the Duke of Zhai presented his poem. Master Zhu said that, without this poem, the ruler of Xu would have occupied the imperial throne. Thus, although ancestral achievements and virtue certainly helped sustain these dynasties, how could admonitory recitations and cautionary remonstrances have failed to contribute as well?

From the Han and Tang onward, the ancient institutions were no longer followed. Though called inspection tours, these journeys were in reality excursions for pleasure; they certainly cannot all be recounted. Among these rulers, Emperor Wen was a worthy sovereign of the Han, yet he went striking hares and hunting foxes with men of outstanding talent and upright conduct. How greatly did this differ from Emperor Cheng’s taking along Gentlemen of the Palace Gate and personal slaves for cockfighting and horse racing? Yet when Emperor Wen heard Jia Shan’s earnest counsel, he commended and accepted it. Emperor Cheng, despite Ban Bo’s forthright counsel, could not bear to demote Zhang Fang. Was not this difference between flourishing rule and decline due to their differing urgency in heeding advice…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
歟太宗唐之英主也乃欲遊南山嚴裝已
辦而不行其視敬宗欲幸驪山銳意一往
而遽還者亦何以遽相異耶然太宗畏魏
徵之直諫故中輟焉敬宗雖有張權輿之
叩頭欲身自試禍而不信也此其禍福之
所以異豈不以聞言之有從違歟觀於成
帝敬宗而知樂不可極觀於文帝太宗而
知言為有益亦彰彰矣洪惟我
朝
===
皇祖芟夷僭偽
太宗逐北腥羶當時櫛風沐雨於行陣之間
駐蹕汗馬於沙漠之外非不可俟大定也以
憂勤成
大業安逸
貽子孫耳
累朝宅中而圖大
列聖恭己而垂裳當時凝
景命於穆清奠坤輿於磐石非不可講時巡
punctuated:
歟？太宗，唐之英主也，乃欲遊南山，嚴裝已辦而不行，其視敬宗欲幸驪山，銳意一往而遽還者，亦何以遽相異耶？然太宗畏魏徵之直諫，故中輟焉；敬宗雖有張權輿之叩頭，欲身自試禍而不信也。此其禍福之所以異，豈不以聞言之有從違歟？觀於成帝、敬宗而知樂不可極，觀於文帝、太宗而知言為有益，亦彰彰矣。
洪惟我朝皇祖芟夷僭偽，太宗逐北腥羶。當時櫛風沐雨於行陣之間，駐蹕汗馬於沙漠之外，非不可俟大定也，以憂勤成大業，安逸貽子孫耳。累朝宅中而圖大，列聖恭己而垂裳。當時凝景命於穆清，奠坤輿於磐石，非不可講時巡
translation_en:
…was it not? Taizong, an outstanding ruler of the Tang, once wished to make an excursion to Nanshan. His preparations were already complete, yet he did not go. How greatly did this differ from Jingzong, who wished to visit Lishan, resolutely set out, but abruptly returned? Yet Taizong respected Wei Zheng’s forthright remonstrance and therefore abandoned his excursion. Jingzong, despite Zhang Quanyu’s knocking his head upon the ground in remonstrance, wished to put the threatened calamity to the test in person and would not believe him. Was not this difference in their misfortune and good fortune due to whether they heeded or rejected the counsel they heard? The examples of Chengdi and Jingzong teach us that pleasure must not be pursued to excess; those of Wendi and Taizong teach us that counsel is beneficial. This is abundantly clear.
We reverently consider how our dynasty’s imperial ancestor cut down the usurpers and pretenders, and Taizong pursued the routed, rank-smelling barbarians. In those days they endured wind and rain amid the ranks of battle, halting the imperial carriage and driving their horses to a sweat beyond the deserts. It was not that they could not have waited for complete pacification: through care and toil they accomplished the great enterprise, leaving peace and ease to their descendants. Successive reigns governed from the center and planned great undertakings; successive sage sovereigns reverently composed themselves and let their robes hang down, ruling without exertion. In those days they secured Heaven’s glorious mandate within the august serenity of the court and established the realm upon solid rock. It was not that they could not undertake periodic inspection tours…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也以
宗社不可離
大寶不可曠耳比者
皇上北狩西征驅馳關塞于以肅羌胡飭邊壘
蓋
法
祖之銳心然而臣子長慮卻顧激切肺肝以爲
不乘危不徼倖乃古人之深戒邇聞
聖心毅然復欲南巡言者相繼得罪遠近莫不
===
惕息而臣子惓惓忠愛之心終不能以自
已也故執事發策諸生而亦詢之以是豈
非欲收千慮之一得乎愚以爲
巡遊之利害
廷臣類能言之顧左右之言未可信也諸大
夫之言未可信也國人言之然後察之而
芻蕘之言聖人擇焉今嶺海之臣自視猶
國人之列而陳狂之言亦豈非芻蕘之倫
歟執事倘與其進而廁之鄉書進之
punctuated: 也，以宗社不可離，大寶不可曠耳。比者，皇上北狩西征，驅馳關塞，于以肅羌胡、飭邊壘，蓋法祖之銳心。然而臣子長慮卻顧，激切肺肝，以爲不乘危、不徼倖，乃古人之深戒。邇聞聖心毅然復欲南巡，言者相繼得罪，遠近莫不惕息，而臣子惓惓忠愛之心，終不能以自已也。故執事發策諸生，而亦詢之以是，豈非欲收千慮之一得乎？愚以爲巡遊之利害，廷臣類能言之。顧左右之言未可信也，諸大夫之言未可信也，國人言之，然後察之，而芻蕘之言，聖人擇焉。今嶺海之臣，自視猶國人之列，而陳狂之言，亦豈非芻蕘之倫歟？執事倘與其進，而廁之鄉書，進之
translation_en:
…It was simply because the ancestral temples and altars of state could not be left, and the imperial throne could not stand vacant. Recently, His Majesty has hunted in the north and campaigned in the west, riding through passes and frontier regions to subdue the Qiang and Hu and put the border fortifications in order. This surely reflects his ardent determination to emulate his ancestors. Yet his servants and subjects, considering the long term and looking back with apprehension, feel deeply and urgently that avoiding danger and not trusting to luck were solemn admonitions of the ancients. We have recently heard that His Majesty is resolutely determined to undertake another southern tour. Those who have spoken out have incurred punishment one after another, and people near and far hold their breath in fear. Nevertheless, his servants and subjects cannot suppress their devoted loyalty and affection.
Thus, when you gentlemen set policy questions for the candidates, you also asked about this matter. Was this not in the hope of gleaning even one sound idea from a thousand reflections? In my humble opinion, court officials can generally explain the advantages and disadvantages of imperial tours. Yet the words of those close to the ruler cannot necessarily be trusted, nor can those of the great officers. Only after the people of the realm have spoken should the matter be examined; the sage selects what is sound even from the words of grass cutters and wood gatherers. Now, as a subject from Linghai, I regard myself as belonging among the people of the realm. And are not the words of Chen Kuang likewise comparable to those of grass cutters and wood gatherers? If you gentlemen should approve my advancement, include me in the provincial register of successful candidates, and submit it to…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天府少經
睿覽未必不□察於此也不識以為何如
第五問
舒素蘊
同考試官教諭唐批〔能原其法之弊而善為之𠙖有用之學□〕
考試官教諭𨞬批〔議所以救弊之方不失立法本意于非〕
〔但善處一方之務也〕
考試官教諭應批〔該博之學超邁之識宏濟之才皆於〕
〔此策見之矣〕
===
有畫一之定法有變通之時宜法立於前
必有以守之則無弊弊生於後必有以變
之則不通守
國家經常之法酌地方變通之宜其不在於
得人矣乎蓋不得其人或因循以長弊或
更張而反常皆非所以善治也執事以時
務策諸生蓋以俊傑待之而□□其人也
何足以知遠姑以廣東之利病陳之可乎
以軍伍言之我
punctuated:
天府，少經睿覽，未必不□察於此也。不識以為何如？

第五問
舒素蘊
同考試官教諭唐批〔能原其法之弊，而善為之𠙖，有用之學□。〕
考試官教諭𨞬批〔議所以救弊之方，不失立法本意，于非〕〔但善處一方之務也。〕
考試官教諭應批〔該博之學，超邁之識，宏濟之才，皆於〕〔此策見之矣。〕

有畫一之定法，有變通之時宜。法立於前，必有以守之，則無弊；弊生於後，必有以變之，則不通。守國家經常之法，酌地方變通之宜，其不在於得人矣乎？蓋不得其人，或因循以長弊，或更張而反常，皆非所以善治也。執事以時務策諸生，蓋以俊傑待之，而□□其人也。何足以知遠？姑以廣東之利病陳之，可乎？以軍伍言之，我
translation_en:
…to the imperial repository, and should it briefly receive Your Majesty’s discerning perusal, it might yet receive consideration in this regard [?]. I do not know what you think of this.

Fifth Question
Shu Suyun
Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor, comments: 〔He can trace the abuses of the system to their source and skillfully address them [?]: learning of practical use [?].〕
Examiner [surname unclear: 𨞬], Instructor, comments: 〔His discussion of remedies for abuses preserves the original intent of the legislation; [unclear: 于非]〕〔merely handling the affairs of a single region well.〕
Examiner Ying, Instructor, comments: 〔Extensive learning, outstanding insight, and the ability to bring wide-ranging benefit are all〕〔evident in this policy essay.〕

There are fixed laws that provide uniform standards, and there are adjustments appropriate to changing circumstances. Once laws have been established, there must be means of upholding them; then there will be no abuses. When abuses subsequently arise, there must be means of changing the laws; then they do not work [?]. Does not upholding the state’s standing laws while weighing the adjustments appropriate to local conditions depend upon obtaining the right people? Without the right people, some perpetuate abuses by following established practice, while others depart from enduring principles through their changes. Neither course produces good government. You, sir, have set the students policy questions on current affairs, presumably treating them as outstanding talents and seeking [?] such people among them. How could I know enough to speak of distant matters? May I provisionally set forth Guangdong’s advantages and problems? To speak of the military ranks, our…

title: 正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
正德十四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
鹽而革官埠乃可以專之頃者便宜許帶
六引盛行其私而官引乎不行矣豈夾帶
私鹽之法不可嚴於是地乎豪要盤據諸
埠得擅其利而商賈亦不行矣豈侵奪民
利之令不可明於是時乎毋惑乎有其害
而無其利也執事以四者爲廣東之切要
信矣然得人其尤切要歟誠得其人以理
之則興利而除害也扶偏而補弊也柔不
失之因循剛不失之更張而天下豈有不
===
舉之事哉管見區區未知是否惟進而教
之
punctuated: 鹽而革官埠，乃可以專之。頃者便宜許帶六引，盛行其私，而官引乎不行矣。豈夾帶私鹽之法不可嚴於是地乎？豪要盤據諸埠，得擅其利，而商賈亦不行矣。豈侵奪民利之令不可明於是時乎？毋惑乎有其害而無其利也。執事以四者爲廣東之切要，信矣。然得人其尤切要歟？誠得其人以理之，則興利而除害也，扶偏而補弊也，柔不失之因循，剛不失之更張，而天下豈有不舉之事哉？管見區區，未知是否，惟進而教之。
translation_en:
…salt, and abolish the official depots; only then can control over it be unified [?]. Recently, as an expedient, permission was granted to carry six yin of salt [six salt-certificate quotas]. Private trafficking flourished, while the official salt certificates ceased to circulate. Could the laws against carrying contraband salt alongside authorized shipments not be strictly enforced here? Powerful and influential men have entrenched themselves at the various depots and monopolized their profits, so merchants, too, have ceased trading. Could the ordinances against encroaching upon the people’s livelihood not be clearly proclaimed at this time? It is no wonder that there are harms but no benefits.

You regard these four matters as Guangdong’s urgent concerns, and rightly so. Yet is securing the right men not still more urgent? If the right men are indeed found to manage these matters, they will promote benefits and eliminate harms, correct imbalances and remedy abuses. Their flexibility will not lapse into mere adherence to established practice, nor their firmness into excessive alteration. What undertaking in the realm could then remain unaccomplished? These are merely my limited views; I do not know whether they are correct. I ask that you favor me with instruction.
